```
Chapter 32 SDIO Interface (SDIO)
```
This chapter's module description applies only to the CH32H417, CH32H415 microcontroller product.
The "SDIO" mentioned separately in this chapter refers to a communication interface on the microcontroller
designed to operate external memory cards such as SD cards or other devices, and is a peripheral of the
microcontroller. The SDIO of the microcontroller is directly mounted on the HB bus, and the clock is directly
provided by HCLK, which can achieve higher communication speed. The SDIO of the microcontroller is used as
the SDIO host, and the controlled devices are also collectively referred to as SDIO devices. In applications, SDIO
is generally used to read and write SD cards, TF cards or eMMC particles, or to control other devices that use
SDIO as a communication interface, such as Wi-Fi/4G modules.
32.1 Main Features
32.1.1 Features
 Support SD card, SDIO card and MMC card
 1-bit, 4-bit and 8-bit bus support
 The highest communication clock can reach 100MHz.
```
 Compatible with MMC Specification 4.5 (Forward compatibility)
```
 Compatible with SD card specification 2.0, SDIO card specification 2.0
 Not compatible with SPI or QSPI
32.1.2 Overview
The SDIO of the microcontroller supports communication with memory such as SD cards or MMC cards. It needs
to be clear that SDIO only provides a set of clocks, data and command control sequences required to realize the
single command transmission of SD cards and MMC cards. The sequence and combination of commands need to
be determined by the user through the program. In addition, for various memory cards, SDIO can only realize the
```
function of reading and writing, and the function of the file system provided by the file system needs to be
```
realized by the user to build the file system through the program.
SDIO is different from the QSPI interface. It has no chip select pin and has an extra CMD pin. CMD can be
```
regarded as a special data line, which is specially used to transmit commands and responses; SDIO is available in
```
```
1-bit, 4-bit and 8-bit data line widths; the SDIO clock generally works at a frequency below 400kHz during
```
configuration. When the data transmission is officially performed, it can be configured as the maximum clock
supported by the SDIO device. The maximum SDIO clock output supported by the microcontroller is Half of
HCLK, according to the protocol, when the clock received by the SDIO device is greater than a certain threshold,
the waveform peaks of the clock line, data line and command line need to be reduced to save the time-consuming
of waveform rising and falling.
Unlike SD cards, SDIO cards often refer to non-storage devices such as WIFI/Bluetooth modules and 4G modules
that use SDIO interfaces. If there is no special instruction, the content described in this chapter must be applicable
to SD card, and the content only applicable to SDIO card or MMC card will be specially pointed out. In the
description of this chapter, the SD card is regarded as the potential operation object first, followed by the SDIO
card, and finally the MMC card.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 706
32.2 Interface and Clock
SDIO receives the control of the CPU through the HB bus. There is a FIFO interface in the SDIO register. The
CPU or DMA obtains or generates data by reading and writing the FIFO. SDIO is directly clocked by HCLK, and
has an interrupt entry that supports multiple interrupt sources. The pins directly controlled by SDIO are SDIO_CK,
SDIO_CMD, SDIO_D [7:0], which are connected to SDIO devices through several pins. SDIO is a
host-dominated communication interface, and all transfers must be initiated by the microcontroller.

The structure of SDIO is shown in Figure 32-1.

SDIO is a peripheral that the microcontroller directly operates the SDIO device as a host. It is roughly composed
of 5 modules: HB interface, clock control part, CMD line control part, data line control part and control register
part. SDIO is a half-duplex for peripherals, the CPU writes the commands and data to be sent to the control
register, and the command line and data line control module is responsible for pushing the command or data to the
IO and adding CRC. The data flow of SDIO is responsible for the transfer from RAM to SDIO FIFO by
general-purpose DMA. SDIO FIFO has 32 32-bit sizes.

The pins that need to be configured for SDIO and their modes are shown in Table 32-1.

```
Note: The SDIO_CK pin should be configured as a float input when in slave mode.
```
32.2.3 Clock
The clock pin of SDIO is SDIO_CK, and its output clock is obtained by dividing the frequency of HCLK, and the
frequency dividing coefficient can be configured as any integer value between 2 and 261. SDIO devices generally
only support a single bus mode with a clock of up to 400kHz during initialization. After initialization, the host
generally initiates a switch to a low voltage operation, and at the same time increases the clock to the maximum
clock that both the microcontroller and the SDIO device can accept. Different versions and speed grades of SD
cards support different clock speeds and switching processes, and users need to understand for themselves.

32.3 SDIO Protocol Description
The communication on SDIO is based on transmission as the smallest unit. Each transmission always starts with
the host sending a command on the CMD line. After some commands are sent, the SDIO device will also send a
piece of data on the CMD line to reply to the host, which is called 'Response', sometimes accompanied by the
transmission of data, the transmission of data is on the D line. The format of commands and responses is fixed,
and the definition of each field is determined according to different commands or responses. Responses and data
transfers need to be issued or stopped within a specified time after the end of the command or response, otherwise
a timeout error will be generated.
The purpose of this section is to let users have a preliminary understanding of the details of some specifications
necessary to use SDIO in a relatively small space, and it does not guarantee detailed and timely updates. The
SDIO of the microcontroller only guarantees that it implements the hardware operation basis of the SD 2.0, SDIO
2.0 and MMC 4.5 specifications, and does not necessarily support the functions defined in the higher version
specifications, such as double-edge sampling. Users should carry out SDIO interactive programming based on SD
specification, SDIO specification and MMC specification when doing specific development.
32.3.1 Bus Timing
The transmission of the SD card is initiated by the host initiating the CMD. The SD card may not reply with a
response, but may reply with a short response and a long response, and some responses will be accompanied by
data transmission. In the communication of the SDIO card or MMC card, there may also be a situation where the
SDIO device actively reports an interruption. The timing is shown in the group of figures below.

```
Most SDIO transfers start with a command (CMD), through which the SDIO host informs the device of its
```

4 types of commands:

```
4） Point-to-point command with data transmission (adtc): issued to a specific card with data transmission
```

32.3.2.2 Erase Command
The SD card is also a FLASH structure, and the FLASH needs to be erased before writing, but the SD card
integrates erasing logic. If it is found that there is no erasure before executing the write command, it will
automatically supplement the erasing operation. In many cases, especially before large lot writes, it can help to

32.3.3 Response
As a necessary reply from the SDIO device to the host, the response is also transmitted on the CMD line and must
be replied within a specified time. The response transmission is high-order first and low-order last. The length of
the response and the definition of each bit and each field are determined by the type of response, but all responses
start with a fixed 0 start bit, followed by a fixed 0 transmission Direction bit [1]. All responses have a stop bit at the
end, fixed at 1[1]. There are roughly 7 kinds of responses, SD card supports R1/R1b/R2/R3/R6/R7, SDIO card also
supports R4 / R5, see the format below.
32.3.3.1 R1 Response
Normal response, the total length is 48 bits, with CRC7, and the card status field is 32 bits. The format is as
follows.
Table 32-7 R1 response
Bit/Field name Start bit Transmissionbit Response index Card Status CRC7 End bit
Rank/Width 47 46 [45:40] / 6 bits [39:8]/32 bits [7:1]/7 bits 0
value 0b 0b Follow CMD Index X X 1b
32.3.3.2 R1b Response
The format of R1b is the same as that of R1, but a busy signal can be added after the response, that is, the data line
```
D2 is clamped. The host needs to deal with it after receiving the busy signal (Detecting that SDIO_D2 is low).
```
32.3.3.3 R2 Response
Responses to specific commands, the total length is 136 bits, the CRC7 is included in the card status field, and the
card status field is 128 bits. The card status field stores the value of the CID register or CSD register. The CID
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 714
register is generally used as the reply to CMD2/CMD10, and the CSD register is generally used as the reply to
CMD9. For the specific meaning of the CID/CSD register, see the section 32.4.2 Device Registers. It should be
noted that R2 will only reply to the [127:1] segment of the CID/CSD register. The reserved bit [2] of the CID/CSD
[0] fixed to 1 is occupied by the end bit, and the end bit is also fixed to 1. The format is as follows.

32.3.4 Data Transfer
Data transfer is carried out on the data line SDIO_D, which has 3 widths of 1/4/8 bits. During data transfer, the
start bit of a clock is generally at the front, the high bit of each byte is in the front, and the low bit is in the back.
For the block transfer mode only supported by the SD card, the data transfer of each block is followed by a CRC.
Enable the RANDOM_LEN_EN bit, configure the byte length indicated by DBLOCKSIZE2, configure the total
length of the transferred data indicated by R32_SDIO_DLEN, enable the DTEN bit, and fill in the data to the
R32_SDIO_FIFO, then you can complete the transfer of the block of any byte length with CRC checksum.
The MMC card also supports the data streaming transfer mode, at this time no CRC is attached. the following
figure shows the format of the data transfer.

32.3.5 Slave Mode
Turning on the SLV_MODE bit means that it is in the state of waiting for commands from the host, with received
command parameters placed in RESP1 and received command indexes placed in RESP2, while automatically
answering to the host with an R1 type of answer, with the answer parameter being the value of CMDARG.
Data sent and received in slave mode refer to master mode, but the slave can use the SLV_FORCE_ERR bit to
force a data block CRC error, thus indicating an undesired data read or write.
```
Note: The slave supports only the R1 type of answer, and the command indexes and parameter meanings used for
```
```
master-slave communication are defined by the software;
```

32.4.1.4 RCA
The relative card address register stores the address of the card, which is 16 bits, and the default value is 0.
32.4.2 Voltage Switch
In the later stage of SD card initialization, it is necessary to switch the interface level, and switch the IO level of
the clock line, data line and command line of the SD card to the 1.8V level. For devices whose slew rate is not
good enough, using a lower-level standard can help increase the frequency. However, the power supply voltage of
SD does not necessarily change, and only SD cards with low voltage power supply appear in the newer version of
the protocol.
The steps for switching the voltage are shown in the figure below.
Figure 32-13 Voltage switch sequence
CMD55 R1 CMD41 R3 CMD55 R1 CMD41 R3 CMD11 R1 VoltageSwitching CMD2 R2
32.4.3 Clock Switch
During initialization, the clock of the SD card is only 400KHz. After the voltage switch is completed, the clock
can be increased to a higher level. For example, the first speed of the SDHC card UHS-I mode, the bus clock can
reach 80MHz. In view of the IO output capability of the microcontroller, the clock should be limited to 50MHz.
32.5 Interrupt
32.5.1 SDIO Interrupt
```
SDIO supports a variety of interrupt sources. As shown in the interrupt enable register (R32_SDIO_IER), there
```
are 24 situations that can trigger interrupts, and users can enable them as appropriate.
32.5.2 SDIO Device Interrupt
It should be noted that not only SDIO peripherals can report interrupts to the CPU, but also external SDIO cards
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 721
and MMC cards can report interrupts to SDIO peripherals. In 4-bit bus mode, the interrupt line is D1, and in 8-bit
bus mode, the interrupt line is D7, active low. If SDIO detects that D1 or D7 is low level in the idle state, it should
read the status register or interrupt flag register of the SDIO device to respond to the interrupt in time. The CPU
can get whether the SDIO host receives an interrupt through the SDIOIT bit of the R32_SDIO_STA register.

```
Chapter 33 SD/EMMC Controller (SDMMC)
```
This chapter's module description applies only to the CH32H417, CH32H416 microcontroller product.
The system provides one SDMMC controller host/slave interface with a maximum transmission clock of 200MHz.
It supports 1-wire, 4-wire, and 8-wire communication modes, as well as dual-edge sampling. External devices
such as SD/TF cards and eMMC cards can be connected. Application code can flexibly configure various
parameters including data transmission/reception commands, response packet formats, valid data packet modes
and lengths, and dual-buffer length switching thresholds.
```
Note: When using 1-wire or 4-wire mode, unused data lines corresponding to GPIO pins cannot be repurposed for
```
output. They may be used for input multiplexing or as general-purpose GPIO outputs.
33.1 Main Features
 Support SD physical layer 1.0 and 2.0 specifications, as well as UHS-I SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 modes
compliant with SD 3.0 specifications
```
 Compliant with EMMC Card Specifications 4.4 and 4.5.1; supports HS200 and HS400 modes per EMMC
```
Card Specification 5.0
 Communication modes support single-wire, four-wire, and eight-wire configurations
 Maximum communication clock single-edge up to 200MHz, dual-edge up to 180MHz
 Support dual-edge sampling
 Flexible configurable packet length, command format, and response status
 Provide hardware-automated clock stop function during data block intervals
 Support SD cards, SDIO cards, eMMC cards, and other devices compliant with SD interface protocols
 Support SDIO slave interface, enabling data exchange with chips featuring SDIO host interfaces
 DMA dual-buffering capability
33.2 Register Description
33.2.1 Communication Clock
 Frequency configuration
The controller interface provides two clock modes: low-speed mode and high-speed mode. Generally, the SD
protocol stipulates that the communication clock of about 400kHz should be used for the early initialization of the
equipment with SD interface to ensure better communication compatibility. When the parameter information of
the external equipment is obtained, it can be switched to a higher clock frequency for communication according to
its internally supported configuration.
Set the bit9 of R16_EMMC_CLK_DIV register to select the clock mode, and set the bit[4:0] frequency division
value to get the final SDIO interface output clock. Bit8 controls whether the EMMC peripheral outputs a clock
signal to the MSDCK pin, and it is necessary to ensure that the IO mode of the MSDCK pin is configured as
push-pull output.
 Phase configuration
When communicating with external SDIO interface devices, due to high clock frequency, hardware wiring, device
characteristics and other factors, signal sampling errors will occur.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 734
```
The system SDIO controller's host interface provides an output clock phase inversion (180° offset) function.
```
Setting bit 10 of register R16_EMMC_CLK_DIV to 1 physically inverts the output clock signal, while the
controller's internal clock remains unchanged. This method allows adjustment of communication timing.
```
Note: At higher SDCLK frequency, if the recommended timing adjustment register value can't communicate stably,
```
users need to initiate a bus sampling tuning sequence to find a better sampling point.
33.2.2 Command Sending and Response
The 48-bit data packet with fixed command length sent by SDIO host interface to slave machine is transmitted
serially on MCMD line. Some commands don't need the slave to respond, and some commands need the slave to
respond to reply packets or data packets with different lengths.
```
 General command format: Start bit (0)+ Transmission bit (1)+ Command index+ Parameter +CRC7+ End bit
```
```
(1)
```
The start bit, data bits, CRC7, and stop bit are automatically filled by the hardware. The command index and
parameters vary depending on the command and must be passed to the hardware controller by the application
```
code. Configure the parameter field in the SD command by writing to the R32_EMMC_ARGUMENT register;
```
Writing bits [5:0] of the R16_EMMC_CMD_SET register populates the command index, while bits [11:8] of this
register configure the hardware's expected response packet detection for this command. Writing to the
R16_EMMC_CMD_SET register triggers the hardware to transmit the command packet sequence on the MCMD
signal line.
```
 Short Response Format: Start bit (0) + Transmission bit (0) + Command Index + Parameters + CRC7 + Stop
```
```
bit (1)
```
```
 Long Response Format: Start bit (0) + Transmission bit (0) + Reserved field (111111b) + Data + Stop bit (1)
```
Slave response packets are categorized by length into 48-bit and 136-bit packets, with 32 bits and 128 bits of
user-valid data respectively. After sending a host command, the R16_EMMC_INT_FG register can be queried. If
the RB_EMMC_IF_CMDDONE flag is set to 1, the R32_EMMC_RESPONSE register can be read to obtain the
valid data from the slave interface response packet. If the response packet is abnormal, corresponding flags in bits
[2:0] of the R16_EMMC_INT_FG register will be set.
33.2.3 Read Multiple Data Blocks Consecutively
```
For the operation of reading data (transmitted through data lines) in the SD protocol command, the following
```
configuration is required:
```
1) Initialization: Configure the R16_EMMC_CONTROL register to set the sampling edges for commands and
```
data, the data bus width for transmission and reception, and enable DMA functionality. Configure the
RB_EMMC_TOCNT_MASK bit in the R8_EMMC_TIMEOUT register to set the command timeout and data
timeout durations. Configure the R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register to set the DMA start address for storing
read data. Configure the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register to set the single data block length during
transfer and the total number of data blocks to be read. Configure the R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE register to
set the DMA transfer direction to “SD to Controller.” Optionally configure whether to automatically stop the
clock during block transfer intervals, allowing sufficient time for application code to perform processing tasks
before software resumes the transfer.
```
2) Send commands to the SDIO slave interface device. These commands instruct the slave device to transmit
```
data from the data bus to the host interface, such as CMD17 and CMD18 in the SD protocol.
```
3) The controller interface reads data from the data line: After the slave interface device responds to the host
```
command, if the device is ready for data transfer, it outputs data from the data line based on the host clock
signal, with the start signal being a low level. The host controller samples the signal and transfers it via
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 735
internal DMA to the user-configured SRAM region. Each transfer of data set by
RB_EMMC_BKSIZE_MASK indicates completion of one data block. Simultaneously, the internal total
number of transferred data blocks is decremented by one. Once all data blocks are transferred, the internal
DMA ceases further data transfers. During this process, the hardware sets the RB_EMMC_IF_BKGAP flag
upon completing each data block read. When all data blocks are read, the hardware sets the
RB_EMMC_IF_TRANDONE flag. If a data timeout occurs during the controller's receive wait period or a
CRC error is detected in the received data, the RB_EMMC_IF_DATTMO and RB_EMMC_IF_TRANERR
flags are set respectively. Application code can configure the corresponding interrupt control bits in the
interrupt enable register R16_EMMC_INT_EN. When the corresponding interrupt flag is set, it triggers the
EMMC interrupt service routine.
```
4) Detection Status: The R32_EMMC_STATUS register enables real-time monitoring of the logic levels on data
```
line MD0 and command line MCMD. It evaluates these levels according to protocol-defined timing
specifications. The MASK_BLOCK_NUM field records the number of data blocks successfully transferred
via DMA during the current command transmission.
33.2.4 Write Multiple Data Blocks Consecutively
```
1) Configure the R16_EMMC_CONTROL register to set the sampling edges for commands and data, the data
```
bus width for transmission and reception, and enable DMA functionality. Configure the
RB_EMMC_TOCNT_MASK bit in the R8_EMMC_TIMEOUT register to set the command timeout and data
timeout durations. After successful command transmission, configure the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG
register to set the single data block length during transfer and the total number of data blocks to be read,
thereby initiating data transfer. Configure the R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE register to set the DMA transfer
direction to “Controller to SD”.
```
2) Send commands to the SDIO slave interface device. These commands require the host interface to transmit
```
data to the slave device via the data cable, such as CMD24 and CMD25 in the SD protocol.
```
3) The controller interface writes data to the data line: After the slave interface device responds to the host
```
```
command, it generates a response packet and releases the data line state (non-low level). At this point, the host
```
can drive the data line to output a data block. Writing to the DMA register R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 or
performing a write operation to the R32_EMMC_WRITE_CONT register both trigger the host interface to
drive the data line. The difference lies in the behavior when manipulating register R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1:
the hardware loads the current value of the R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register internally and fetches data
from this address to send to the controller. whereas writing to the R32_EMMC_WRITE_CONT register
instructs the hardware to continue fetching SRAM data from the position currently occupied by the DMA
```
internally. Therefore, to change the DMA address (making it non-contiguous with previous data), the
```
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register must be rewritten to resume data line output. If the new address is
contiguous with previously written data, the hardware automatically fetches data from the address and moves
it. You can directly write to the R32_EMMC_WRITE_CONT register to instruct the controller to continue
data line output. Each time data of the size specified by RB_EMMC_BKSIZE_MASK is output, it indicates
the completion of one data block transfer. Simultaneously, the internal total number of transferred data blocks
is decremented by one. Once all data blocks have been transferred, the internal DMA will cease further data
output. During this process, upon completing the read of each data block, the hardware sets the
RB_EMMC_IF_BKGAP flag. When all data blocks are read, the hardware sets the
RB_EMMC_IF_TRANDONE flag. If a data timeout occurs during the controller's wait for reception or a
CRC error is detected in the received data, the RB_EMMC_IF_DATTMO and RB_EMMC_IF_TRANERR
flags are set respectively. Application code can configure the corresponding interrupt control bits in the
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 736
interrupt enable register R16_EMMC_INT_EN. When the corresponding interrupt flag is set, it triggers the
EMMC interrupt service routine.
Note 1: When the controller interface writes data blocks to external devices, it must wait for command
transmission and acknowledgment completion before setting the DMA address. This is because setting the DMA
```
address notifies the hardware to drive the data lines; if the command has not yet finished transmitting at this point,
```
the device will not accept the data.
```
Note 2: During a transmission process (including data read and write) for a given command execution, if a CRC
```
```
error (RB_EMMC_IF_TRANERR) occurs, the hardware will not count it as a successful transmission and will not
```
decrement the total transmission block count. It will proceed to transmit the next block. However, DMA will still
place the data block containing this CRC error into the corresponding SRAM address area. Application code must
handle this situation appropriately.
33.2.5 DMA Dual-buffer Function
The system provides DMA dual-buffering functionality, featuring two DMA address registers:
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 and R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG2, along with the data block length threshold
RB_EMMC_DMATN_CNT for DMA switching. When the data block length threshold starting from the
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register address completes transmission, the hardware switches to the address range
set by R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG2 for data transfer. Upon reaching the transfer threshold, it cycles back to the
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 range. This process repeats until all data blocks configured by
RB_EMMC_BKNUM_MASK are fully transferred.
Each time non-zero data is written to the RB_EMMC_BKNUM_MASK field of the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG
register, a data transfer is initiated. Concurrently, the hardware directs DMA operations to the address range
starting at R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1. The flag-setting conditions during the transfer process remain consistent
with the previously described behavior. Application code may optionally enable the corresponding interrupt flag
to trigger the EMMC interrupt service routine.
33.2.6 Slave Mode
Slave mode operation
The hardware in slave mode only supports R1-type responses, so the R16_EMMC_CMD_SET register has no
effect in slave mode.
```
1) Host queries slave data status:
```
The slave device pre-populates the ARGUMENT register with its desired data reception/transmission status. The
host sends CMD13 to query the slave's status and determines whether to read or write to the slave based on the
response.
```
Note: The use of CMD13 and the bit definitions in the slave's response are software-defined.
```
```
2) Host sends CMD18 to read multiple blocks:
```
The CMD18 command parameter from the host no longer specifies a sector address but instead indicates the
number of blocks to be read in this operation. Upon receiving the command interrupt, the slave configures the
DMA address, sets the R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE, reads the block count from the command parameter register,
and writes it into the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register.
```
2) Host sends CMD25 to write multiple blocks:
```
The CMD25 command parameter from the host no longer specifies a sector address but instead indicates the
number of blocks to be written in this operation. Upon receiving the command interrupt, the slave configures the
DMA address and sets R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE. It then reads the block count from the command parameter
register and writes it into the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 737
Slave error processing
The slave responds to host commands with an R1-type acknowledgment, where the response parameter is the
value of the slave's ARGUMENT register. If the slave fails to acknowledge the host due to a CRC error during
command reception, the host should retry the current command.
If the slave experiences an internal FIFO overflow during transmission or reception, the hardware automatically
forces the current data block to be CRC-erroneous, signaling transmission issues to the host. Alternatively,
software can set RB_SLV_FORCE_ERR to force transmission of the erroneous CRC block.
The slave hardware parses a special command, CMD63, to simplify the slave software's handling of transmission
errors. If a CRC error occurs during host transmission or reception, the host immediately sends CMD63. Upon
receiving CMD63, the slave software must reset the data state machine. The hardware automatically sets the DMA
address to the starting address of the previous erroneous packet. Once master-slave negotiation resumes
transmission, for read operations, the slave software only needs to set the block count in
R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG. For write operations, the software configures the block count in
R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG and writes to the RESPONSE3 register to complete retransmission and resume data
transfer.
Dual buffer mode
If the slave operates in dual-buffered mode, and an error occurs while the master reads the last block of data from
buf0, the master will send CMD63 during the transmission of the first block of buf1 to indicate a CRC error in the
previous packet. Therefore, the slave should only update the data in buf0 after the first block of buf1 has been
successfully transmitted. The newly added interrupt bit RB_SIF_SLV_BUF_RELEASE is generated when the
first sector of the new buffer is successfully transmitted.
1 block | Update buf1 buffer
buf0 ----------------------------------------------------------------
1 block | Update buf0 buffer
buf1 ----------------------------------------------------------------

```
Chapter 34 Programmable Protocol I/O Microcontroller (PIOC)
```
A programmable protocol I/O microcontroller is embedded in the chip. The microcontroller is based on the RISC
core with a single clock cycle, runs at the main frequency of the system, has a program ROM with 2K instructions,
49 SFR registers and PWM timers/counters, and supports the protocol control of two I/O pins.
34.1 Main Features
 RISC core, optimized single cycle bit manipulation instruction set, fully static design.
 Multiplex 4K bytes of system SRAM as 2K capacity program ROM, supports program pause and dynamic
loading.
 Provide 33 bytes of 1 register each in bidirectional and unidirectional mode, providing 6 levels of
independent stacking.
 Support 2 general-purpose bi-directional I/O protocol controls and input level change detection.
 Support 1- and 2-wire interfaces with multiple protocol specifications by dynamically loading different
protocol programs.
 Support 1-wire ARGB chip 1024-stage series connection
34.2 Instruction, Program Space and Stack
34.2.1 Instruction Set
eMCU adopts RISC8B core with reduced instruction set, with data width of 8 bits and instruction width of 16 bits.
There are 66 instructions, all of which are single clock cycles, except that the jump instruction is double clock
cycle and the program space reading and writing instruction is double cycle. For more information, please refer to
RISC8B core instruction set and assembly tool document CHRISC8B.PDF.
34.2.2 Program ROM
EMCU's program ROM comes from 4-kbyte system SRAM multiplexing. When SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 0, it is
dedicated to the system SRAM on the host side, and when SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 1, it is dedicated to eMCU's
program ROM.
The program space of eMCU is 2048 words, and the address of the program space ranges from 0x0000 to 0x07FF.
The instruction at address 0 in the program ROM has a special purpose and will not be executed.
eMCU chip supports reading program space. The steps are as follows: first, write the lower 8 bits of the target
address into SFR_INDIR_ADDR, and the upper 3 bits of the target address into the A register, and then execute
the RDCODE instruction, so that the 16-bit data in the program space can be read out at one time, which is
divided into high and low bytes, with the low byte returned to the A register and the high byte returned to the
SFR_INDIR_ADDR. This operation can be used for double-byte table lookup.
eMCU chip does not support writing to program space.
34.2.3 Stack
The eMCU features a stack memory with a depth of 6 levels and an 11-bit data width. It is used to store the
program return address during subroutine calls and can also be employed with the PUSHAS instruction to save
variables, status data, and other information from the running program onto the stack.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 751
34.2.4 Sleep and Awakening
When SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 0, the eMCU program will suspend execution. After executing the SLEEP or
SLEEPX instruction, the eMCU enters sleep mode. The eMCU is designed as fully static, where program
suspension and sleep mode have equivalent effects.
After entering sleep, the eMCU supports two wake-up methods: - Wake-up via level change on a pin with level
change detection enabled. - Wake-up via the SB_MST_CLK_GATE signal transitioning from 0 to 1.
34.2.5 Event Wait Instruction
The WAITB instruction supports waiting for 8 types of events. When the event is invalid, WAITB continues to
```
wait indefinitely, with the program counter (PC) remaining unchanged. Upon detecting the target event, the wait is
```
terminated, and the next instruction is executed. Timer timeout reset can be optionally enabled during the wait.
```
The instruction parameter WB_DATA_SW_MR_0 indicates waiting until SB_DATA_SW_MR becomes 0 to exit;
```
if it is already 0, exit immediately.
```
The instruction parameter WB_BIT_CYC_TAIL_1 indicates waiting until SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL becomes 1 to exit;
```
if it is already 1, it exits immediately.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_I0_FALL indicates waiting until SB_PORT_IN0 detects a falling edge to
```
exit; if a falling edge was previously detected and recorded, it also exits immediately, clearing the falling edge
```
detection record upon exit.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_I0_RISE indicates waiting until SB_PORT_IN0 detects a rising edge to
exit. If a rising edge has already been detected as recorded, it exits directly and clears the rising edge detection
record upon exit.
The instruction parameter WB_DATA_MW_SR_1 indicates waiting until SB_DATA_MW_SR is 1 to exit. If it is
already 1, it exits directly.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_XOR1_1 indicates waiting until SB_PORT_XOR1 is 1 before exiting. If it
is already 1, exit directly.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_XOR0_0 indicates waiting until SB_PORT_XOR0 is 0 before exiting. If it
is already 0, exit directly.
```
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_XOR0_1 indicates waiting until SB_PORT_XOR0 is 1 before exiting; if it
```
is already 1, exit immediately.
34.2.6 Bit Transfer Instruction
Bit transfer instructions support two bit operation registers: BP1F and BG1F correspond to register
SFR_INDIR_ADDR, while BP2F and BG2F correspond to register SFR_DATA_EXCH.
Bit transfer instructions BP1F and BP2F support four independent bit outputs: Parameter 0# BIO_FLAG_C
corresponds to SB_FLAG_C bit, parameter 1# BO_BIT_TX_O0 corresponds to SB_BIT_TX_O0, parameter 2#
BO_PORT_OUT0 corresponds to SB_PORT_OUT0, and parameter 3# BO_PORT_OUT1 corresponds to
SB_PORT_OUT1.
```
Bit transfer instructions BG1F and BG2F support four independent bit inputs: Parameter 0# (BIO_FLAG_C)
```
```
corresponds to bit SB_FLAG_C, parameter 1# (BI_BIT_RX_I0) corresponds to bit SB_BIT_RX_I0, parameter 2#
```
```
(BI_PORT_IN0) corresponds to bit SB_PORT_IN0, and parameter 3# (BI_PORT_IN1) corresponds to bit
```
SB_PORT_IN1.
The bit transfer instruction BCTC supports four independent bit inputs: Parameter 0# BI_C_XOR_IN0 updates bit
```
SB_FLAG_C to the XOR result of SB_FLAG_C and SB_PORT_IN0; Parameter 1# BI_BIT_RX_I0 corresponds
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 752
```
to SB_BIT_RX_I0; Parameter 2# BI_PORT_IN0 corresponds to SB_PORT_IN0; Parameter 3# BI_PORT_IN1
```
corresponds to SB_PORT_IN1.
34.3 Data Space and Registers and Addressing
```
The data space of the eMCU includes 49 dedicated special function registers (SFRs) addressed via 8-bit addresses
```
within the range 0x00 to 0x3F. All registers have a data width of 1 byte, equivalent to 8 bits.
Some SFRs are accessible for read/write or read-only operations from the host side, which supports 8-bit, 16-bit,
or 32-bit width read/write operations. The host side has write priority. When both the eMCU and host attempt to
write to the same register simultaneously, the eMCU's write operation is automatically discarded.
The eMCU's addressing modes include: immediate address, immediate fast address, standard direct address,
extended direct address, indirect address, and bit address. The latter four are used for register addressing.
The indirect addressing range is 0x000-0x0FF, covering all registers of the eMCU. The eMCU provides two sets
of indirect address registers, each consisting of an address register and a data read/write port. First, write the target
register's address into the address register, then read or write the target register via the data read/write port.
The address range for extended direct addressing is 0x000-0x1FF, where the instruction directly provides a 9-bit
register address. This is only applicable to the following two direct register read/write instructions: MOV
register,A or F, and MOVA register.
The addressing range for standard direct addressing is 0x000-0x0FF. The instruction directly provides an 8-bit
register address, applicable to all direct address instructions except those covered by extended direct addressing,
such as CLR register, ADD register, BS register, bit, etc. When addressing a larger range is required, indirect
addressing should be employed.
Immediate number fast addressing enables rapid writing of operands from instruction codes to target registers
```
without requiring an A register intermediary. MOVA1F is used for fast setting of register #1 (SFR_PORT_DIR),
```
```
while MOVA2F is used for fast setting of register #2 (SFR_PORT_IO). MOVA1P and MOVA2P employ indirect
```
addressing for rapid setting of all registers, equivalent to first performing immediate addressing followed by
indirect addressing within a single cycle.
Bit addressing utilizes a 3-bit address provided directly by the instruction. Register addressing can employ either
standard direct addressing or indirect addressing, covering address ranges 0x000 to 0x0FF respectively, thereby
enabling access to any bit within any register.

The default values after reset are all represented by binary numbers, and the bit values are described as follows:
```
0: Always 0 after reset;
```
```
1: Always 1 after reset;
```
```
X: Reset does not affect data; initial data value is undefined;
```
```
-: Always clears to 0 after power-on reset; system reset or host forced reset does not affect data.
```
The read/write specifications for the host side are as follows:
```
W: Bits that can be read or written;
```
```
R: Read-only bits;
```
```
U: Invisible bit, neither readable nor writable;
```
```
S: Read-only switch bit. The host-side visible SFR_TIMER_CTRL differs from the eMCU side in that the
```
SB_TMR0_ENABLE and SB_TMR0_OUT_EN bits are replaced by SB_GP_BIT_Y and SB_GP_BIT_X
respectively.

```
34.4.4 Address Register of Indirect Addressed 2 (SFR_INDIR_ADDR2)
```
These are 2 sets of indirect address registers, each consisting of an address register and a data read/write port. First,
write the destination register's address into the address register. Then, read or write the destination register by
accessing the data read/write port.
The data read/write port SFR_INDIR_PORT for indirect addressing reads/writes the destination register specified
by the indirectly addressed address register SFR_INDIR_ADDR. The data read/write port SFR_INDIR_PORT2
for indirect addressing reads/writes the destination register specified by the indirectly addressed address register
SFR_INDIR_ADDR2.
The dedicated instruction MOVIP is used to load an 8-bit destination address into SFR_INDIR_ADDR.
Additionally, SFR_INDIR_ADDR can be modified independently by other non-dedicated instructions.
The dedicated instruction MOVIA is used to load an 8-bit target address into SFR_INDIR_ADDR2, and
SFR_INDIR_ADDR2 can also be independently modified by other non-dedicated instructions.
The address register SFR_INDIR_ADDR2 for Indirect Addressing Mode 2 features automatic incrementing.
When executing the “MOV SFR_INDIR_PORT2,A” read instruction or the “MOVA SFR_INDIR_PORT2” write
instruction to RAM, SFR_INDIR_ADDR2 will automatically increment by 1 upon instruction completion.
The dedicated instructions MOVA1P and MOVA2P are used to directly and rapidly write operands from the
instruction code into target registers, equivalent to performing immediate addressing followed by indirect
addressing within a single cycle.
```
34.4.5 Status Register (SFR_STATUS_REG)
```
The status register contains the result status of the ALU, general-purpose bit variables, and stack usage flags. After
executing arithmetic or logical operations, the eMCU sets corresponding status bits based on the results, enabling
the program to make judgments and perform further processing. General-purpose bit variables can be defined for
specific purposes by the application.
The timer timeout reset monitors the timeout of WAITB wait instructions. After disabling SB_TMR0_ENABLE
and enabling SB_EN_TOUT_RST, the timer counts during WAITB execution. When overflow occurs and
SB_TMR0_CYCLE is 1, a timeout reset is triggered. The timer initial value is automatically reloaded each time
the WAITB instruction exits the WAITB wait state upon condition fulfillment. Counting does not occur during
execution of non-WAITB instructions when SB_TMR0_ENABLE is 0, meaning the timer timeout reset applies
exclusively to the WAITB instruction.

operations within a 256-byte range.

```
34.4.10 Initial Value Register of Timer 0 (SFR_TMR0_INIT)
```

```
34.4.11 Control Register of Timer (SFR_TIMER_CTRL)
```
Timer 0 is an 8-bit counter. The count value is stored in the SFR_TMR0_COUNT register, which supports direct
data write to load new values. The clock frequency for Timer 0 is selected via SB_TMR0_FREQ. Timer 0 can
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 758
```
operate in either timer mode or pulse width modulator (PWM) mode.
```
In timer mode, Timer 0's initial count value is stored in advance in the initial value register SFR_TMR0_INIT.
Timer 0 always counts from this initial value up to 0FFH. Upon overflowing from 0FFH, Timer 0 automatically
reloads the initial value from the initial value register SFR_TMR0_INIT and begins counting from the initial
value toward 0FFH again. When counting from 0FEH to 0FFH, Timer 0 automatically sets the cycle signal
SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 1. When counting overflows from 0FFH back to the initial value, Timer 0 automatically
```
clears the cycle signal SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 0. The frequency of SB_TMR0_CYCLE is (SB_TMR0_FREQ
```
```
clock frequency) / (256 - SFR_TMR0_INIT), with a duty cycle of 1 / (256 - SFR_TMR0_INIT). This means
```
SB_TMR0_CYCLE is active for one clock cycle per period.
In pulse width modulator mode, Timer 0 always counts from 00H to 0FFH, then overflows from 0FFH and resets
to 00H to begin a new count cycle. Its period is always 256 clock cycles. When the count value exceeds the value
```
stored in the Timer 0 initialization register (SFR_TMR0_INIT), Timer 0 automatically sets the cycle signal
```
SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 1. When the count value overflows from 0FFH back to 00H, Timer 0 automatically clears
```
the cycle signal SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 0. The duty cycle of SB_TMR0_CYCLE is (255 - SFR_TMR0_INIT) /
```
256.
SB_TMR0_OUT_EN determines whether the internal signal SB_TMR0_CYCLE or its 2-division signal is output
```
to the IO0 pin. When the internal signal is high, the pin outputs a high level; otherwise, it outputs a low level. If
```
```
the cycle signal output is enabled, then in timer mode, the 2-division signal of SB_TMR0_CYCLE (reduced to
```
```
half frequency with a 50% duty cycle) will be output through the IO0 pin; in pulse width modulator mode, the
```
SB_TMR0_CYCLE signal will be output through the IO0 pin.
The following table describes the timer control register SFR_TIMER_CTRL.
Bit Name Description Reset value

```
34.4.14 System Configuration Register (SFR_CTRL_RD)
```
The System Configuration Register provides control bits for the host and status bits for bidirectional data
exchange.
SB_INT_REQ is fully controlled by the eMCU to request interrupts or cancel requests to the host. However, the
host can clear SB_INT_REQ to 0 by performing a dummy write operation to the read-only register
SFR_CTRL_RD. Writing to SFR_CTRL_RD has no practical effect on its data.
After the eMCU writes to SFR_CTRL_RD, SB_DATA_SW_MR is automatically set to 1. After the host reads
SFR_CTRL_RD, SB_DATA_SW_MR is automatically cleared to 0.
After the host writes to SFR_CTRL_WR, SB_DATA_MW_SR is automatically set to 1. After the eMCU reads
SFR_CTRL_WR, SB_DATA_MW_SR is automatically cleared to 0.
SB_MST_CLK_GATE also controls the multiplexing of the eMCU program ROM. When SB_MST_CLK_GATE
is 0, it is dedicated to the host-side system SRAM, totaling 4K bytes, enabling dynamic loading of new programs
for the eMCU. When SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 1, it is dedicated to the eMCU program ROM, containing 2K
instructions.
Bits 0 to 4 of the system configuration register are fully controlled by the host and are read-only on the eMCU
side.
The following table describes the system configuration register SFR_SYS_CFG.
Bit Name Description Reset value


```
1: eMCU has written data but the host has not yet read it;
```
0: eMCU has not written data or the host has already read it.
0
5 SB_DATA_MW_SR
SFR_CTRL_WR read status bit:
```
1: Written by host but not yet read by eMCU;
```
0: Not yet written by host or already read by eMCU.
0
4 SB_MST_CFG_B4 Configuration information bit, software-defined purpose 0
3 SB_MST_IO_EN1
IO1 pin mode and output control switch:
```
1: Controlled by eMCU;
```
0: Controlled by host.
0
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 760

```
eMCU;
```

resets.

```
34.4.15 Coded Bit Period Register (SFR_BIT_CYCLE)
```
```
34.4.16 Coded Bit Configuration Register (SFR_BIT_CONFIG)
```
The eMCU supports 2 bit-modulation methods: PWM duty cycle modulation and Manchester modulation.
Setting SB_BIT_CYCLE greater than 3 enables encoding/decoding. When SB_BIT_TX_EN=0, the system
receives data. Input status is received from IO0 based on the preset width, and decoded data is stored in
SB_BIT_RX_I0. When SB_BIT_TX_EN=1, the system transmits data. Raw data to be transmitted is placed in
SB_BIT_TX_O0. After encoding, it is automatically delivered to SB_PORT_OUT0 for pin output.
SB_BIT_CYC_CNT and SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL indicate the cycle status of the encoded bit. When
```
SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL=1, it signifies the current phase is within the last 25% of the bit cycle, indicating that
```
SB_BIT_RX_I0 has completed reception and decoding, and the transmission encoding is finished and has reached
SB_PORT_OUT0.
Setting SB_BIT_CYCLE=0 forces SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL to 1, facilitating Manchester encoding/decoding
initiation.
Setting SFR_BIT_CYCLE clears the rising and falling edge detection records for IO0, enabling the WAITB
instruction to restart waiting.
The following table describes the encoding bit cycle register SFR_BIT_CYCLE.
Bit Name Description Reset value
7 SB_BIT_TX_O0
The original bit data of the coded bit to be sent, which has a
double buffer structure. When a new bit period starts, this bit
can load the next bit data in advance.
0
[6:0] SB_BIT_CYCLE
Sets the width of the coded bit in clock period, which is the
actual clock number of the bit minus 1. Its high 5 bits are 0 to
turn off the encoding and decoding, and they are not 0 to turn
on.
0000000
The following table is a description of the encoding bit configuration register SFR_BIT_CONFIG.
Bit Name Description Reset value
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 761

SB_PORT_OUT0.
0: Disable transmission. If SB_BIT_CYCLE is active,
reception is permitted.
0
6 SB_BIT_CODE_MOD
Modulation methods for encoding bits:
1: Manchester modulation, where 0 remains unchanged
```
within a cycle and 1 flips within a cycle;
```

cycle and 1 having a 75% duty cycle.
0
5 SB_PORT_IN_EDGE
Pin input level sampling timing selection:
1: Sample at the edge of the previous cycle, equivalent to

relatively higher real-time performance.

```
encoding/decoding is complete;
```

The cycle timing status of the encoding bit. Bit cycle timing
operates in clock cycles and is a 7-bit counter.
SB_BIT_CYC_CNT6 to 3 represent bits [6:3] of the counter.

```
34.4.17 Data Register (SFR_DATA_x) (x=0-31)
```
SFR_DATA_x are all bidirectional read/write data registers. Write operations from the host take precedence, and
their functions are software-defined.
Among these, SFR_DATA_EXCH also supports single-cycle bit transfer instructions.
34.5 Application
The eMCU operates at the same clock frequency as the host side, facilitating dynamic data exchange. It features a
rich set of bit manipulation instructions, enabling single-cycle I/O configuration, single-cycle I/O status polling, or
bit data copying. It supports hardware encoding/decoding of PWM or Manchester-modulated bit data, making it
suitable for implementing I/O for various low-to-medium speed communication protocols and for I/O control
requiring precise timing.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 762
```
Chapter 35 Operational Amplifier (OPA) and Comparator (CMP)
```
```
The module consists of 3 independently configurable operational amplifier (OPA1/OPA2/OPA3) and 1
```
```
independently configurable voltage comparator (CMP). The operational amplifier (OPA) supports gain selection
```
or can be used as a voltage comparator.
The input and output of each operational amplifier are connected to the I/O port, and the input pin or gain is
optional, and the output pin can be optionally configured to the universal I/O port or multiplexed as an ADC
sampling channel. The external analog small signal is amplified into the ADC to achieve small-signal ADC
conversion.
The input and output of each voltage comparator are connected to the I/O port, and the input pins are optional, and
the output pins can be optionally configured to the universal I/O port or multiplexed as an TIM internal sampling
```
channel (without using the I/O pin).
```
35.1 Main Features
 OPA input pin/output channel can be selected.
 OPA1 output channel directly connected to comparator input
```
 OPA supports voltage buffer (BUFFER) and programmable gain amplifier (PGA)
```
 CMP input pin selectable
```
 CMP positive input supports selectable DAC output; negative input supports selectable internal self-bias
```
voltage
 CMP supports selectable digital filtering and hysteresis
 CMP output pin selectable as general-purpose I/O port or TIM internal sampling channel
35.2 Function Description
35.2.1 OPA1/OPA2/OPA3
```
OPA1, OPA2, and OPA3 support voltage buffers (BUFFER) and programmable gain amplifiers (PGA). As shown
```
in Figure 35-1, these 3 OPAs share essentially identical functionality. Compared to OPA2 and OPA3, OPA1
features an additional output channel connected to the CMP_P2 input of the voltage comparator.
```
In the R32_OPA_CTLR1 register: Setting the EN1 bit enables OPA1; Setting the PSEL1 bit selects the positive
```
```
input channel for OPA1; Setting the NSEL1 bit selects the negative input channel for OPA1 or enables PGA mode
```
to configure the internal gain of OPA1. Configuring the FB_EN1 bit enables the PGA mode feedback for OPA1.
Configuring the PGADIF1 bit enables the differential input PGA mode, allowing OPA1 to function as a PGA in
conjunction with NSEL1, with the N terminal connected to PA7. Configuring the HS1 bit enables high-speed
mode, which improves slew rate in this mode. Configuring the MODE1[1:0] bits selects the output channel as
either a GPIO or the positive input of a comparator.
```
In the R32_OPA_CTLR2 register: Setting the EN2 bit enables OPA2; Setting the PSEL2 bit selects the positive
```
```
input channel for OPA2; Setting the NSEL2 bit selects the negative input channel for OPA2 or enables PGA mode
```
```
to configure the internal gain of OPA2. Configure the FB_EN2 bit to enable OPA2's PGA mode feedback;
```
configure the PGADIF2 bit to enable differential input PGA mode, allowing OPA2 to function as a PGA with
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 763
```
NSEL2 set, with the N terminal connected to PF12; configure the HS2 bit to enable high-speed mode, which
```

```
improves slew rate in this mode; configure the MODE2 bit to select the output channel.
```
```
In the R32_OPA_CTLR3 register: Configure the EN3 bit to enable OPA3; Configure the PSEL3 bit to select the
```
```
positive input channel for OPA3; Configure the NSEL3 bit to select the negative input channel for OPA3 or enable
```
PGA mode, setting the internal gain of OPA3. Configure the FB_EN3 bit to enable OPA3's PGA mode feedback.
Configure the PGADIF3 bit to enable differential input PGA mode, allowing OPA3 to function as a PGA with
NSEL3 set, with the N terminal connected to PA3. Configure the HS3 bit to enable high-speed mode, which
improves slew rate in this mode. Configure the MODE3 bit to select the output channel.

35.2.2 CMP
CMP supports optional hysteresis characteristics, digital filtering at the output, and optional output filtering. The
structure diagram is shown in Figure 35-2.
```
In the R32_CMP_CTLR register: Configure the EN bit to enable the CMP module; Configure the PSEL[1:0] bits
```
```
to select whether the P-channel is connected to a GPIO input or internally linked to the OPA operational amplifier;
```
Configure the NSEL[1:0] bits to select whether the N-channel is connected to a GPIO input, internally linked to
the DAC output, or connected to an optional internal self-bias voltage. Configure the HYPSEL bit to select the
```
comparator hysteresis voltage; configure the VREF bit to select the CMP internal bias voltage magnitude;
```
```
configure the FILT_EN bit to enable the CMP output digital filtering function; configure the FILT_CFG[8:0] bits
```
to select the CMP output digital filtering sampling interval, which must be greater than the noise width and less
```
than twice the noise width; Configure the FILT_BASE[2:0] bits to set the time reference for the CMP output
```
digital filter sampling. Configure the MODE[3:0] bits to select whether the CMP2 output connects internally to
the I/O or connects to the timer brake input/internal sampling channel of the timer.
In the R32_CMP_STATR register, the output result of CMP filtering function closing/opening can be read through
the OUT_FILT bit.

```
Chapter 36 Serial Audio Interface (SAI)
```
```
Serial Audio Interface (SAI) supports various common audio protocols, such as I2S, PCM/DSP, AC'97, LSB or
```
MSB alignment and TDM, which is suitable for mono and stereo applications. In order to realize the flexibility
and configurability of SAI interface, it adopts two completely independent audio submodules, each of which
```
contains up to four IO pins (SD, SCK, FS and MCLK).
```
SAI can be configured as any combination of master/slave and sending/receiving, and its operation mode can be
set as full duplex/simplex according to the synchronous/asynchronous configuration of audio submodule.
36.1 Main Features
 Provide 2 independent control modules, with each audio submodule configurable in any combination of
master/slave or transmit/receive roles, each featuring an 8-word FIFO
 Audio submodules can operate in synchronous or asynchronous modes, with master/slave configurations
independent of each other
 Flexible slot length configuration, with slots configurable as valid or invalid
```
 Frame synchronization configuration (valid level, valid length, and offset)
```
 Each audio frame contains up to 16 configurable slots
 Up to 16 slots, each supporting 8-bit, 10-bit, 16-bit, 20-bit, 24-bit, or 32-bit data
 Support LSB or MSB data transmission
 Support multiple audio protocols including I2S standard, LSB or MSB alignment, PCM/DSP, TDM, and
AC'97
 Features mono/stereo audio functionality with mute settings
```
 Serial clock strobe edge selection (SCK)
```
 Each audio submodule has 2 independent DMA interfaces supporting slave mode at frequencies up to 4MHz
 Error flag bits and interrupt sources:
- FIFO overflow and underflow;
- Frame sync advance detection in slave mode;
- Frame sync lag detection in slave mode;
- AC'97 codec not ready;
- Clock configuration error.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 771

The SAI primarily consists of 2 independent audio submodules connected to the output via an I/O management
```
module. The I/O line controller manages four dedicated pins (SD, SCK, FS, MCLK) for the specified audio
```
module within the SAI. If both submodules are declared as synchronous modules, certain pins can be shared,
freeing others for use as general-purpose I/O. Whether the MCLK pin can function as an output pin depends on
the specific application and decoding requirements, as well as whether the audio module is configured in master
mode.
Each audio module integrates a 32-bit shift register controlled by the module's own functional state machine. Data
storage and retrieval are performed via dedicated FIFOs. These FIFOs can be accessed by the CPU or via DMA to
reduce the CPU's communication load.
The audio submodule can function as either a transmitter or receiver in both master and slave modes. Master
mode indicates that the SAI generates the SCK bit clock and frame synchronizing signal, while slave mode
indicates that the SCK bit clock and frame synchronizing signal originate from another external or internal master
device. In specific cases, the direction of the FS signal is not directly related to the master or slave mode definition.
```
Within the AC'97 protocol, even when the SAI (link controller) is configured to consume the SCK clock, the FS
```
```
signal remains an SAI output (this also applies in slave mode).
```
36.3 Function Description
36.3.1 Clock Generator
Both independent audio submodules of the SAI have their own clock generators, but these clock generators
```
function identically.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 772
```
When the audio module is configured in master mode, the clock generator provides the bit clock (SCK) and the
```
```
master clock (MCLK) for the external decoder. When the audio module is defined as slave mode, the clock
```
generator is disabled.
The bit clock strobe edge on SCK can be configured via the CKSTR bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. This
bit applies to both master and slave modes.
It is recommended to select the PLL output of 295MHz as the input clock for the SAI.


The clock source of the clock generator comes from the product clock controller. SAI_CK_x clock is equivalent to
the master clock, and can divide the frequency for the external decoder through MCKDIV[5:0] bits:
```
If MCKDIV[5:0] is not equal to 0000b, then MCLK_x = SAI_CK_x / (MCKDIV[5:0] * 2)
```
If MCKDIV[5:0] is equal to 0000b, then MCLK_x = SAI_CK_x
The MCLK signal is used only in TDM.
Frequency division must be uniform to maintain a 50% duty cycle on both the MCLK output and the SCK clock.
If the MCKDIV[5:0] bits are set to 0000b, a single division ratio is used to make MCLK equal to SAI_CK_x.
In the SAI, a single ratio MCLK/FS = 256 is used. In most cases, three frequency ranges will be encountered, as

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 773
If the corresponding audio module is configured as the master module and the NODIV bit in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register is set to 0, the master clock can be generated for an external decoder via the I/O port.
When the audio module is defined as slave mode, the clock generator is disabled. The values of the NODIV and
MCKDIV bits are ignored. Additionally, the MCLK I/O pin is released and can be used as a general-purpose I/O.
The bit clock is derived from the master clock. The bit clock divider sets the division factor between the bit clock
```
(SCK) and the master clock (SCK) according to the following formula:
```
```
SCK = MCLK*(FRL[7:0]+1)/256
```
Among them:
```
256 is the fixed ratio between MCLK and the audio sampling frequency;
```
FRL[7:0] represents the number of bit clock cycles within an audio frame minus one, configured in the
R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
```
In Master Mode, (FRL[7:0]+1) must equal a power of 2 to yield an even number of MCLK pulses per bit clock
```
```
cycle. A 50% duty cycle is guaranteed on the bit clock (SCK).
```
The SAI_CK_x clock may also equal the bit clock frequency. In this case, the NODIV bit in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register should be set to 1, and the values within the MCKDIV divider and the bit clock
divider will be ignored. At this time, the number of bits in each frame is completely configurable, and it is not
necessary to be equal to several powers of 2.
36.3.2 Operation Mode
The SAI audio submodule can be configured via the MODE[1:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to operate
in any combination of master/slave, transmit/receive modes.
Each audio module within the SAI is enabled via the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. In slave mode,
once this bit is activated, the transmitter or receiver becomes sensitive to activity on the clock line, data line, and
sync line.
In master TX mode, the enabled audio module immediately generates bit clocks for the external slave module
even if no data is present in the FIFO, but the generation of the FS signal is controlled by the presence of data in
the FIFO. Upon receiving the first data to be transmitted, the FIFO outputs this data to the external slave module.
If no data is present in the FIFO for transmission, subsequent values of zero are transmitted within the audio frame,
and an underflow flag is generated.
In slave mode, audio frames commence when the audio module is enabled and the SOF bit is detected.
In slave TX mode, an underflow event cannot occur on the first frame after enabling the audio module, as the
forced operation sequence is as follows:
```
1) Write to R32_SAI_xDATAR via software or DMA;
```
```
2) Wait until the FIFO threshold (FLTH) flag differs from 000b (indicating FIFO is empty);
```
```
3) Enable the audio module for slave transmit mode.
```
Master mode
In master mode, the SAI provides clock signals to connected external devices:
```
1) Bit clock and frame sync are output on pins SCK and FS, respectively;
```
```
2) If required, the SAI can also generate the master clock on the MCLK pin.
```
FS is generated when the FIFO is not empty and at the start of a frame. CK and MCLK generation, however, are
not dependent on the FIFO status and are produced whenever the audio submodule is enabled.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 774
Slave mode
In slave mode, the SAI receives clock signals from external devices:
```
1) When the SAI submodule is configured for asynchronous mode, the SCK and FS pins are configured as inputs.
```
```
2) If the SAI submodule is configured to operate synchronously with the second audio submodule, the
```
corresponding SCK and FS pins are released for use as general-purpose I/O.
In slave mode, the MCLK pin is not used and can be assigned to other functions. It is recommended to enable the
slave device before enabling the master device.
36.3.3 Internal Synchronization Mode
The audio submodule can run synchronously with another audio submodule in the same SAI, which is also called
internal synchronization mode. In this case, they will share the bit clock and frame synchronization signal to
reduce the number of external pins occupied during communication. An audio module configured in synchronous
mode will release its SCK, FS and MCLK pins to be used as GPIO, while an audio module configured in
```
asynchronous mode will use its SCK, FS and MCLKI/O pins (if the audio module is configured as a master
```
```
module).
```
Typically, the audio module in synchronous mode can be used to configure the SAI in full-duplex mode. One of
```
the two audio modules can be configured as the master module and the other as the slave module; alternatively,
```
```
both can be configured as slave modules. One module can be set as the asynchronous module (with the
```
```
SYNCEN[1:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register set to 00b), and the other as the synchronous module (with
```
```
the SYNCEN[1:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register set to 01b).
```
```
Note: Due to the internal resynchronization phase, the HCLK frequency must be greater than twice the bit rate
```
clock frequency.
36.3.4 Frame Configuration
36.3.4.1 Frame Synchronization
```
The FS signal is used as a frame synchronization signal (SOF) in audio. The waveform of this signal can be
```
completely configurable by configuring R32_SAI_xFRCR register, which can support various audio protocols
with special specifications during frame synchronization. The following figure shows the configurability of audio
frames.

V1.7 775
```
In AC'97 mode or SPDIF mode (when the PRTCFG[1:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register are set to 10b or
```
```
01b), the frame sync signal waveform is forced to conform to the AC'97 protocol. The value of the
```
R32_SAI_xFRCR register is ignored.
Each audio module operates independently and therefore requires specific configuration.
36.3.4.2 Frame Length
Master mode
Setting the FRL[7:0] field of the R32_SAI_xFRCR register to 1 configures the audio frame length to a maximum
of 256 bit clock cycles.
If the frame length exceeds the number of slots declared for that frame, the remaining bits to be transmitted will
be zero-padded or the SD line will be released to a high configuration, depending on the state of the TRIS bit in
the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register. In receive mode, the remaining bits are ignored.
```
If the NODIV bit is cleared, (FRL+1) must equal a power of 2 (from 8 to 256) to ensure each bit clock cycle of the
```
```
audio frame contains an integer number of MCLK pulses. If the NODIV bit is set to 1, the (FRL+1) field can take
```
any value from 8 to 256.
Slave mode
The audio frame length is primarily used to specify the number of bit clock cycles for each audio frame
transmitted from the external master module to the slave module. It is mainly employed to detect frame
synchronization signals that occur ahead of schedule or behind schedule during audio frame transmission from the
master module. Errors occur in such cases.
In slave mode, the configuration of the FRL[7:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xFRCR register is unrestricted.
36.3.4.3 Frame Synchronization Polarity
Set the effective polarity of the FS pin through the FSPOL bit in R32_SAI_xFRCR register, and start the frame
through this polarity. SOF signal is sensitive to edge.
In the slave mode, the audio module is in a waiting state until a valid frame signal is received to perform the
sending or receiving operation, and the SOF signal is synchronized with the frame signal. The frame
synchronization polarity is valid only when the SOF signal is not detected during communication and the SOF
signal is consistent with the expected SOF signal.
In the main mode, every time an audio frame is completed, a frame synchronization signal is sent until the SAIEN
bit in the R32_SAI_xCTLR1 register is cleared. If there is no data in the FIFO at the end of the previous audio
frame, the underflow will be handled as described in section 36.3.12.1, but the audio communication flow will not
be interrupted.
36.3.4.4 Frame Synchronization Effective Level Length
The FSALL[6:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xFRCR register configure the length of the active level for the frame sync
signal. This length can be set to between 1 and 128 bit clock cycles.
```
In I2S, LSB, or MSB alignment modes, the active length is set to half the frame length; in PCM/DSP or TDM
```
modes, the active length is set to 1 bit.
36.3.4.5 Frame Synchronization Offset
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 776
```
According to the audio protocols supported in the application (such as I2S standard protocol and MSB alignment
```
```
protocol), setting the audio frame synchronization offset can make the frame synchronization signal valid when
```
the last bit or the first bit is transmitted. You can select one of two configurations by using the FSOFF bit in the
R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
36.3.4.6 Function of FS Signal
The meaning of FS signal varies with the function of FS, and the meaning of FS signal can be configured in the
FSDEF bit of R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
- When the FSDEF bit is set to 1, the FS signal simultaneously carries both the SOF signal and channel
identification signal within the frame, suitable for audio frame structures such as I2S, MSB-aligned, or
```
LSB-aligned protocols;
```
- When the FSDEF bit is set to 0, the FS signal functions as the SOF signal, suitable for PCM/DSP, TDM, AC'97,
and audio protocols.
When interpreting the FS signal as the SOF signal and channel identification signal within a frame, the declared
number of slots should be evenly distributed between the left and right channels. If the number of bit clock cycles
on a half audio frame exceeds the dedicated slot count for a channel and the TRIS bit is set to 0, the remaining bit
clock cycles in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register will output 0. Conversely, if the TRIS bit is set to 1, the SD line
will enter a high-impedance state. During reception, the remaining bit clock cycles are only considered when a
channel change occurs.

36.3.5 Slot Configuration
The basic unit of an audio frame is a Slot, with each audio frame capable of being divided into up to 16 Slots. The
number of Slots within an audio frame is determined by NBSLOT[3:0]+1.
```
For AC'97 or SPDIF protocols (when PRTCFG[1:0] bits are set to 10b or 01b), the number of Slots is
```
automatically configured according to the respective protocol specifications, and the value of NBSLOT[3:0] is
ignored.
By setting the SLOTEN[15:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register, individual slots can be enabled or disabled.
When transmitting an invalid slot, the SD data line is forcibly set to 0 or placed in a high-impedance state,
```
depending on the configuration of the TRIS bit in transmit mode (see the section on invalid slot output data line
```
```
management for details). In receive mode, data received after the end of this invalid slot is ignored. Consequently,
```
there are no FIFO accesses, nor any FIFO read/write requests associated with the state of this invalid slot.
Additionally, the slot size can be selected by setting bits SLOTSZ[1:0] in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register to 1, as
shown in Figure 36-6.

36.3.6 Internal FIFO
Each SAI audio submodule contains an independent 8-word-wide synchronous FIFO to enhance transmission
efficiency. These FIFOs can be accessed by either the CPU or DMA, with FIFO request interrupts used to request
CPU and DMA access.
Depending on whether the audio module is defined as a transmitter or receiver, corresponding reads or writes to
the FIFO are executed. Regardless of the access size, each read or write operation to the FIFO operates on a single
word-sized FIFO cell. Each FIFO word contains one audio slot. Following each access to the R32_SAI_xDATAR
register, the FIFO pointer increments by one word. Consequently, only one FIFO request is associated with the
```
FREQ bit (FIFO request flag) in the R32_SAI_xSR register.
```
When the FREQIE bit in the R32_SAI_xINTENR register is enabled, an interrupt will be generated. The
triggering conditions for this interrupt depend on the operating mode, FIFO threshold, FIFO status, and DMA
burst transfer size.
The specific interrupt triggering mechanism is detailed in Table 36-2 and the subsequent sections 'Generating
Interrupts in Transmit Mode' and 'Generating Interrupts in Receive Mode'.

36.3.7 AC'97 Link Controller
SAI can function as an AC'97 link controller. This mode is configured via the PRTCFG[1:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. When this protocol is selected, numerous configuration fields are ignored.
Consequently, the number of slots and slot size are fixed, and the frame synchronization signal must be fully
defined with a fixed waveform. Failure to meet these requirements will prevent SAI from operating correctly.
```
The NBSLOT[3:0] bits and SLOTSZ[1:0] bits will be ignored;
```
- The number of slots is fixed at 13. The first slot is 16 bits wide, while all other slots are 20 bits wide (data slots);
- The FBOFF[4:0] bits in the SAI_xSLOTR register are ignored;
- The SAI_xFRCR register is ignored;
- MCLK is not used.
Regardless of whether the master or slave configuration is adopted, since the AC'97 link controller drives the FS
signal, the FS signal generated by the asynchronous module will be automatically configured as an output.

```
Note: In the AC'97 protocol, bit 2 of the TAG is reserved (always set to 0). Therefore, regardless of the value
```

One SAI can be used for AC'97 point-to-point communication, as shown in Figure 36-9. In SAI, audio module A
must be declared as an asynchronous master transmitter, while audio module B must be defined as a slave receiver
and synchronized with audio module A internally.

36.3.8 SPDIF Output
```
SPDIF (Sony/Philips Digital Interface) is a digital audio interconnect for consumer audio equipment, designed to
```
transmit audio over reasonably short distances. The SPDIF interface is available only in transmit mode and
supports the IEC 60958 standard. SPDIF mode can be selected by setting the PRTCFG[1:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to 01b.
For the SPDIF protocol:
```
1) Enable only the SD data line;
```
```
2) Release the FS, SCK, and MCLK I/O pins;
```
```
3) To enable the SAI clock generator and manage the data rate on the SD line, force the MODE[1] bit to 0 to
```
```
select master mode;
```
```
4) Force the data size to 24 bits. Values set in DS[2:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register are ignored;
```
```
5) The clock generator must be configured to define the symbol rate, where the known-bit clock should be twice
```
```
the symbol rate. Data is encoded using the Manchester protocol;
```
```
6) Ignore the SAI_xFRCR and SAI_xSLOTR registers. Internally configure the SAI to comply with SPDIF
```
protocol requirements, as shown in Figure 36-0.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 783

In SPDIF mode, underflow is the only error flag used in R32_SAI_xSR register. Since SAI can only work in the
send mode, to recover from the underflow error detected by the underflow interrupt or underflow status bit, the
following steps should be performed in sequence:
```
1) If DMA is already in use, disable the DMA stream via the DMA peripheral.
```
```
2) Disable SAI operation and verify physical disablement by polling the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1
```

```
3) Clear the flag by writing a 1 to the OVRUDR bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register.
```
```
4) Flush the FIFO by setting the FFLUSH bit to 1 in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register. The software must point to
```
```
the subsequent data address corresponding to the start of the new data block (data in header B). If DMA is in use,
```
update the DMA source start address pointer accordingly.
```
5) Re-enable the DMA stream if the DMA controller resumes data transfer based on the new source start address
```
pointer.
```
6) Re-enable the SAI by setting the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to 1.
```
