36.3.9 Stereo/Mono
```
In transmit mode, if the number of slots equals 2 (with the NBSLOT[3:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register
```
```
set to 0001b), mono mode can be addressed without any data preprocessing in memory. In this case, since the data
```
from Slot 0 is copied to data Slot 1 during transmission, the FIFO access time is reduced by half.
To enable mono mode, the following steps are required:
```
1) Set the MONO bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to 1;
```
```
2) Set the NBSLOT bit in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register to 1 and configure the SLOTEN bit to 3.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 785
```
In receive mode, the MONO bit setting to 1 is only meaningful when the Slot count equals 2 (same as in transmit
```
```
mode). When this bit is set to 1, only data from Slot 0 will be stored in the FIFO. Data from Slot 1 is discarded as
```
it is considered identical to the previous slot's data. If the data stream in receive mode is a true stereo audio stream
where the left and right channel data are distinctly different, the MONO bit is irrelevant. The conversion from the
output stereo file to an equivalent mono file is handled by software.
36.3.10 Mute Mode
When the audio sub-module is used as a transmitter or receiver, the mute mode can be used.
Audio sub-module in transmission mode
In transmit mode, mute mode can be selected at any time. Mute mode is effective for all audio frames. During
frame transmission, mute mode can be enabled by setting the MUTE bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register to 1.
This mute mode bit is latched only at the end of a frame. If the MUTE bit is set to 1 at the end of a frame, mute
mode activates at the start of the next audio frame and persists throughout its entire duration until the next frame
ends. The bit is then latched to determine whether the subsequent frame remains a mute frame.
If the number of slots set via the NBSLOT[3:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register is less than or equal to 2,
you can specify whether the value sent in mute mode is 0 or the last value for each slot. This is selected via the
MUTEVAL bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register.
If the number of slots set in the NBSLOT[3:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register exceeds 2, the MUTEVAL
bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register becomes meaningless since a value of 0 is sent on every bit of each slot.
In mute mode, the FIFO pointer continues to increment. This means that data requested for transmission in the
FIFO during mute mode will be discarded.
Audio sub-module in receiving mode
```
In receive mode, for a given number of consecutive audio frames (R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register MUTECNT[5:0]
```
```
bits), if zero is received in all declared active slots of the audio frame, a mute pattern from an external transmitter
```
is detected. Upon detecting the corresponding number of mute frames, the MUTEDET flag in the R32_SAI_xSR
register is set to 1 and triggers an interrupt if the MUTEDETIE bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register is set to 1.
The mute frame counter is reset when the audio submodule is disabled or when at least one data frame is received
within a valid slot. An interrupt is generated only once when the counter reaches the value specified in the
MUTECNT[5:0] bits. Subsequent interrupt events are reinitialized when the counter is reset.
```
Note: Mute mode is not available for SPDIF audio module.
```
36.3.11 Compressed Expansion Mode
In the field of mobile communications, pre-processing of data for transmission often involves the application of
data compression and decompression algorithms.
```
The application can select whether to process data before transmission on the SD serial output line (compression)
```
```
and whether to decompress data after reception on the SD serial input line (expansion) based on the COMP[1:0]
```
```
bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register (used only when TDM mode is selected), as shown in Figure 36-11. The
```
two supported compression/decompression modes are μ-Law and A-Law, both of which are standards
recommended by CCITT G.711.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 786
```
The μ-Law standard, adopted in the United States and Japan, permits a 14-bit dynamic range (R32_SAI_xCFGR2
```
```
register COMP[1:0] bits set to 10b). The European A-Law standard supports a 13-bit dynamic range
```
```
(R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register COMP[1:0] bits set to 11b).
```
Regarding the calculation method for μ-Law or A-Law compression/expansion standards, based on the setting of
the CPL bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register, either 1's complement or 2's complement may be used for
computation.
```
In both μ-Law and A-Law standards, data is encoded in an 8-bit format aligned to the most significant bit (MSB),
```
and the width of data after compression/expansion processing remains consistently 8 bits.
```
Therefore, when the SAI audio module is enabled (R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register SAIEN bit set to 1) and either of
```
these two compression/expansion modes is selected via the COMP[1:0] bits, the DS[2:0] bits of the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register are forced to 010b. If no compression/expansion processing is required, the
COMP[1:0] bits should remain cleared.
Specifically, if the SAI audio module is configured as a transmitter and the COMP[1] bit in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register is set to 1, the compression mode is employed. If the SAI audio module is declared as
a receiver, the expansion algorithm is used.

Output data line management on invalid Slot
In the transmission mode, when an invalid Slot is transmitted on the data line, the behavior of SD line output can
be controlled by TRIS bit.
- When an invalid slot is transmitted, the SAI forces the SD output line to 0.
- After the last data bit is transmitted, the SD output line is placed in a high-impedance state to release the data
line for use by other transmitters connected to this node.
2 transmitters must not simultaneously drive the same SD output pin to prevent short-circuit conditions. To ensure
a gap exists during transmission, if the data is less than 32 bits, set the SLOTSZ[1:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xSLOTR register to 10b to expand the data to 32 bits. Subsequently, if the next slot is declared invalid,
```
the SD output pin will be tri-stated at the end of the LSD of the valid slot (during the zero-padding phase to extend
```
```
data to 32 bits).
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 787
Additionally, if the product of the number of slots and the slot size is less than the frame length, the SD output line
will be tri-stated when supplementing the audio frame end with zero-padding.
Figure 36-13 illustrates these behaviors.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com

36.3.12 Error Flag
SAI uses the following error flags:
- FIFO overflow/underflow;
- Frame sync advance detection;
- Frame sync delay detection;
- Codec not ready (AC'97 only);
- Master mode clock configuration error.
```
36.3.12.1 FIFO Overflow/Underflow (OVRUDR)
```
The FIFO overflow/underflow bit is the OVRUDR bit in R32_SAI_xSR register.
Since audio modules can be used as both receivers and transmitters, and each audio module in the specified SAI
has its own R32_SAI_xSR register, overflow or underflow errors share the same bit.
Overflow
If the audio module is configured as a receiver, an overflow occurs when audio frame data is received while the
FIFO is full and cannot store any more received data. In this case, the received data is lost, and the OVRUDR flag
in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1. If the OVRUDRIE bit in the R32_SAI_xINTENR register is set to 1, an
interrupt is also generated. The internal system records the slot number at the time of overflow. The FIFO cannot
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 790
store additional data until space is freed to accommodate new data. Once the FIFO has freed space for at least one
data item, the SAI audio module receiver begins receiving new data from the new audio frame starting from the
slot number internally recorded after the overflow detection. This prevents data slot misalignment in the target
memory. Refer to Figure 36-15 for details.
To clear the OVRUDR flag, set the OVRUDR bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register to 1.
Figure 36-15 Overflow error detection

Underflow
When the audio module in SAI is used as a transmitter, if the FIFO is empty when data needs to be sent,
underflow may occur. If underflow is detected, the Slot number of the event will be stored and the MUTE value
```
(00b) will be sent until the FIFO is ready to send the data corresponding to the Slot where underflow is detected.
```
See Figure 36-16 for details. This can avoid synchronization failure between memory pointer and Slot in audio
frame.
The underflow event will set the OVRUDR flag in the R32_SAI_xSR register to 1, and if the OVRUDRIE bit in
the R32_SAI_ xINTENR register is set to 1, an interrupt will be generated. To clear this flag, just write 1 to bit
OVRUDR in R32_SAI_xSR register.
When the audio submodule is configured as master mode or slave mode, an underflow event will occur.

```
36.3.12.2 Frame Synchronization Advance Detection (AFSDET)
```
AFSDET flag is only used when SAI audio module is used as slave mode, and it will be disabled in master mode.
In R32_SAI_xFRCR register, the frame length, frame polarity and frame offset configuration are all known, and
```
this flag is used to indicate whether the frame synchronization (FS) signal is detected earlier than expected. When
```
the frame detection advance occurs, the AFSDET flag in R32_SAI_xSR register will be set.
For the current audio frame which is insensitive to FS advance, the secondary detection will not affect it. In other
words, the "parasitic" event of the FS signal will be marked, but it will not interfere with the processing of the
current audio frame.
If the AFSDETIE bit in the R32_SAI_xINTENR register is set to 1, an interrupt will be generated. Clearing the
AFSDET flag requires writing a 1 to this bit.
To resynchronize with the main module after a Frame Sense Detect Early error occurs, the following steps must be
```
followed:
```
```
1) Disable the SAI module by resetting the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. To ensure SAI is
```
disabled, read back the SAIEN bit and verify its value is set to 0.
```
2) Flush the FIFO by setting the FFLUSH bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register to 1.
```
```
3) Re-enable the SAI peripheral by setting the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to 1.
```
```
4) The SAI module will wait for the FS enable signal to restart synchronization with the main module.
```
```
Note: The SAIEN flag is not enabled in AC'97 mode because the SAI audio module, acting as a link controller,
```
generates the FS signal even when declared as a slave module. Since the AC'97 protocol does not utilize the FS
signal, this feature serves no practical purpose in SPDIF mode.
```
36.3.12.3 Frame Synchronization Lag Detection (LFSDET)
```
```
The LFSDET flag is only used when the SAI audio module operates as a slave module; it is disabled in master
```
mode. In the R32_SAI_xFRCR register, the frame length, frame polarity, and frame offset configurations are
known. If the external master module fails to send the FS signal within the scheduled time or generates the FS
signal too late, the LFSDET flag will be set to 1. An interrupt will also be generated if the LFSDETIE bit in the
R32_SAI_xINTENR register is set to 1. Writing a value of 1 to the LFSDET bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register
clears the LFSDET flag.
The Frame Synchronization Lag Detection flag is set to 1 when the corresponding error is detected, indicating that
the SAI requires resynchronization with the master module. Refer to Section 36.3.12.2: Frame Synchronization
```
Advance Detection (AFSDET) for the specific sequence described.
```
In noisy environments, the audio module's state machine may incorrectly detect interference on the SCK clock
and shift SAI data to an erroneous frame position. The SAI detects this event and reports it as a frame
synchronization delay detection error.
Frame corruption does not occur if the external master module manages audio data frame transmission in
continuous mode, which is the case for most applications. If this situation occurs, the LFSDET flag will be set to
1.
```
Note: The LFSDET flag is not enabled in AC'97 mode because the SAI audio module, acting as a link controller,
```
generates the FS signal even when declared as a slave module. Since the AC'97 protocol does not utilize the FS
signal, this functionality is not relevant in SPDIF mode.
```
36.3.12.4 Codec Not Ready (CNRDY AC'97)
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 792
```
When the SAI audio module is configured to operate in AC'97 mode (i.e., when the PRTCFG[1:0] bits in the
```
```
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register are set to 10b), the CNRDY flag in the R32_SAI_xSR register becomes meaningful.
```
If the CNRDYIE bit in the R32_SAI_xINTENR register is set to 1, an interrupt will be generated when the
CNRDY flag is set to 1.
```
During reception of the TAG0 (slot0) AC'97 audio frame, if the codec is not yet ready for communication, the
```
CNRDY flag will be set to 1. In this case, data will not be automatically stored into the FIFO until TAG0 indicates
the codec is ready, because the codec is not yet prepared. Once the codec is ready, all valid slots defined in the
R32_SAI_xSLOTR register will be captured.
To clear the CNRDY flag, the CNRDY bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register must be written to 1.
```
Master mode clock configuration error (NODIV=0)
```
```
When the audio module works in the main mode (MODE[1:0]=0x) and the NODIV position is 0, if the following
```
conditions are met, the WCKCFG flag will be set to 1 as long as SAI is enabled:
- (FRL+1) is not a power of 2;
- (FRL+1) is not between 8 and 256.
The MODE bit, the NODIV bit and the SAIEN bit belong to the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register, and the FRL bit
belongs to the R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
If the WCKCFGIE bit is set, an interrupt will be generated when the WCKCFG flag in the R32_SAI_xSR register
is set. To clear this flag, write a 1 to bit WCKCFG in R32_SAI_xSR register.
When WCKCFG is set to 1, the audio module is automatically disabled, so the SAIEN bit will be hardware
cleared.
36.3.13 DMA Interface
To reduce CPU load and optimize bus bandwidth, each SAI audio module features an independent DMA interface
```
for read/write operations on the R32_SAI_xDATAR register (accessing the internal FIFO). Each audio submodule
```
is equipped with a DMA channel supporting the basic DMA request/response protocol.
When configuring DMA transfers to serve the audio submodule, set bit 1 of the DMAEN field in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. DMA requests are directly managed by the FIFO controller, and their generation
depends on the FIFO threshold. When the audio submodule is configured in transmit mode, the FIFO threshold
must be set to a specific value to ensure sufficient remaining space for a complete DMA burst write operation
under worst-case conditions. Failure to do so may result in a FIFO overflow error. When the audio submodule is
configured in receive mode, the FIFO threshold must be set to a specific value to ensure sufficient data in the
FIFO for a complete DMA burst read operation, thereby preventing FIFO underflow errors.
The DMA transfer direction is related to the configuration of the SAI audio submodule:
- If the audio module functions as a transmitter, the audio module's FIFO controller will issue DMA requests to
load data written into the SAI_xDATAR register into the FIFO.
- If the audio module functions as a receiver, DMA requests are associated with read operations from the
R32_SAI_xDATAR register.
Configure the SAI interface for DMA mode in the following sequence:
```
1) Configure the SAI and FIFO thresholds to specify when to initiate DMA requests.
```
```
2) Configure the SAI DMA channel.
```
```
3) Enable DMA.
```
```
4) Enable the SAI interface.
```
```
Note: Before configuring the SAI module, the SAI DMA channel must be disabled.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 793

```
Chapter 37 QSPI Interface (QuadSPI)
```
This chapter's module description applies only to the CH32H417, CH32H416 microcontroller product.
```
The chip incorporates 2 dedicated QSPI communication interfaces (QuadSPI) for connecting to single-, dual-, or
```
```
quad-wire (data-line) SPI flash storage media. The interface primarily supports the following operating modes:
```
 Indirect Mode: In this mode, the QSPI interface performs all operations through the QSPI register. This mode
is suitable for applications requiring frequent read/write operations.
 Status Polling Mode: In this mode, the system periodically reads the external FLASH status register. When
```
the flag is set to 1 (e.g., erase or program complete), the system generates an interrupt. This mode is suitable
```
for applications requiring real-time monitoring of the external Flash status.
Memory-mapped mode: In this mode, the external Flash is mapped into the microcontroller's address space,
allowing the system to access it as internal memory. For chips where the fifth-to-last digit of the lot number is less
than 3, the memory-mapped address may only be used for data access.
Dual-Flash Mode: When operating in dual-Flash mode, the system can simultaneously access 2 Quad-SPI FLASH
devices, doubling both throughput and capacity. This mode is suitable for applications requiring extensive data
processing.
37.1 Main Features
 3 functional modes: Indirect mode, Status polling mode, and Memory-mapped mode
 Dual flash mode via parallel access to two FLASH devices
 Integrated FIFOs for transmission and reception
 Supports SDR mode
 Fully programmable frame format for indirect and memory-mapped modes
 Fully programmable opcode for indirect and memory-mapped modes
 Generates DMA trigger signals upon reaching FIFO threshold and transmission completion
 Generates interrupts upon reaching FIFO threshold, timeout, operation completion, and access errors
37.2 Overview

37.3 Function Description
37.3.1 QSPI Command Sequence
QSPI communicates with FLASH through commands, and each command includes five stages: instruction,
address, alternate byte, null instruction and data. Any phase can be skipped, but at least one of instruction, address,
alternate byte or data phase should be reserved. NCS drops before each instruction starts and rises again after each
instruction is completed.
Figure 37-3 Example of read command in 4-wire mode
7SIO0

I/O switch from output to input
Instruction Phase
During the instruction phase, an 8-bit instruction configured in the INSTRUCTION[7:0] field of the
R32_QSPIx_CCR register is sent to the FLASH to specify the type of operation to be executed. Most FLASH
```
devices can only receive instructions one bit at a time via the SIO0 signal (single-wire SPI mode). However, by
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 806
configuring the IMODE[1:0] field in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register, selective transmission during the instruction
```
phase can be enabled. This allows sending 2 bits at a time (via SIO0/SIO1 in dual-wire SPI mode) or 4 bits at a
```
```
time (via SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3 in quad-wire SPI mode). If IMODE = 00b, the instruction phase is skipped, and
```
```
the command sequence begins with the address phase (if present).
```
Address Phase
During the address phase, 1 to 4 bytes may be sent to the FLASH to indicate the operation address. The number of
address bytes to be sent is configured in the ADSIZE[1:0] field of the R32_QSPIx_CCR register. In Indirect Mode
and Auto Polling Mode, the address bytes to be sent are specified in the ADDRESS[31:0] field of the
R32_QSPIx_AR register. In Memory-Mapped Mode, the address is provided directly by the system.
```
The address phase can be configured to transmit 1 bit (via SIO0 in single-wire SPI mode), 2 bits (via SIO0/SIO1
```
```
in dual-wire SPI mode), or 4 bits (via SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3 in quad-wire SPI mode) by setting the
```
ADMODE[1:0] field in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register. If ADMODE = 00b, the address phase is skipped, and the
```
command sequence proceeds directly to the next phase (if present).
```
Alternate Byte Phase
During the alternate byte phase, 1-4 bytes of data are sent to the FLASH, typically used to control operating
modes. The number of alternate bytes to be sent is configured in the ABSIZE[1:0] field of the R32_QSPIx_CCR
register. The specification of the bytes to be sent is completed in the R32_QSPIx_ABR register.
Configured via the ABMODE[1:0] field in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register, the Alternate Byte Phase can transmit 1
```
bit at a time (via SIO0 in single-wire SPI mode), 2 bits at a time (via SIO0/SIO1 in dual-wire SPI mode), or 4 bits
```
```
at a time (via SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3 in quad-wire SPI mode). If ABMODE=00b, the alternate byte phase is
```
```
skipped, and the command sequence proceeds directly to the next phase (if present).
```
During the alternate byte phase, it is sometimes sufficient to transmit a single half-byte rather than a full byte. For
```
example: When transmitting alternate bytes using only 2 cycles in dual-wire mode. In this case, the firmware can
```
```
adopt four-wire mode (ABMODE=11b) and transmit a byte by setting bits [7] and [3] of ALTERNATE to 1 (SIO3
```
```
remains high) and bits [6] and [2] to 0 (SIO2 line remains low). The upper 2 bits of the half-byte are stored in bits
```
```
[4:3] of ALTERNATE, while the lower 2 bits reside in bits [1] and [0]. For instance, if half-byte 2 (0010) is
```
```
transmitted via SIO0/SIO1, ALTERNATE should be set to 0x8A (1000_1010).
```
Null Instruction Cycle Phase
During the null instruction cycle phase, when operating at higher clock frequencies, no data transmission or
reception occurs within a specified 1-31 cycle window to ensure sufficient time for the FLASH to prepare data.
The number of cycles in this phase is defined by the DCYC[4:0] field in the R32_QSPIx_CCR[22:18] register.
In SDR mode, the duration is defined by a fixed number of full clock cycles. If DCYC is 0, the empty instruction
```
cycle phase is skipped, and the command sequence proceeds directly to the data phase (if present).
```
The operating mode during the empty instruction cycle phase is fixed to single-wire mode.
Data Phase
During the data phase, any number of bytes can be received from or transmitted to the FLASH. In indirect mode
and automatic polling mode, the number of bytes to be received/transmitted is specified in the R32_QSPIx_DLR
register. In indirect write mode, data to be sent to the FLASH is written into the R32_QSPIx_DR register. In
indirect read mode, data received from the FLASH is obtained by reading the R32_QSPIx_DR register.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 807
In memory-mapped mode, read data is returned directly to the system.
By configuring the ABMODE[1:0] field in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register, the data phase can transmit/receive 1
```
bit at a time (via SIO0 in single-wire SPI mode), 2 bits at a time (via SIO0/SIO1 in dual-wire SPI mode), or 4 bits
```
```
at a time (via SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3 in quad-wire SPI mode). If DMODE = 00b, the data phase is skipped, and
```
the command sequence completes immediately upon pulling nCS high. This configuration applies only to indirect
write mode.
37.3.2 QSPI Signal Interface Protocol Mode
Single-wire SPI mode
Traditional SPI mode permits serial transmission/reception of individual 1-bit data. In this mode, data is sent to
the FLASH via SIO0. Data received from the FLASH is delivered via SIO1.
To utilize this single-bit mode, configure different command phases by setting the
IMODE/ADMODE/ABMODE/DMODE field in R32_QSPIx_CCR to 01b.
Within each phase configured for single-wire mode:
 SIO0 is in output mode
```
 SIO1 is in input mode (high impedance)
```
```
 SIO2 is in output mode and forced to 0 (to disable the “write protection” function)
```
```
 SIO3 is in output mode and forced to 1 (to disable the “hold” function)
```
If DMODE=01b, this also applies to the empty instruction phase as described above.
Dual-Wire SPI Mode
In dual-wire mode, 2 bits are transmitted/received simultaneously via the SIO0/SIO1 signals. By configuring the
IMODE/ADMODE/ABMODE/DMODE field of the R32_QSPIx_CCR register to 10b, different command phases
can be set accordingly.
In each phase configured for dual-wire mode:
```
 SIO0/SIO1 are in high-impedance state (input) during data phase read operations and in output mode
```
otherwise.
 SIO2 is in output mode and forced to 0.
 SIO3 is in output mode and forced to 1.
During the empty instruction phase, if DMODE=01b, SIO0/SIO1 remain in high-impedance state at all times.
Quad-wire SPI Mode
In quad-wire mode, four bits of data are transmitted/received simultaneously via the SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3
signals. Configuring the IMODE/ADMODE/ABMODE/DMODE fields in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register to 11b
enables corresponding settings for different command phases.
In each phase configured for quad-wire mode:
```
 SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3 are in high-impedance state (input) during the data phase of read operations and
```
```
function as outputs in other cases.
```
 SIO2 and SIO3 are used exclusively for QSPI mode. If no phase is configured for quad-wire SPI mode, the
corresponding SIO2 and SIO3 pins can be used for other functions even when QSPI is active.
During the empty command phase, if DMODE=11, SIO0/SIO1/SIO2/SIO3 are all in high-impedance state.
SDR Mode
```
QSPI operates in Single Data Rate (SDR) mode.
```
In SDR mode, when QSPI drives the SIO0, SIO1, SIO2, and SIO3 signals, these signals transition only on the
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 808
falling edge of SCK.
When receiving data in SDR mode, the QSPI assumes the FLASH transmits data on the falling edge of SCK and
```
samples the signal on the subsequent edge (rising edge) of SCK.
```
Dual Flash Mode
```
When the DFM bit (R32_QSPIx_CR[6]) is set to 1, QSPI enters dual flash mode. The QSPI utilizes 2 external
```
```
four-wire SPIFLASHes (FLASH1 and FLASH2), transmitting/receiving 8 bits of data per cycle, effectively
```
doubling throughput and capacity. Each FLASH uses the same SCK signal and may optionally share the same
nCS signal, but their SIO0, SIO1, SIO2, and SIO3 signals are independent.
Dual Flash mode can be combined with Single-bit mode, Dual-bit mode, Quad-bit mode, and SDR mode.
```
Specify the FLASH size in FSIZE[4:0] (R32_QSPIx_DCR[20:16]). The specified parameter should reflect the
```
total FLASH capacity, i.e., twice the capacity of a single component. When address X is even, the byte assigned
by QSPI to address X is the byte stored at address X/2 in FLASH1. The byte assigned by QSPI to address X+1 is
the byte stored at address X/2 in FLASH2. That is, bytes at even addresses are stored in FLASH1, while bytes at
odd addresses are stored in FLASH2.
In dual-flash mode, the number of bytes required to read the FLASH status register is twice that of single-flash
mode. Specifically, since each FLASH provides 8 valid bits after executing the status register read instruction,
```
QSPI must be configured for a data length of 2 bytes (16 bits), with QSPI receiving 1 byte from each FLASH. If
```
each FLASH provides a 16-bit status, the QSPI must be configured to read 4 bytes to capture all status bits from
both FLASHes in dual-flash mode. Consequently, the least significant byte in the data register is the least
significant byte of FLASH1's status register, while the next byte is the least significant byte of FLASH2's status
register. The third byte in the data register is the second byte of FLASH1, and the fourth byte is the second byte of
```
FLASH2 (when the FLASH has a 16-bit status register).
```
In dual flash mode, accesses must always be to an even number of bytes. Therefore, when DRM=1, bit 0 of the
```
data length field (R32_QSPIx_DLR[0]) is always maintained as 1.
```
In dual flash mode, the behavior of the FLASH1 interface signals is essentially identical to that in normal mode.
During instruction, address, alternate byte, and empty instruction cycle phases, the waveforms of the FLASH2
interface signals are identical to those of the FLASH1 interface signals. That is, each FLASH always receives the
same instruction and address. Subsequently, during the data phase, the SIOx and SIOXx buses transmit data in
```
parallel, but the data sent to (or received from) FLASH1 differs from that in FLASH2.
```
37.3.3 QSPI Indirect Mode
```
In indirect mode, the command is triggered by writing to the QSPI register; Data is transmitted by reading and
```
writing data registers in the same way as other communication peripherals.
```
When FMODE=00b (R32_QSPIx_CCR[27:26]), the QSPI operates in indirect write mode, transmitting bytes to
```
```
the FLASH during the data phase. Data is provided by writing to the data register (R32_QSPIx_DR). When
```
```
FMODE=01b, QSPI operates in indirect read mode, receiving bytes from FLASH during the data phase. Data is
```
```
acquired by reading from the data register (R32_QSPIx_DR).
```
```
Specify the number of bytes to read/write in the Data Length Register (R32_QSPIx_DLR). If R32_QSPIx_DLR =
```
```
0xFFFF_FFFF (all bits set to 1), the data length is considered undefined, and QSPI will continue transferring data
```
```
until reaching the end of the FLASH (as defined by FSIZE). If no bytes are transferred, the DMODE bit in the
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 809
```
R32_QSPIx_CCR register is set to 00b. If R32_QSPIx_DLR = 0xFFFF_FFFF and FSIZE = 0x1F (data length of
```
```
4G bytes), during J-mode flash access, the configuration must ensure flash address + DLR ≤ FSIZE. In this case,
```
the transfer will continue indefinitely, stopping only when QSPI is disabled or a terminate request occurs. After
```
reading the last memory address (address 0xFFFF_FFFF), reading will resume starting from address
```
0x0000_0000.
When the programmed number of bytes to transmit or receive is reached, if TCIE=1, TCF is set to 1 and an
interrupt is generated. When the data quantity is uncertain, the system will also set TCF to 1 when the external SPI
limit is reached, based on the FLASH size defined in the R32_QSPIx_CR register.
QSPI supports write flow control. This means that when the length filled in the DLR has not been fully
transmitted and the FIFO is empty, the shift register transmission is paused. In this mode, for efficiency, the
software should first write to the DR register to fill data into the FIFO, or set DMAEN to 1 to automatically
request a certain amount of data from the DMA before writing the START bit to initiate transmission.
Trigger Command Start
Essentially, once the firmware provides the last information required by the command, the command will start.
According to the configuration of QSPI, in indirect mode, there are three ways to trigger the command to start:
```
1) Perform a write operation to the INSTRUCTION[7:0] field of the R32_QSPIx_CCR register. This is required
```
```
when ADMODE=00b (address is mandatory) and when no data is provided by the firmware (when FMODE=01b
```
```
or DMODE=00b);
```
```
2) Write to the ADDRESS[31:0] field of the R32_QSPIx_AR register if an address is required (when
```
```
ADMODE=00b) and no data is provided by the firmware (when FMODE=01b or DMODE=00b);
```
```
3) Write to the DATA[31:0] field of the R32_QSPIx_DR register if an address is required (when ADMODE ≠
```
```
00b) and data is provided by the firmware (when FMODE = 00b and DMODE ≠ 00b).
```
```
Writing to the Alternate Byte Register (R32_QSPIx_ABR) never triggers a command start. If alternate bytes are
```
required, they must be programmed in advance. Once a command starts, the BUSY bit in the R32_QSPIx_SR
register is automatically set to 1.
FIFO and Data Management
In indirect mode, data is transferred through the 32-byte FIFO internal to the QSPI. The FLEVEL[5:0] bits of the
R32_QSPIx_SR register indicate how many bytes are currently stored in the FIFO.
```
In indirect write mode (FMODE=00b), when the firmware writes data to the R32_QSPIx_DR register, the data is
```
appended to the FIFO. A word write adds 4 bytes to the FIFO, a half-word write adds 2 bytes, and a byte write
adds only 1 byte. If the firmware writes data to the FIFO exceeding the value indicated by DL[31:0], any excess
```
bytes are cleared from the FIFO upon completion of the write operation (when TCF is set to 1). Access to
```
bytes/half-words in the R32_QSPIx_DR register must be strictly confined to the least significant byte/half-word
of this 32-bit register.
```
FTHRES[4:0] defines the FIFO threshold. When the threshold is reached, the FTF (FIFO Threshold Flag) is set to
```
1. In indirect read mode, the FTF is set to 1 when the number of valid bytes read from the FIFO exceeds the
threshold. After reading the last byte from FLASH, if data remains in the FIFO, FTF will be set to 1 regardless of
the FTHRES setting. In indirect write mode, FTF is set to 1 when the number of empty bytes in the FIFO exceeds
the threshold. If FTIE=1, an interrupt is generated when FTF is set to 1. Once the threshold condition is no longer
met, that is, after the CPU or DMA has transmitted enough data, the HW will clear the FTF.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 810
In indirect mode, QSPI will pause byte reads from Flash when the FIFO is full to prevent overflow. Reading from
```
FLASH resumes only when four bytes in the FIFO are empty (FLEVEL ≤ 11). Therefore, if FTHRES ≥ 13, the
```
application must read a sufficient number of bytes to ensure QSPI can continue retrieving data from FLASH.
Conversely, whenever 11 < FLEVEL < FTHRES, the FTF flag will remain at 0.
37.3.4 QSPI Status Flag Polling Mode
```
In automatic polling mode, QSPI periodically starts commands to read a certain number of status bytes (up to 4).
```
By masking the received bytes, some status bits can be isolated. When the selected bit has a preset value, an
interrupt can be generated.
```
Access to FLASH starts in the same way as in indirect reading mode: if an address (AMODE=00b) is not needed,
```
access will start when R32_QSPIx_CCR is written. Conversely, if an address is required, the first access will start
when R32_QSPIx_AR is written. At this time, BUSY becomes high level and remains unchanged even during
periodic access.
In automatic polling mode, the contents of the R32_QSPIx_PSMAR register's MASK[31:0] bits are used to mask
data from the FLASH. If MASK[n]=0, bit n in the result is masked and ignored. If MASK[n]=1 and the content of
bit [n] matches the content of bit [n] in the R32_QSPIx_PSMAR register's MATCH[n] field, bit n is considered a
match.
```
If the Polling Match Mode bit (PMM, bit 23 of R32_QSPIx_CR) is 0, the “AND” match mode is activated. This
```
```
means the Status Match Flag (SMF) is set only when all unmasked bits match. If PMM=1, the “OR” match mode
```
is activated, meaning SMF is set to 1 if a match occurs on any unmasked bit. If SMIE=1, an interrupt is triggered
```
when SMF is set to 1. If the automatic polling mode is stopped (APMS=1), the operation halts and the BUSY bit
```
is cleared upon detecting a match. Otherwise, the BUSY bit remains set, and periodic accesses continue until an
```
abort occurs or QSPI is disabled (EN=0).
```
```
The data register (R32_QSPIx_DR) contains the most recently received status byte (FIFO disabled). The contents
```
of the data register are unaffected by the masking method used by the matching logic. The FTF status bit is set to
```
1 after a new status read completes; once data is read, FTF is cleared.
```
37.3.5 QSPI Memory Mapping Mode
When configured in memory-mapped mode, the external SPI device is treated as internal memory. If the QSPI
peripheral is not properly configured and enabled, the QSPI Flash memory area cannot be accessed. Even with
larger FLASH capacity, its address space is limited to a maximum of 256MB.
```
Note: For chips where the fifth-to-last digit of the lot number is less than 3, the memory-mapped addresses may
```
only be used for data access, not for instruction access.
Byte, half-word, and word access types are supported. The QSPI anticipates subsequent microcontroller accesses
and preloads bytes from later addresses. Subsequent accesses to contiguous addresses are accelerated because the
data has already been fetched.
By default, the QSPI never interrupts its pre-fetch operation. Even during extended periods without access to the
FLASH, it maintains the previous read operation, and nCS remains at a low level. However, when nCS stays low,
```
FLASH power consumption increases. Therefore, the application may activate the timeout counter (TCEN=1, bit
```
```
3 of R32_QSPIx_CR) . Consequently, after the FIFO is filled with prefetched data, nCS is released if no access
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 811
```
occurs within TIMEOUT[15:0] (R32_QSPIx_LPTR) cycles. Upon the first memory-mapped access, the BUSY
```
signal transitions high. Due to the prefetch operation, the BUSY signal remains high until a timeout occurs, an
abort is triggered, or the peripheral is disabled.
37.3.6 QSPI FLASH Configuration
```
The device configuration register (R32_QSPIx_DCR) is used to define the characteristic parameters of the
```
external SPI FLASH. The FSIZE[4:0] field determines the capacity of the external memory according to the
following formula:
Number of bytes in FLASH = 2[FSIZE+1]
FSIZE+1 represents the number of address bits required for FLASH addressing. In indirect mode, the maximum
```
FLASH capacity reaches 4GB (using 32-bit addressing), but the addressable space in memory-mapped mode is
```
limited to 256MB. If DFM=1, FSIZE denotes the combined capacity of 2 FLASH chips.
```
When QSPI executes two consecutive commands, it holds the chip select signal (nCS) high between commands
```
for a default duration of one SCK cycle. If the FLASH requires a longer interval between commands, the Chip
```
Select High Time (CSHT) field can be used to specify the minimum number of SCK cycles (maximum 8) that
```
```
nCS must remain high. The clock mode (CKMODE) bit indicates the logic level of the SCK signal between
```
```
commands (when nCS=1).
```
37.3.7 QSPI Configuration
QSPI configuration occurs in 2 stages: QSPI IP configuration and QSPI FLASH configuration. Once configured
and enabled, the QSPI can operate in one of three modes: Indirect Mode, Status Polling Mode, and
Memory-Mapped Mode.
QSPI IP Configuration: Configured via R32_QSPIx_CR. The user must configure the clock prescaler division
factor for incoming data and the sampling shift settings. The FIFO level for generating DMA triggers or interrupts
is programmed in the FTHRES bit. If a timeout counter is required, set the TCEN bit to 1 and program the timeout
value in the R32_QSPIx_LPTR register. Dual flash mode can be activated by setting DFM to 1.
QSPI FLASH Configuration: Configure parameters related to the external target FLASH via the
R32_QSPIx_DCR register. Users must program the FLASH size in the FSIZE bit, program the minimum hold
```
time for the chip select high level in the CSHT bit, and set the functional mode (Mode 0 or Mode 3) in the MODE
```
bit.
37.3.8 Usage of QSPI
Select the operation mode through R32_QSPIx_CCR register FMODE[1:0].
Indirect Mode
When FMODE=00b, the indirect write mode is selected, enabling data transmission to the FLASH. When
```
FMODE=01b, the indirect read mode is selected, allowing data retrieval from the FLASH.
```
When QSPI operates in indirect mode, frames are constructed as follows:
```
1) Specify the target address in the R32_QSPIx_AR register;
```
```
2) Specify the operating mode in the R32_QSPIx_CR register;
```
```
3) Specify the number of bytes to read or write in the R32_QSPIx_DLR register;
```
```
4) Specify the frame format, mode, and command code in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register;
```
```
5) Read data from/write data to the FIFO via the R32_QSPIx_DR register;
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 812
```
6) Specify optional alternate bytes to be sent immediately after the address phase in the R32_QSPIx_ABR
```
register.
```
When writing to the control register (R32_QSPIx_CR), the user can specify the following settings:
```
```
 Enable bit (EN) set to 1
```
```
 Timeout counter enable bit (TCEN)
```
```
 FIFO threshold (FTRHES), indicating when the FTF flag should be set to 1
```
 Interrupt enable
```
 Auto-polling mode parameters: Match mode and Stop mode (effective when FMODE=11b)
```
 Clock prescaler
```
When writing to the communication configuration register (R32_QSPIx_CCR), the user specifies the following
```
```
parameters:
```
 DCYC bit specifies the number of empty instruction bytes
 DBMODE bit specifies whether empty instruction bytes exist
 INSTRUCTION bit specifies the instruction byte
```
 Specify the number of alternate bytes (1/2/3/4) via the ABSIZE bit
```
```
 Specify the instruction transmission mode (1/2/4-wire) via the IMODE bit
```
```
 Specify the address length (8/16/24/32 bits) via the ADSIZE bit
```
```
 Specify the address transmission mode (none/1/2/4-wire) via the ADMODE bit
```
```
 Specify alternate byte transmission mode (None/1-wire/2-wire/4-wire) via the ABMODE bit
```
```
 Specify data transmission/reception mode (None/1-wire/2-wire/4-wire) via the DMODE bit
```
```
If no data register (R32_QSPIx_DR) or address register (R32_QSPIx_AR) needs updating for a command, the
```
command sequence initiates immediately upon writing the R32_QSPIx_CCR register. This occurs when both
```
ADMODE and DMODE are 00b, or when ADMODE=00b alone in indirect read mode (FMODE=01b). When an
```
```
address is required (ADMODE ≠ 00) and no data register write is needed (FMODE = 01b or DMODE = 00b), the
```
command sequence starts immediately upon updating the address via writing to the R32_QSPIx_AR register. In
```
data transfer scenarios (FMODE=00b and DMODE!=00b), writing to the FIFO via the R32_QSPIx_DR register
```
triggers communication initiation.
Status Flag Polling Mode
Enable Status Flag Polling Mode: Set the FMODE field in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register to 10b. In this mode,
programmed frames are sent and data is periodically retrieved. The maximum data read per frame is 4 bytes. If the
data requested in the R32_QSPIx_DLR register exceeds 4 bytes, the excess is ignored and only 4 bytes are read.
The periodicity is specified by the R32_QSPIx_PISR register.
After retrieving status data, it can be processed internally to achieve the following purposes:
 Automatically stops periodic status byte retrieval
 Sets the status match flag to 1 and generates an interrupt when enabled
The received value can be masked using the value stored in the R32_QSPIx_PSMKR register, and then ORed or
ANDed with the value stored in the R32_QSPIx_PSMAR register. If a match exists, the status match flag is set to
```
1 and an interrupt is generated if enabled; if AMPS is set to 1, the QSPI automatically stops. In all cases, the latest
```
read value is available in the R32_QSPIx_DR register.
Memory-Mapped Mode
In memory-mapped mode, the external FLASH is treated as internal memory despite access latency. Only read
operations to the external FLASH are supported in this mode. Memory-mapped mode can be activated by setting
FMODE to 11b in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register. When the host device accesses the memory-mapped space, it
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 813
transmits the configured frames and commands.
The FIFO functions as a prefetch buffer to support continuous linear read operations. In this mode, any access to
```
the R32_QSPIx_DR register returns zero. The data length register (R32_QSPIx_DLR) is invalid in
```
memory-mapped mode.
37.3.9 Instruction Sent Only Once
```
Certain FLASH devices (e.g., Winbound) support a mode where commands must be sent using only the first
```
command sequence, with subsequent commands executed directly based on the address. Users enable this feature
by setting the SIOO bit in the R32_QSPIx_CCR register.
The SIOO bit applies to all functional modes: Indirect Mode, Status Polling Mode, and Memory-Mapped Mode.
When SIOO is set to 1, only the first command is sent as an instruction, and a write operation is performed on the
R32_QSPIx_CCR register. Subsequent command sequences skip the instruction phase until the R32_QSPIx_CCR
```
register is written again. However, the SIOO bit is ineffective when IMODE=00b (no instruction).
```
37.3.10 QSPI Error Management
The possible error situations are:
 In indirect mode or status flag polling mode, if an incorrect address is set in the R32_QSPIx_AR register,
TEF will be set to 1 based on the FLASH size defined by FSIZE[4:0] in the R32_QSPIx_DCR register. If
enabled, an interrupt will also be generated.
 In indirect mode, if the sum of the address and data length exceeds the FLASH size, TEF will be set to 1
when the access is triggered.
37.3.11 Busy Bit and Abort Function of QSPI
When QSPI begins operating on the FLASH, the BUSY bit in the R32_QSPIx_SR register is automatically set to
1. In indirect mode, the BUSY bit is cleared when QSPI completes the requested command sequence and the
```
FIFO is empty; In automatic polling mode, the BUSY bit goes low only after the last periodic access completes,
```
either due to a match when APMS=1 or due to an abort operation. In memory-mapped mode, after the first access,
the BUSY bit goes low only upon a timeout event or an abort.
Any operation can be aborted by setting the ABORT bit to 1 in the R32_QSPIx_CR register. Upon completion of
the abort, the BUSY and ABORT bits automatically reset, and the FIFO is cleared.
```
Note: If the writing operation to the status register is stopped, some FLASH may have abnormal behavior.
```
37.3.12 NCS Behavior
By default, nCS is high, disabling external FLASH. nCS goes low before the operation begins and immediately
goes high after the operation completes.
```
When CKMODE=0 (“Mode 0”, where SCK remains low when no operation is in progress), nCS is pulled low one
```
SCK cycle before the first rising edge of SCK during an operation and pulled high one SCK cycle after the last
rising edge of SCK during an operation, as shown in the figure below.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 814
```

When CKMODE=1 ('Mode 3', where SCK rises to high level without any operation), nCS still falls to low level
```
one SCK cycle before the first rising edge of SCK during operation, and rises to high level one SCK cycle after
the last rising edge of SCK during operation, as shown in the figure below.

If the FIFO remains full in a read operation or empty in a write operation, the operation stops and SCK remains
low before the firmware intervenes in the FIFO. If the operation stops, the nCS will rise to the high level after
requesting the suspension, and the SCK will rise to the high level after half a cycle, as shown in the following
figure.
```

When not in Dual Flash Mode (DFM=0) and FSEL=0 (default), only FLASH1 is accessed. Therefore, if FSEL=1,
```
only FLASH1 is accessed, and nCS remains high. In Dual Flash Mode, the nCS behavior for both FLASH1 and
FLASH2 is identical. Consequently, if FLASH2 is present and the application always operates in Dual Flash
Mode, the nCS signal for FLASH1 can also be used for FLASH2, while the nCS pin output for FLASH2 can be
repurposed for other functions.

In indirect write mode, data written to this register is

too full, writing is paused until sufficient space
becomes available to accept the data to be written.
In indirect mode, reading this register retrieves data
```

```
If the number of bytes in the FIFO is less than the
number of bytes requested by the read operation and
```
BUSY=1, the read operation will pause until
```

sufficient data is available or the transfer completes
```
(whichever occurs first).
```
In automatic polling mode, this register contains the
```
last data read from FLASH (unmasked).
```
Word, half-word, and byte accesses are supported for
this register. In indirect write mode, a byte write
adds 1 byte to the FIFO, a half-word write adds 2
bytes, and a word write adds 4 bytes. Similarly, in
indirect read mode, a byte read erases one byte from
the FIFO, a half-word read erases two bytes, and a
word read erases four bytes.
Accesses in indirect mode must align with the least
significant bits of this register: byte reads must
access DATA[7:0], while half-word reads must
access DATA[15:0].

```
Chapter 38 Single-wire Protocol Main Interface (SWPMI)
```
```
The Single Wire Protocol Master Interface (SWPMI) is a full-duplex single-wire communication technology that
```
```
implements Single Wire Protocol (SWP) communication based on the ETSI TS 102 613 standard specification.
```
In SWPMI, data transmission occurs via two physical methods: First, data flows from the master device to the
```
slave device through the voltage domain (S1 signal). Second, data flows from the slave device to the master
```
```
device through the current domain (S2 signal). The S1 signal employs pulse width modulation (PWM) for digital
```
transmission, while the S2 signal conveys data through current variations.
38.1 Main Features
 Support full-duplex communication mode
 Support automatic processing of fill bits
 Support automatic SWP bus state management
 Provide loopback mode for testing
```
 Support automatic processing of Start of Frame (SOF) and End of Frame (EOF)
```
 Support configurable bit rate up to 2Mbit/s with configurable interrupts
 Provide CRC error, underflow, overflow, and slave device recovery monitoring flags
 Support CRC-16 calculation, generation, and verification
38.2 Overview
Figure 38-1 Structure block diagram of single-wire protocol main interface

38.3 Register Description
38.3.1 SWP Initialization and Activation
SWP initialization and activation transition the SWPMI_IO state from low to high. When using the internal
transceiver, the software operation follows this sequence:
```
1) Enable the SWPMI_IO transceiver via bit 1 of the R32_SWPMI_CR register (SWPTEN) and set SWPMI_IO
```
```
to low (SWP bus “disabled”);
```
```
2) Wait for bit 1 of the RDYF field in the R32_SWPMI_SR register (polling flag) or enable interrupts via the
```
```
RDYIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register;
```
```
3) Set bit 1 of the SWPACT field in the R32_SWPMI_CR register to transition the SWP bus from “Disabled” to
```
“Suspended” state, thereby activating SWP.
38.3.2 SWP Bus Status
The SWP bus has three states: “Disabled,” “Suspended,” and “Activated.”
State transitions include:
```
 Activate: Transition from “Disabled” state to “Suspended” state;
```
```
 Suspend: Transition from “Activated” state to “Suspended” state;
```
```
 Disable: Transition from “Suspended” state to “Disabled” state;
```
 Master Device Recovery: Transition initiated by the master device from “Suspended” state to “Activated”
```
state;
```
 Slave Device Recovery: Transition initiated by the slave device from “Suspended” state to “Activated” state.
Activation
During the reset phase and immediately after reset completion, SWPMI_IO is configured for emulation mode.
Refer to Section 38.3.1 for the SWP bus activation procedure.
Suspended
```
If communication exists between the SWP bus and a slave device (regardless of whether in transmit or receive
```
```
mode), the SWP bus remains in the “active” state. If no subsequent transmit or receive requests occur, the SWP
```
bus will transition back to the “suspended” state after seven idle bits.
Disable
```
1) Disabling Request
```
When the SWP is in the “Suspended” state, if communication is no longer required, the user may request
switching the SWP to the ‘Disabled’ state by disabling the SWPMI peripheral. Setting the DEACT bit in the
R32_SWPMI_CR register to 1 enables switching to the “Disabled” state. If the SWPMI does not detect a “Slave
Device Recovery” state, the DEACTF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register will be set to 1, and the SWPACT bit
in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register will be cleared. If SWPMI detects a “Slave Device Recovery” state after
DEACT is set to 1, the SRF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register will be set to 1, DEACTF remains cleared,
SWPACT remains set to 1, and the DEACT bit is cleared. Clear the DEACT bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register,
then set SWPACT to 1 to reactivate SWP.
```
2) Disabled Mode
```
The user must clear the SWPACT bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register for the SWP to immediately transition to
the “Disabled” mode and ignore any incoming “Slave Device Recovery” state.
```
Note: To further reduce current consumption, configure the SWPMI_IO port in the GPIO controller to push-pull
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 831
output mode, set it to low, and finally clear the SWPTEN bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register.
Master device recovery
After SWPMI is enabled, the user may request SWPMI frame transmission. First, SWPMI transmits a transition
sequence and eight idle bits, indicating master device recovery, then commences frame transmission. Following
“Master Device Recovery,” the SWP transitions from the ‘Suspended’ state to the “Activated” state. Refer to
Figure 38-2: SWP Bus States.
Figure 38-2 SWP bus state diagram
```

```


Slave device recovery
When SWPMI is enabled, if SWPMI receives a slave device recovery status signal, the SWP transitions from the
“suspended” state to the ‘activated’ state. “Slave device recovery” triggers the SRF flag bit in the
R32_SWPMI_ISR register to be set to 1.
```
38.3.3 SWPMI_IO (Internal Transceiver) Bypass
```
```
The microcontroller integrates an SWPMI_IO (internal transceiver) compliant with the ETSI TS 102 613
```
technical specification. To bypass this transceiver, set the SWP_TBYP bit in the R32_SWPMI_OR register to 1.
In bypass mode, the SWPMI_IO is disabled, and the SWP_RX, SWP_TX, and SWPMI_SUP signals become
available as multiplexed functions on these three GPIO pins. This configuration can be used to connect an external
transceiver.
```
Note: In SWPMI_IO bypass mode, the SWPTEN bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register must be cleared.
```
38.3.4 SWPMI Baud Rate
In the R32_SWPMI_BRR register, set the bit rate according to the following formula:
```
FSWP = FHCLK/((BR[7:0]+1)x4)
```
```
Note: Maximum bit rate is 2 Mbit/s.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 832
38.3.5 SWPMI Frame Processing
```
The SWP frame consists of the following components: Start of Frame (SOF), a payload of 1 to 30 bytes, a 16-bit
```
```
CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check), and End of Frame (EOF). See Figure 38-3.
```
```
The SWPMI integrates a 32-bit data transmit register (R32_SWPMI_TDR) and a 32-bit data receive register
```
```
(R32_SWPMI_RDR).
```
In data transmission mode, SOF insertion, EOF insertion, CRC calculation, and insertion are all automatically
managed by SWPMI. The user only needs to provide the payload size and content. After writing data to the
R32_SWPMI_TDR register, frame transmission occurs immediately. Specific flag bits indicate when the
transmission data register is empty and when the data frame transmission is complete.
In data reception mode, SOF deletion, EOF deletion, CRC calculation, and verification are all automatically
managed by SWPMI. Users need only read the payload size and content. Specific flag bits will indicate frame
reception completion, register full status, and potential CRC error events.
Figure 38-3 SWP frame structure
```
SOF D1D0 D2 ... CRC(2 bytes) EOF
```
```
SOF=7Eh=01111110b EOF=7Fh=01111111b
```
```
PAYLOAD(up to 30 bytes)
```
```
Insertion (in transmit mode) and deletion (in receive mode) of padding bits are automatically managed by SWPMI
```
core. These operations are transparent to users.
38.3.6 Transmit Processing
```
Before transmitting a frame, the user must first activate the SWP; refer to Section 38.3.1. Software
```
implementations for frame transmission include multiple modes: no software buffer mode, single software buffer
mode, and multiple software buffer mode. When using software buffers, data is transferred via a DMA channel
from the software buffer in RAM memory to the SWPMI peripheral's transmit data register.
No software buffer mode
In No Software Buffer Mode, DMA does not need to be enabled. Polling the status flag within the main loop or
SWPMI interrupt routine handles SWP frame transmission. The SWPMI includes a 32-bit transmit data register
```
(R32_SWPMI_TDR); writing to this register triggers transmission of up to 4 bytes.
```
Software-Bufferless Mode can be selected by clearing the TXDMA bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register.
The first write to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register triggers frame transmission. Within the first word written to the
R32_SWPMI_TDR register, bits [7:0] indicate the number of data bytes in the payload. Bits [15:8], bits [23:16],
and bits [31:24] contain the first three bytes of the payload, where bits [15:8] contain the first byte, bits [23:16]
contain the second byte, and bits [31:24] contain the third byte. Subsequent writes to the R32_SWPMI_TDR
```
register will only contain additional payload data bytes (up to four bytes per write operation).
```
```
Note: The least significant byte of the first 32-bit word written to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register encodes the
```
number of data bytes in the payload. This value must fall within the range of 1 to 30. If the least significant byte
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 833
exceeds this range, it will be ignored and will not trigger data transmission.
Writing to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register triggers the following sequence of operations:
```
1) When the SWP bus is in the “Suspended” state, the system sends a transition sequence followed by 8 idle bits
```
```
(for host recovery). Conversely, if the SWP bus is in the “Active” state, this operation is not triggered;
```
```
2) Frame start transmission;
```
```
3) Transmit the payload based on the contents of the R32_SWPMI_TRD register. If the payload contains more
```
than 3 bytes, the R32_SWPMI_TDR must be refilled by software whenever the TXE flag in the
```
R32_SWPMI_ISR register is set to 1, provided the TXBEF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register is not set to 1;
```
```
4) Transmit the 16-bit CRC (automatically computed by the SWPMI core);
```
```
5) Transmit the end-of-frame (EOF) signal.
```
When the software performs a write operation to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register, it will automatically clear the
TXE flag.
```
After a complete frame transmission succeeds, if no other frame transmission is requested (i.e., no subsequent
```
```
write operation to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register occurs after the TXBEF flag is set to 1), the TCF and SUSP
```
flags in the R32_SWFMI_ISR register will be set to 1 after 7 idle bits following the completion of the EOF
transmission. Additionally, setting the TCIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register triggers an interrupt. See Figure
38-4.

Single software buffer mode
In Single Software Buffer Mode, complete SWP frames can be transmitted via DMA without CPU intervention.
DMA will refill the 32-bit R32_SWPMI_TDR register. Software can poll the SWPMI_TXBEF flag to determine
if frame transmission has completed. To select Single Software Buffer Mode: Clear the TXDMA bit 1 and
TXMODE bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register.
```
The DMA channel or data stream must be configured in one of the following modes (refer to the DMA section):
```
```
 Memory size set to 32 bits;
```
```
 Peripheral size set to 32 bits;
```
```
 Enable memory increment mode;
```
```
 Disable cycle mode;
```
```
 Disable peripheral increment mode;
```
```
 Disable memory-to-memory mode;
```
```
 Number of words to transfer must be set according to SWP frame length;
```
```
 Target address is the R32_SWPMI_TDR register;
```
 Data transfer direction is set to read from memory.
 Source address is the SWP frame buffer in RAM.
Subsequently, the user performs the following operations:
```
1) Set the TXDMA bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register to 1;
```
```
2) Set the TXBEIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register to 1;
```
```
3) Populate the buffer in RAM memory (the number of data bytes in the payload is indicated by the least
```
```
significant byte of the first word);
```
```
4) Trigger the DMA transfer and frame transmission by enabling the data stream or channel within the DMA
```
module.
When the TXE flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR is set to 1, the SWPMI will initiate a DMA request. During the
DMA write operation to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register, the TXE flag bit will be automatically cleared.
Within the SWPMI interrupt service routine, the user must check the TXBEF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register.
If this bit is set and additional frames remain to be transmitted, the user must perform the following actions:
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 835
```
1) Disable the data stream or channel within the DMA module;
```
```
2) Update the buffer in RAM with the contents of the next frame to be transmitted;
```
```
3) Set the total number of words to transfer in the DMA module;
```
```
4) Enable the data stream or channel in the DMA module to trigger the next frame transmission;
```
```
5) Clear the TXBEF flag by setting the CTXBEF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register to 1.
```
Multi-Software buffer mode
Multi-Software buffer mode supports configuring multiple frame buffers in RAM memory to ensure continuous
data transmission, maintain extremely low CPU load, and provide software with additional latency to execute
```
buffer updates (using DMA). Software can monitor the DMA counter at any time and update the SWP frame in
```
RAM memory accordingly.
For optimal performance, Multi-Software Buffer Mode should be used in conjunction with DMA in cyclic mode.
Within the SWP frame payload, each transmit buffer in RMA memory must have a fixed length of eight 32-bit
words, regardless of the actual byte count. These transmit buffers require software filling, with an 8-byte offset
maintained between consecutive buffers. The first data byte of the buffer indicates the total number of bytes in the
frame payload, as illustrated below.

Select the multi-software buffer mode by setting the TXDMA and TXMODE bits in the R32_SWPMI_CR register
to 1. To use 4 transmit buffers, the user must configure the DMA as follows:
```
The DMA channel or data stream must be configured in the following modes (refer to the DMA section):
```
```
 Memory size set to 32 bits;
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 836
```
 Peripheral size set to 32 bits;
```
```
 The number of words to transfer must be set to 32 (8 words per buffer);
```
```
 Data transfer direction set to read from memory;
```
```
 Disable memory-to-memory mode;
```
```
 Disable peripheral increment mode;
```
```
 Enable memory increment mode;
```
```
 Enable cycle mode;
```
```
 Source address is buffer 1 in RAM;
```
 Destination address is the R32_SWPMI_TDR register.
Subsequently, the user performs the following operations:
```
1) Set the TXDMA bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register to 1;
```
```
2) Set the TXBEIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register to 1;
```
```
3) Populate buffers 1, 2, 3, and 4 in RAM (the number of data bytes in the payload is indicated by the least
```
```
significant byte of the first word);
```
```
4) Trigger the DMA transfer and frame transmission by enabling the data stream or channel within the DMA
```
module.
Within the SWPMI interrupt routine, the user must check the TXBEF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register. If this
bit is set to 1, the user should set the CTXBEF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register to 1 to clear the TXBEF flag
and update Buffer 1 in RAM memory. Upon the next SWPMI interrupt, the user updates Buffer 2, repeating this
cycle.
```
Software can also read the DMA counter (data volume to be transferred) in the DMA register to retrieve frames
```
already transferred from RAM and sent. For example, if software uses 4 transmit buffers and the DMA counter
value equals 17, this indicates two buffers in the RAM region are ready for update. This feature effectively
addresses scenarios where the software must transmit multiple frames before handling the SWPMI interrupt. In
such cases, the software must update multiple buffers.
When no frames require transmission, the user must disable the DMA module's cyclic mode. Transmission will
cease upon completion of buffer 4.
If transmission is terminated prematurely, such as upon completion of buffer 2, the user must set the least
significant byte of the first word in both buffer 3 and buffer 4 to 0.
When the data byte count in the least significant byte of the first word read is 0, the TXDMA bit in the
R32_SWPMI_CR register will be cleared by hardware.
38.3.7 Receive Processing
Before frame transmission, the user must activate the SWP. Refer to Section 38.3.1. After setting bit 1 of the
SWPACT field in the R32_SWPMI_CR register, the “slave device recovery” state will set the SRF flag in the
R32_SWPMI_ISR register to 1 and automatically enable the SWPMI for frame reception.
If the SWP bus is in an "active" state, such as during frame transmission, the SWPMI core does not require a
"slave device recovery" state and can immediately proceed with reception.
Software implementation for frame reception includes multiple modes: no software buffer mode, single software
buffer mode, and multiple software buffer mode. Utilizing software buffers requires a DMA channel to transfer
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 837
data from the receive data register within the SWPMI peripheral to the software buffer in RAM memory.
No software buffer mode
In No Software Buffer Mode, DMA does not need to be enabled. Polling the status flag within the main loop or
SWPMI interrupt routine handles SWP frame transmission. SWPMI includes a 32-bit receive data register
```
(R32_SWPMI_RDR), allowing reception of up to 4 bytes before reading this register.
```
No Software-buffer mode is selected by clearing the RXDMA bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register.
```
After receiving the Start of Frame (SOF), subsequent payload bytes are stored in the R32_SWPMI_RDR register.
```
When R32_SWPMI_RDR is full, the RXNE flag in R32_SWPMI_ISR is set to 1. Additionally, an interrupt is
generated if the RIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register is set to 1. Users can read the R32_SWPMI_RDR
register to retrieve data. When software reads the R32_SWPMI_RDR register, the RXNE flag is automatically
cleared.
```
Upon receiving a complete frame (CRC, EOF), the RXNE and RXBFF flags in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register are
```
```
set to 1. The user must read the last byte(s) of the payload from the R32_SWPMI_RDR register and set the
```
CRXBFF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register to clear the RXBFF flag. The number of data bytes in the payload
can be obtained from the R32_SWPMI_RFL register. When software reads the R32_SWPMI_RDR register, the
RXNE flag is automatically reset again. As shown in the figure below.
When RXNE is cleared, reading the R32_SWPMI_RDR register returns 0.

Single software buffer mode
In Single Software Buffer Mode, complete SWP frames can be transmitted via DMA without CPU intervention.
DMA transfers received data from the 32-bit R32_SWPMI_RDR register to RAM storage. Software can poll the
SWPMI_RBFF flag to determine if frame reception has completed. Single Software Buffer Mode: Clear the
RXDMA bit position 1 and RXMODE bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register.
```
The DMA channel or data stream must be configured in one of the following modes (refer to the DMA section):
```
```
 Memory size set to 32 bits;
```

Multi-Software Buffer Mode
Multi-Software Buffer Mode supports configuring multiple frame buffers in RAM memory to ensure continuous
data transmission while maintaining extremely low CPU load. Frame payloads and frame status flags are stored
together in RAM memory. Software can check the DMA counter and status flags at any time to process SWP
frames received in RAM memory.
For optimal performance, Multi-Software Buffer Mode should be used in conjunction with DMA in cyclic mode.
Select Multi-Software Buffer Mode: Set the RXDMA and RXMODE bits in the R32_SWPMI_CR register to 1.
To implement n receive buffers in RAM, the DMA channel or data stream must be configured in one of the
```
following modes (refer to the DMA section):
```
```
 Memory size set to 32 bits;
```
```
 Peripheral size set to 32 bits;
```
```
 Number of words to transfer must be set to 8*n (8 words per buffer);
```
```
 Data transfer direction set to read from peripheral;
```
```
 Disable memory-to-memory mode;
```
```
 Disable peripheral increment mode;
```
```
 Enable memory increment mode;
```
```
 Enable cyclic mode;
```
```
 Source address is the R32_SWPMI_TDR register;
```
 Destination address is buffer 1 in RAM.
Subsequently, the user performs the following operations:
```
1) Set bit 1 in the RXDMA field of the R32_SWPMI_CR register;
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 840
```
2) Set bit 1 in the RXBEIE field of the R32_SWPMI_IER register;
```
```
3) Enable the data stream or channel within the DMA module.
```
In the SWPMI interrupt routine, the user must check the RXBEF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register. If this bit is
set to 1, the user should set the CTXBEF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register to 1 to clear the RXBEF flag. The
```
first frame payload received in the first buffer (the RAM address set in DMA2_CMAR1) can then be read. The
```
number of data bytes in the payload can be obtained from bits [23:16] of the 8th word from the end.
```
Upon the next SWPMI interrupt routine, the user reads the second frame received in the second buffer (address set
```
```
in DMA2_CMAR1 + 8), repeating this process cyclically. See Figure 38-9.
```

If the application software cannot guarantee processing the SMPMI interrupt before receiving the next frame, each
buffer status will be presented in the most significant byte of the 8th buffer word:
 Receive Overflow Flag: The RXOVRF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register, indicated by bit 25 of the
eighth word. For details on overflow errors, refer to Section 38.3.8.
 Receive Buffer Full Flag: The RXBFF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register, indicated by bit 26 of the
eighth word.
 CRC error flag: The RXBERF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register, indicated by bit 24 of the 8th word. For
details on CRC errors, see Section 38.3.8.
When a CRC error occurs, both the RXBFF and RXBERF flags are set to 1, meaning bits 24 and 26 will be set to
1. When an overflow occurs, the overflow flag bit is set to 1, i.e., bit 25 is set to 1. The receive buffer full flag is
```
only set to 1 if the overflow occurs during the reception of the last byte; Subsequently, for both the current and
```
next frame reception, bits 25 and 26 will be set to 1.
Software can read the DMA counter in the DMA register to retrieve frames transferred via DMA and stored in
RAM. For example, if software uses 4 receive buffers and the DMA counter value equals 17, this indicates two
buffers are ready for software readout in the RAM region. In multi-software buffer reception mode, if the software
is reading bits 24, 25, and 26 of the eighth word, the RXBERF, RXOVRF, and RXBFF flags need not be cleared
after each received frame.
38.3.8 Error Management
Underflow occurred during payload transmission
In the process of transmitting the frame payload, if the transmission underflow occurs, the TXUNRF flag in
R32_SWPMI_ISR register will be triggered as a warning. If the TXBUNREIE bit in R32_SWPMI_IER register is
set, an interrupt will be generated. When transmission underflow occurs, SWPMI will stop sending payload and
```
send damaged CRC (the first bit of the first CRC byte sent is inverted), followed by EOF flag. If DMA is used, the
```
TXDMA bit in R32_SWPMI_CR register will be cleared automatically.
When TXUNRF is set to 1, any writing to the R32_SWPMI_TDR register is ignored. The user must set the
CTXUNRF bit of R32_SWPMI_ICR register to 1 to clear the TXUNRF flag.
Overflow occurred during payload reception
In the process of receiving the frame payload, if there is reception overflow, the RXOVRF flag in
R32_SWPMI_ISR register will be triggered as a warning. When receiving overflow occurs, the incoming data
will not be used by SWPMI to update R32_SWPMI_RDR, so the incoming data will be lost.
Data reception continues until EOF. Once the overflow condition ceases, the RXBFF flag will be set to 1. When
the RXBFF flag is set, the user may check the RXOVRF flag. To clear the RXOVRF flag, the user must set the
CRXOVRF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register to 1. If immediate overflow detection is required, set the
RXBOVREIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register to ensure an immediate interrupt trigger upon overflow
occurrence.
When both the RXOVRF and RXNE flags are set, two R32_SWPMI_RDR read operations will execute following
an overflow event. This indicates that at least one received byte was lost, and the byte loaded into
R32_SWPMI_RDR contains the byte received immediately before the overflow occurred.
In multi-software buffer mode, if the last byte of a received frame sets the RXOVRF flag, both the current frame
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 842
```
and the next frame will set the overflow bit (bit 25 of the 8th byte) to 1.
```
A CRC error occurred during payload reception
Upon receiving two CRC bytes, if a CRC error occurs, the RXBERF flag in the R32_SWPMI_ISR register will be
set to 1 after completing EOF reception. At this point, if the RXBEIE bit in the R32_SWPMI_IER register is set to
1, an interrupt will be triggered. Refer to Figure 38-10. To clear the RXBERF flag, the user must set the
CRXBERF bit in the R32_SWPMI_ICR register to 1.

Loss or corruption of padding bits during payload reception
When the padding bits in the payload are lost or damaged, the RXBERF and RXBFF flags in R32_SWPMI_ISR
will be set to 1 after receiving EOF.
Receiving damaged EOF
```
After receiving SOF, SWPMI will start to accumulate the received bytes until EOF is received (ignoring any
```
```
possible SOF). After receiving EOF, SWPMI will be ready to start a new round of frame reception and wait for
```
the next SOF. If the EOF is damaged, the RXBERF and RXBFF flags in the SWPMI_ISR register will be set after
the next EOF is received.
```
Note: When the damaged EOF is received, the payload will continue to be received. Therefore, if the number of
```
bytes received exceeds 30, the number of bytes in the payload can take the value of 31. The number of bytes in the
payload is read in the R32_SWPMI_RFL register, or in bits [23:16] of the 8th word in the RAM memory buffer
according to different working modes.
38.3.9 Loopback Mode
You can use loopback mode for testing. The user must set the LPBK bit in the R32_SWPMI_CR register to enable
loopback mode. When loopback mode is enabled, SWP_TX and SWP_RX signals will be connected. Therefore,
all frames sent through SWPMI will be retracted.

```
Chapter 39 Electronic Signature (ESIG)
```
Electronic Signature contains chip identification information: Flash memory area capacity and unique
identification. It is burned into the system storage area of the memory module by the manufacturer when leaving
```
the factory, and can be read through SWD (SDI) or application code.
```
39.1 Function Description
Flash memory area capacity: Indicates the size that the current chip user application can use.
Unique identification: 96-bit binary code, unique to any microcontroller, users can only read and access it and
cannot modify it. This unique identification information can be used as the security password, decryption key,
```
product serial number, etc. of the microcontroller (product) to improve the system security mechanism or indicate
```
identity information.
Users of the above content can perform read access in 8/16/32 bits.

```
Chapter 40 Flexible Memory Controller (FMC)
```
This chapter's module description applies only to the CH32H417 microcontroller product.
```
The Flexible Memory Controller (FMC) is a controller for managing external memory, comprising: NAND
```
```
memory controller, NOR/PSRAM memory controller, and synchronous DRAM (SDRAM/Mobile LPSDR
```
```
SDRAM) controller.
```
40.1 Main Features
The FMC manages expanded connectivity to different types of memory, including: SDRAM, NAND Flash, and
synchronous/asynchronous static memory. Its primary purposes are: meeting the access time requirements of
```
external memory devices; and translating HB data communication transactions into appropriate external device
```
protocols.
All external memories share address, data, and control signals, but each possesses an independent chip select
signal. The FMC can access only one external device at a time.
The main features of FMC controllers are as follows:
 Connect static memory mapped devices:
- Static Random Access Memory (SRAM)
- PSRAM (4 memory regions)
- NOR Flash/OneNAND Flash
- NAND Flash memory with hardware ECC capable of verifying up to 8KB of data
```
 Connect to synchronous DRAM (SDRAM/Mobile LPSDR SDRAM) memory
```
 External asynchronous wait control
 16×32-bit depth write FIFO
 Each memory region configurable independently
 Independent chip select control for each memory region
 Support 8-bit, 16-bit, or 32-bit wide memory data buses
 Programmable continuous clock output for asynchronous and synchronous access
```
 SDRAM controller features a cacheable 6×32-bit depth read FIFO (6×14-bit address tag)
```
 Write enable and byte channel select outputs compatible with PSRAM, SRAM, and SDRAM devices
```
 Support burst mode for accelerated access to synchronous devices (e.g., NOR Flash, PSRAM, and SDRAM)
```
40.2 Overview
As shown in the figure below, the FMC comprises four main modules: the HB interface, SDRAM controller,
NAND controller, and NOR Flash/PSRAM/SRAM controller.
