40.3 HB Interface
The HB device interface permits the CPU and other HB bus masters to access external memory. HB transactions
are translated into external device protocols. Specifically, when the selected external memory width is 16 bits or 8
bits, the 32-bit-wide transaction in the HB is split into multiple consecutive 16-bit or 8-bit accesses. Between
```
consecutive accesses, the FMC chip select (FMC_NEx) does not toggle, except when operating in access mode D
```
with extended mode enabled.
The FMC generates an HB error under the following conditions:
 Reading or writing to an FMC memory region that is not enabled.
```
 Violating the SDRAM address range (accessing reserved address ranges).
```
```
 Writing to a write-protected SDRAM memory region (WP bit 1 in the R32_FMC_SDCRx register).
```
 Reading or writing to NOR Flash memory regions when the FACCEN bit in the R32_FMC_BCRx register is
reset.
The impact of this HB error depends on the HB master device attempting the read/write access.
 If it is the DMA controller, a DMA transfer error is generated and the corresponding DMA channel is
automatically disabled.
```
The HB clock (HCLK) serves as the reference clock for the FMC.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 856
40.3.1 Supported Memory and Transactions
Common transaction rules
The HB transaction data width requested is 8, 16, 32, or 256 bits, whereas the external device accessed has a fixed
data width. This difference can cause data width mismatch problems. To avoid this problem, the transaction rules
to follow are as follows:
 HB transaction data width equals memory data width: Normal operation.
 HB transaction data width exceeds memory width: The FMC splits the HB transaction into multiple smaller
```
contiguous memory accesses to match the external data width. The FMC chip select (FMC_NEx) does not
```
toggle between contiguous accesses.
 HB transaction data width is less than memory width: Transfer consistency may be affected, depending on
the type of external device.
- Accessing devices with byte selection capability (ROM, SRAM, SDRAM, PSRAM): The FMC permits
read and write transactions, accessing the correct data through its byte select lines NBL[1:0]. The byte
```
to be written is addressed via NBL[1:0]. All memory bytes are read (NBL[1:0] remains low during read
```
```
transactions), with invalid bytes subsequently discarded.
```
- Accessing devices without byte selection capability (NOR, NAND Flash): This occurs when byte access
```
is required for 16-bit wide FLASH memory. Since these devices do not support byte-mode access (only
```
```
allowing 16-bit words to be read from or written to Flash), read transactions are permitted but write
```
```
transactions are not (the controller reads the entire 16-bit memory word but uses only the required
```
```
byte).
```
NOR Flash/PSRAM and SDRAM rewinding support
Since not all masters can issue rollback transactions, synchronous memory must be configured in a linear burst
mode of undefined length. If a master generates HB rollback transactions:
 Read operations will be divided into two linear burst transactions.
```
 If the write FIFO is enabled, write operations will be divided into two linear burst transactions; if the write
```
FIFO is disabled, write operations will be divided into multiple linear burst transactions.

external memory address FMC_A[24:0]. When the memory width is 32 bits, the FMC will use the internal
HADDR[25:2] address for external addressing. Regardless of the external memory width, FMC_A[0] must be
connected to the external memory address A[0].
40.4.2 NAND Flash Address Mapping
The NAND memory area is divided into several memory areas, as shown in the following table.
Table 40-4 NAND memory mapping and timing register
Start address End address FMC storage area Storage space Timing register
0x88000000 0x8BFFFFFF
Storage area 3-NAND Flash
Characteristic
```
region R32_FMC_PATT(0x8C)
```
```
0x80000000 0x83FFFFFF Universalarea R32_FMC_PMEM(0x88)
```
For NAND Flash memory, the storage space of general area and characteristic area is divided into three parts, all
of which are located in the lower 256KB, as shown in the following table:
Table 40-5 NAND storage area selection
Partial name HADDR[17:16] Address range
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 859
Address area 1X 0x020000-0x03FFFF
Command area 01 0x010000-0x01FFFF
Data area 00 0x000000-0x0FFFF
```
Data Area: The first 64KB within the general/feature storage space; Command Area: The second 64KB within the
```
```
general/feature storage space; Address Area: The next 128KB within the general/feature storage space.
```
Application software utilizes these three areas to access the NAND Flash memory:
 To send a command to NAND Flash, the software must write the command value to any memory cell within
the command area.
 To specify a read or write address for NAND Flash, the software must write the address value to any memory
```
cell within the address area. Since the address length can be 4 or 5 bytes (depending on the actual memory
```
```
size), specifying a complete address requires multiple consecutive write operations to the address area.
```
 Read or write data: The software reads data from or writes data to any storage cell within the data region.
 Since NAND Flash memory automatically increments addresses, it is unnecessary to increment addresses
within the data region to access consecutive memory locations.
Because NAND Flash memory will automatically increment the address, it can access continuous memory
locations without incrementing the address of the data area.

40.5 NOR Flash/PSRAM Controller
The FMC generates appropriate signal timing to drive the following memory types:
```
 Asynchronous SRAM and ROM: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit;
```
```
 PSRAM (Cellular RAM): Asynchronous mode, burst mode with synchronous access, multiplexed or
```
```
non-multiplexed;
```
 NOR Flash: Asynchronous mode, burst mode with synchronous access, multiplexed or non-multiplexed.
```
The FMC outputs unique chip select signals NE[4:1] for each memory region. All other signals (address, data, and
```
```
control) are shared. The FMC supports multiple devices through programmable timing, including:
```
```
 Programmable continuous clock (FMC_CLK) output
```
```
 Programmable wait cycles (up to 15 clock cycles)
```
```
 Programmable bus turnaround cycles (up to 15 clock cycles)
```
 Independent read and write timing and protocols to support various memory types and timing requirements
```
 Programmable output enable and write enable delays (up to 15 clock cycles)
```
To generate the FMC_CLK continuous clock, memory area 1 must also be configured to support synchronous
```
mode (refer to Section 40.5.6: NOR/PSRAM Control Registers). Since all synchronous memory uses the same
```
```
clock, the HB data size must match the memory data width (MWID) when generating continuous output clocks
```
and performing synchronous accesses. Otherwise, the FMC_CLK frequency will vary based on the occurrence of
```
HB data transactions (refer to Section 40.5.5: Synchronous Transactions for information on the FMC_CLK
```
```
division ratio formula).
```
```
Each memory region has a fixed size of 64MB. Each memory region is configured via dedicated registers (refer to
```
```
Section 40.5.6: NOR/PSRAM Control Registers). Programmable memory parameters include access times (as
```
```
shown in the table below) and support for wait management (used for burst mode access to NOR Flash and
```
```
PSRAM).
```
When reading data using the NOR Flash/PSRAM controller, only DMA 256-bit reads are permitted.
Table 40-11 Programmable access parameters of NOR/PSRAM

40.5.3 General Timing Rule
Signal synchronization
```
 All controller output signals change on the rising edge of the internal clock (HCLK);
```
```
 In synchronous mode (read/write), all output signals change on the rising edge of HCLK. Regardless of the
```
CLKDIV value, all output signals change as follows:
- NOEL/NWEL/NEL/NADVL/NADVH/NBLL address valid outputs change on the falling edge of the
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 866
FMC_CLK clock.
- NOEH/NWEH/NEH/NOEH/NBLH address valid outputs change on the rising edge of the FMC_CLK
clock.
40.5.4 NOR Flash/PSRAM Controller Asynchronous Transaction
```
Asynchronous static memory (NOR Flash, PSRAM, SRAM)
```
```
 Signals are synchronized via the internal clock HCLK. This clock is not sent to the memory;
```
 FMC always samples data before disabling the chip select signal NE. This ensures compliance with memory
```
data hold timing requirements (typically 0ns from chip select enable high to minimum data conversion time).
```
```
 If extended mode is enabled (EXTMOD bit set to 1 in the R32_FMC_BCRx register), up to four extended
```
```
modes (A, B, C, D) are available. Modes A, B, C, and D can be mixed for read and write operations. For
```
example, a read operation can be performed in mode A while a write operation occurs in mode B.
```
 If extended mode is disabled (EXTMOD bit cleared in the R32_FMC_BCRx register), the FMC can operate
```
in either Mode 1 or Mode 2 as described below:
- When selecting SRAM/PSRAM memory type, Mode 1 is the default mode (MTYP = 0x0 or 0x01 in the
```
R32_FMC_BCRx register);
```
- When selecting NOR memory type, Mode 2 is the default mode (MTYP = 0x10 in the
```
R32_FMC_BCRx register).
```
```
Mode 1-SRAM/PSRAM (CRAM)
```

WAIT management in asynchronous access
If the asynchronous memory sends a WAIT signal indicating that it is not ready to receive or provide data, the
ASYNCWAIT bit in the R32_FMC_BCRx register must be set.
```
If the WAIT signal is in an active state (the level depends on the WAITPOL bit), the second access phase (data
```
```
establishment phase) controlled by the DATAST bit will be extended until WAIT becomes invalid. Unlike the data
```
```
establishment phase, the first access phase (address establishment and address holding phase) controlled by
```
ADDSET and ADDHLD bits is insensitive to WAIT, so the first access phase will not be extended.
The data setup phase must be configured to detect WAIT 4 HCLK cycles before the end of the memory
transaction. The following situations must be considered:
```
1) The WAIT signal sent by the memory is aligned with the NOE/NEW signal:
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 879
```
DATAST≥(4*HCLK)+ max_wait_assertion_time
```
```
2) The WAIT signal sent by the memory is aligned with NEx (or the NOE/NWE signal does not flip):
```
If
max_wait_assertion_time>address_phase+hold_phase
```
Then:
```
```
DATAST≥(4*HCLK)+(max_wait_assertion_time–address_phase–hold_phase)
```
Otherwise
DATAST≥4*HCLK
Where max_wait_assertion_time is the longest time it takes for the memory to enable the wait signal after
NEx/NOE/NWE goes low.
Figures 40-15 and 40-16 show the number of increased HCLK clock cycles in the memory access phase after the
```
asynchronous memory releases WAIT (independent of the above situation).
```

40.5.5 Synchronous Transaction
The memory clock FMC_CLK is a divisor of HCLK. It depends on the value of CLKDIV and the MWID/HB data
size, as shown in the following formula:
```
FMC_CLK Frequency division ratio = max (CLKDIV+1, MWID (HB data size))
```
When MWID is 16-bit or 8-bit, the frequency division ratio of FMC_CLK is always defined by the setting value
of CLKDIV.
When MWID is 32-bit, the frequency division ratio of FMC_CLK also depends on the size of HB data.
```
Example:
```
 LKDIV=1, MWID=32 bits, when HB data size=8 bits, FMC_CLK=HCLK/4.
 CLKDIV=1, MWID=16 bits, when HB data size =8 bits, FMC_CLK=HCLK/2.
NOR Flash specifies the minimum time from NADV enable to CLK high. In order to meet this limitation, FMC
```
will not send the clock to the memory within the first internal clock cycle of synchronous access (before NADV is
```
```
enabled). This ensures that the rising edge of the memory clock appears in the middle of the NADV low pulse.
```
Data delay and NOR delay
Data delay is the number of cycles to wait before sampling data. The value of DATLAT must match the delay
value specified in the NORFLASH configuration register. When NADV is low in the data delay count, FMC will
not count the clock period.
Some NOR Flash count the NADV low period in the data delay count, so the exact relationship between the NOR
Flash delay and the FMC DATLAT parameter can be any of the following:
```
 NOR Flash delay =(DATLAT+2) CLK clock cycles.
```
```
 NOR Flash delay =(DATLAT+3) CLK clock cycles.
```
Recently, some memories will enable NWAIT in the delay phase. In this case, you can set DATLAT to the
minimum value. Then, FMC will sample the data and wait long enough to evaluate whether the data is valid. In
this way, FMC can detect the delay time in the memory, so as to process the real data.
Other memories will not enable NWAIT during the delay. In this case, the delay of FMC and memory must be set
correctly, otherwise invalid data may be misused as valid data, or valid data may be lost in the initial stage of
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 881
memory access.
Single burst transmission
When the selected storage area is configured in synchronous burst mode, for example, if an HB single burst
```
transaction is requested from a 16-bit memory, FMC will execute a burst transaction with a length of 1 (if the HB
```
```
transmission is 16 bits) or a burst transaction with a length of 2 (if the HB transmission is 32 bits), and then
```
disable the chip selection signal at the last data strobe.
Compared with asynchronous read operation, this is not the most efficient transmission method in terms of cycle.
However, random asynchronous reading requires reprogramming the memory access mode first, so the total time
will be longer.
Cross the border page of Cellular RAM1.5
Cellular RAM1.5 does not allow burst access to cross page boundaries. When the CPSIZE bit in the
R32_FMC_BCR1 register is configured according to the memory page size to reach the memory page size, the
FMC controller will automatically separate the burst access.
Waiting management
```
For synchronous NOR Flash, NWAIT will be evaluated after the configured delay period (equivalent to
```
```
(DATLAT+2) CLK clock cycles).
```
```
If NWAIT is valid (low level when WAITPOL=0 and high level when WAITPOL=1), the waiting state will be
```
```
inserted until NWAIT is invalid (high level when WAITPOL=0 and low level when WAITPOL=1).
```
```
When NWAIT is invalid, the data will be considered valid immediately (bit WAITCFG=1) or at the next clock
```
```
edge (bit WAITCFG=0).
```
During the waiting period when the NWAIT signal is inserted, the controller will continue to send clock pulses to
the memory to keep the chip select and output enable signals valid. But the data is not considered valid.
In burst mode, NOR Flash NWAIT signal has two timing configurations:
```
 Flash sends out NWAIT signal (the default value after reset) one data period before the waiting period.
```
 Flash sends out NWAIT signal during the waiting period.
FMC supports these 2 configurations of NOR Flash waiting period, and each chip selection is configured through
```
the WAITCFG bit (x=0..3) pin of R32_FMC_BCRx register.
```

devices generate an NWAIT signal (refer to the specific Flash datasheet for details).

Each timing configuration register contains 4 parameters: three define the number of HCLK cycles for the 3
access phases of the NAND Flash, while the fourth defines the timing for initiating data bus drive during write
```
access. The diagram above illustrates the timing parameter definitions for general memory access; access timing
```
for feature memory spaces follows a similar pattern.
40.6.4 NAND Flash Operation
```
The Command Latch Enable (CLE) signal and Address Latch Enable (ALE) signal for NAND Flash devices are
```
driven by the address signals from the FMC controller. This means that to send a command or address to the
NAND Flash, the CPU must perform a write operation to a specific address within its memory space.
A typical page read operation from a NAND Flash device requires the following steps:
```
1) Based on NAND Flash characteristics (PWID bit indicates NAND Flash data bus width, PTYP=1, set
```
```
PWAITEN=0 or 1 as required; For timing configuration, refer to Section 40.4.2: NAND Flash Address
```
```
Mapping), configure the FMC_PCR and FMC_PMEM registers (for certain devices, configure the
```
```
R32_FMC_PATT register; refer to Section 40.6.5: NAND Flash Pre-Wait Function). This process configures
```
and enables the corresponding storage regions.
```
2) The CPU performs a byte write operation to the general memory space, where the data byte equals one Flash
```
```
command byte (e.g., 0x00 for Samsung NAND Flash devices). During the write enable period (a low-level
```
```
pulse on NWE), the LE input of the NAND Flash is active. Consequently, the written byte is interpreted as a
```
command for the NAND Flash. Once this command is latched by the memory device, it need not be rewritten
during subsequent page read operations.
```
3) By writing the four bytes STARTAD[7:0], STARTAD[16:9], STARTAD[24:17], and STARTAD[25] (for
```
```
64Mb*8-bit NAND Flash) into the general memory space or feature space (three bytes for smaller capacity
```
```
devices), the CPU can send the start address (STARTAD) for the read operation. During the write enable
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 900
```
period (a low-level pulse on NWE), the ALE input of the NAND Flash device is active, causing the written
```
byte to be treated as the starting address for the read operation. Utilizing the feature memory space, an
alternative timing configuration of the FMC can be employed to implement the pre-wait functionality
```
required by certain NAND Flash devices (for details, refer to Section 40.6.5: NAND Flash Pre-Wait
```
```
Functionality).
```
```
4) The controller waits for the NAND Flash to become ready (R/NB signal high) before initiating a new access
```
to the same or another storage area. During this wait period, the controller maintains the NCE signal active
```
(low).
```
```
5) The CPU can then execute byte-read operations from general memory space, thereby reading NAND Flash
```
```
pages (data field + spare field) byte by byte.
```
```
6) The next NAND Flash page can be read without any CPU command or address write operation. This can be
```
achieved in three distinct ways:
- Perform the operation described in Step 5
- Randomly access a new address by restarting the operation in Step 3
- Send a new command to the NAND Flash device by restarting Step 2
40.6.5 NAND Flash Pre-waiting Function
Some NAND Flash devices need the controller to wait for the R/NB signal to go low after writing the last part of
the address, as shown in the following figure.

However, all read or write accesses to NAND Flash by the CPU incur a hold delay of (MEMHOLD + 1) HCLK
```
```
cycles (inserted between the rising edge of the NWE signal and the next access).
```
To overcome this timing constraint, use the feature memory space. Program its timing register with an ATTHOLD
value that satisfies the tWB timing and maintain MEMHOLD at its minimum value. Subsequently, the CPU must
perform all NAND Flash read and write operations using the general memory space, except when writing the last
address byte to the NAND Flash device. In this case, the CPU must execute a write operation to the feature
memory space.

40.6.6 Error Correction Code (ECC) Calculation (NAND Flash)
```
```
The FMC NAND card controller incorporates two error correction code (ECC) calculation hardware modules, one
```
for each storage area. These modules reduce the host CPU workload during software-based ECC processing.
Both ECC modules are identical and associated with storage areas 2 and 3, respectively. Consequently, hardware
ECC calculations do not apply to memory connected to storage area 4.
During read or write operations to NAND Flash, the ECC algorithm employed in the FMC corrects single-bit
errors and detects double-bit errors for every 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, or 8192 bytes. This operation is based
on the Hamming code algorithm and includes the calculation of row and column parity.
Whenever the NAND Flash storage area is active, the ECC module monitors the NAND Flash data bus and
```
read/write signals (NCE and NWE).
```
ECC operates as follows:
 When accessing NAND Flash memory regions 2 or 3, it latches data appearing on the D[15:0] bus and uses it
for ECC computation.
 When accessing any other address in the NAND Flash, the ECC logic enters idle state and performs no
operation. Therefore, write operations defining NAND Flash commands or addresses are invalid during ECC
computation.
After the host CPU completes the read/write operation for the required number of bytes to the NAND Flash, it
must read the R32_FMC_ECCR register to retrieve the computed value. Following this read operation, these
registers should be cleared by resetting the ECCEN bit to zero. To compute a new data block, the ECCEN bit in
the FMC_PCR register must be set to 1.
To perform ECC calculation:
```
1) Enable the ECCEN bit in the R32_FMC_PCR register.
```
```
2) Write data to the NAND Flash page. During NAND page write, the ECC module calculates the ECC value.
```
```
3) Read the ECC value provided in the R32_FMC_ECCR register and store it in a variable.
```
```
4) Clear and then enable the ECCEN bit in the R32_FMC_PCR register. Read back the written data from the
```
NAND page. During the NAND page read operation, the ECC module will compute the ECC value.
```
5) Read the new ECC value provided in the R32_FMC_ECCR register.
```
```
6) If the two read ECC values match, no correction is needed. Otherwise, an ECC error exists, and the software
```
correction routine will return information indicating whether the error can be corrected.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 902

40.7 SDRAM Controller
40.7.1 Main Features of SDRAM Controller
The main features of SDRAM controller are as follows:
 Support word, half-word, and byte access
 Power-down mode
 CAS delays 1, 2, 3
 Self-refresh mode
 Programmable timing parameters
 Software-configurable SDRAM power-up initialization
 2 independently configurable SDRAM storage regions
 Multi-region ping-pong access
 SDRAM clock can be HCLK, HCLK/2, or HCLK/3
 Supports automatic refresh operation with programmable refresh rate
 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit memory data bus width
 Automatic storage region boundary management
```
 Read FIFO cache with 6 lines × 32-bit depth (6 × 14-bit address tags)
```
```
 13-bit address row, 11-bit address column, 4 internal storage regions: 4*16M*32bit (256MB), 4*16M*16bit
```
```
(128MB), 4*16M*8bit (64MB)
```

must be configured through the user application. Unused SDRAM controller I/O pins of application programs can
be used for other purposes.

40.7.3 SDRAM Controller Function Description
```
All SDRAM controller outputs (signal, address and data) can be configured to change on the falling edge of the
```
```
memory clock (FMC_SDCLK).
```
SDRAM initialization
The initialization sequence is managed by software. If 2 memory regions are used, the target memory region bits
CTB1 and CTB2 in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register must be set to 1, and the initialization sequences for memory
region 1 and memory region 2 must be generated at the same time:
```
1) Program the memory device characteristics into the R32_FMC_SDCRx registers. The SDRAM clock
```
frequency, RBURST, and RPIPE characteristics must be programmed into the R32_FMC_SDCR1 register.
```
2) Program the memory device timing into the R32_FMC_SDTRx registers. TRP and TRC timing must be
```
programmed into the R32_FMC_SDTR1 register.
```
3) Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to “001” and configure the target memory region bits
```
```
(CTB1 and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to begin clocking the memory (SDCKE driven high).
```
```
4) Wait for the specified delay cycle. Typical delay is 100μs.
```
```
5) Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to “010” and configure the target memory area bits (CTB1
```
```
and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to send the “Full Precharge” command.
```
```
6) Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to “011” and configure the target storage area (CTB1
```
```
and/or CTB2) and the number of Non-Repeatable Automatic Refresh (NRFS) commands in the
```
R32_FMC_SDCMR register.
```
7) Configure the MRD field according to the SDRAM device. Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register
```
```
to “100” and configure the target storage area bits (CTB1 and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to
```
send the “Load Mode Register” command and program the SDRAM device. Specifically:
```
a) The CAS delay must be selected based on the value in R32_FMC_SDCR1/2;
```
```
b) The burst length (BL) must be set to 1 by configuring the MRD[2:0] bits in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to
```
000.
If the mode registers for the two SDRAM storage regions differ, this step must be repeated twice—once for each
storage region—with the corresponding target storage region bit set to 1.
```
8) Program the refresh rate in the R32_FMC_SDRTR register. The refresh rate corresponds to the delay between
```
refresh cycles. Its value must be compatible with the SDRAM device.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 908
At this stage, the SDRAM device is ready to receive commands. If a system reset occurs during an SDRAM
access, the data bus may still be driven by the SDRAM device. Therefore, the SDRAM device must be
reinitialized after reset before the NOR Flash/PSRAM/SRAM or NAND Flash controller can issue new access
commands.
```
Note: If two SDRAM devices are connected to the FMC, simultaneous access to both devices via the command
```
```
mode register (loading the mode register command) will issue access commands based on the timing parameters
```
```
(TMRD and TRAS timing) configured for SDRAM memory region 1 in the R32_FMC_SDTR1 register.
```
SDRAM controller write cycle
SDRAM controller can receive single and burst write requests and treat them as a single memory access. In both
cases, the SDRAM controller will track the valid lines of each storage area, so as to be able to make continuous
```
write access to different storage areas (multi-storage area ping-pong access). Before performing any write access,
```
the WP bit in R32_FMC_SDCRx register must be cleared to prohibit write protection of SDRAM storage area.
The SDRAM controller always checks for the next access:
```
1) If the next access occurs on the same row or another valid row, the write operation proceeds directly.
```
```
2) If the next access points to an invalid row, the SDRAM controller generates a precharge command, activates
```
the new row, and initializes the write command.

SDRAM controller read cycle
SDRAM controller can receive single and burst read requests and treat them as a single memory access. In both
cases, the SDRAM controller will track the valid lines of each storage area, so as to be able to perform continuous
```

The FMC SDRAM controller features a cacheable read FIFO (6 lines × 32 bits) that pre-fetches read data during
```
CAS latency cycles and RPIPE delays according to the following formula. The RBURST bit in the
R32_FMC_SDCR1 register must be set to 1 to accept the next read access. Expected data count = CAS latency +
```
1 + (RPIPE latency) / 2, example:
```
```
 CAS latency = 3, RPIPE latency = 0: Four data items (uncommitted) stored in the FIFO.
```
```
 CAS latency = 3, RPIPE latency = 2: Five data items (uncommitted) stored in the FIFO.
```
Each row in the read FIFO has a 14-bit address tag to identify its contents: 11 bits for the column address, 2 bits
for selecting the internal memory region and valid row, and 1 bit for selecting the SDRAM device. During HB
```
burst reads, if the end of the row is reached prematurely, the data read ahead (not yet committed) is not stored in
```
the read FIFO. For single read accesses, the data is correctly stored in the read FIFO.
Whenever a read request occurs, the SDRAM controller checks:
 Whether the address matches one of the address tags. If a match is found, data is read directly from the FIFO,
the corresponding address tag/row content is cleared, and the remaining data in the FIFO is compressed to
avoid empty rows.
 Otherwise, a new read command is sent to memory and the FIFO is updated with the new data. If the FIFO is
full, earlier data will be lost.

During a read access or precharge command, the read FIFO will refresh and prepare to fill with new data.
Upon receiving the first read request, if the current access has not yet reached a row boundary, the SDRAM
```
controller will accept the next read access during the CAS latency cycle and RPIPE latency (if configured). This is
```
achieved by incrementing the memory address. The following conditions must be met:
 The RBURST control bit in the R32_FMC_SDCR1 register must be set to 1
Address management depends on the next HB request:
```
 The next HB request is consecutive (HB burst)
```
In this case, the SDRAM controller will increment the address.
 The next HB request is not consecutive
- If the new read request targets the same row as the previous request or another valid row, the new
address is transmitted to the memory while the master device halts operations during the CAS latency
period, awaiting new data from the memory.
- If the new read request targets an invalid row, the SDRAM controller generates a precharge command,
activates the new row, and initializes the read command.
If RURST is set to 0, the read FIFO is not used.
Row and storage area boundary management
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 911
When a read/write access crosses a row boundary, if the next read/write access is continuous and the current
access has been executed to the row boundary, the SDRAM controller will perform the following operations:
```
1) Precharge the active row;
```
```
2) Activate the new row;
```
```
3) Initiate the read/write command.
```
For all column and data bus width configurations, automatic row activation at row boundaries is supported.
The SDRAM controller may insert additional clock cycles between the following commands as required:
```
 Inserted between the precharge and activate commands to match the TRP parameter (only when the next
```
```
access targets another row within the same memory area).
```
 Inserted between the activate and read commands to match the TRCD parameter.
These parameters are defined in the FMC_SDTRx register.
For information on row boundary crossing reads and burst write accesses, refer to the diagram below.

If the next access is continuous and the current access crosses the storage area boundary, the SDRAM controller
will activate the first row of the next storage area and issue a new read/write command. There are two possible
```
situations:
```
 If the current memory area is not the last memory area, the active row in the new memory area must be
precharged. For various row/column and data bus width configurations, the automatic activation of the next
row at the boundary of the storage area is supported.
 If the current storage area is the last storage area, the automatic activation of the next row is only supported
when addressing SDRAM devices with 13-bit rows, 11-bit columns, 4 internal storage areas and 32-bit data
bus. Otherwise, SDRAM address range will be violated and HB error will be generated.
 For the SDRAM memory with 13-bit row address, 11-column address, 4 internal storage areas and 32-bit bus
width, the SDRAM controller will continue the read/write operation through the second SDRAM device
```
(assuming that the second SDRAM device is initialized):
```
- The SDRAM controller will activate the first row (assuming that there is a valid row in the first internal
```
storage area after precharging the valid row) and issue a new read/write command;
```
- If the first row is activated, the SDRAM controller will only issue read/write commands.
SDRAM controller refresh cycle
The automatic refresh command is used to refresh the contents of SDRAM devices. SDRAM controller will send
automatic refresh command periodically. It uses an internal COUNTer to load the count value in the
```
R32_FMC_SDRTR register. This value defines the number of memory clock cycles (refresh rate) between refresh
```
cycles. When the value of the counter reaches zero, an internal pulse will be generated.
If there is an ongoing memory access, the automatic refresh request will be delayed. However, when memory
access and automatic refresh request occur at the same time, the automatic refresh request is given priority.
If the memory is accessed during the automatic refresh, the access request is cached and processed after the
automatic refresh is completed.
If a new automatic refresh request appears when the last automatic refresh request has not been completed, the RE
```
(refresh error) bit in the status register will be set to 1. If this bit is enabled (REIE=1), an interrupt will be
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 913
generated.
```
If the SDRAM rows are not idle (not all rows are closed), the SDRAM controller will generate a PALL
```
```
(pre-charge all) command before automatic refresh.
```
```
If the automatic refresh command is generated by the R32_FMC_SDCMR command mode register (mode bit =
```
```
"011"), the PALL command (mode bit = "010") must be issued first.
```
40.7.4 Low-power Mode
2 low-power modes are available:
 Self-Refresh Mode
The SDRAM device performs automatic refresh cycles to retain data without requiring an external clock.
 Power-Down Mode
The SDRAM controller performs automatic refresh cycles.
Self-refresh mode
```
This mode is selected by setting the MODE position to '101' and configuring the target storage area bits (CTB1
```
```
and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register.
```
The SDRAM clock ceases operation after the TRAS delay, while the internal refresh timer only stops counting
when one of the following conditions is met:
 A self-refresh command was issued to both devices.
```
 One of the devices was not activated (the SDRAM storage area was not initialized).
```
Before entering self-refresh mode, the SDRAM controller automatically issues a PALL command.
If the write data FIFO is not empty, all data will be sent to memory before self-refresh mode activates, and the
BUSY status flag remains set to 1.
In self-refresh mode, all inputs to the SDRAM device are invalid except for SDCKE, which must remain low.
SDRAM devices must remain in self-refresh mode for a minimum duration equal to the TRAS time and must be
capable of sustaining self-refresh mode for extended periods. To ensure this minimum duration, the BUSY status
flag remains high throughout the TRAS delay period following self-refresh activation.
The SDRAM controller immediately generates a command sequence to exit self-refresh mode upon selection of
an SDRAM device. After memory access completes, the selected device remains in normal mode.
```
To exit self-refresh mode, the MODE bit must be set to “000” (normal mode) and the target storage area bits
```
```
(CTB1 and/or CTB2) within the R32_FMC_SDCMR register must be configured.
```

If the write data FIFO is not empty, all data will be sent to memory before power-down mode is activated.
The SDRAM controller will exit power-down mode immediately after an SDRAM device is selected. After
memory access completes, the selected SDRAM device will remain in normal mode.
During power-down mode, all input/output buffers of the SDRAM device will be disabled, except for SDCKE,
which remains low.
SDRAM devices can't stay in power-down mode for longer than refresh cycle, and they can't perform self-refresh
cycle. Therefore, the SDRAM controller performs refresh by:
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 915
```
1) Exit power-down mode and drive SDCKE high.
```
```
2) Generate the PALL command. (provided an activation line exists in power-down mode)
```
```
3) Generate an auto-refresh command
```
```
4) Drive SDCKE low again to return to power-down mode.
```
```
To exit power-down mode, the MODE bit must be set to “000” (normal mode) and the target storage area bits
```
```
(CTB1 and/or CTB2) must be configured in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register.
```

Chapter 41 Encryption Module (ECDC)
```
The system has built-in block cipher algorithm module, which supports AES and SM4 block cipher algorithms
```
and electronic codebook (ECB) and counter (CTR) modes. The module completes one encryption and decryption
```
process with 128-bit data size as the basic unit, and provides a DMA encryption and decryption mode for data in
memory and a single encryption and decryption mode for SFR registers.
41.1 Main Features
 ECB and CTR modes for SM4 algorithm with 128-bit keys
 ECB and CTR modes for AES algorithm with 128/192/256-bit keys
 Support direct encryption of individual 128-bit data via software writing to SFRs
```
 Support DMA-based (memory-to-memory) encryption/decryption of software-specified data blocks
```
41.2 AES/SM4 Algorithm
```
The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm is a block cipher that employs a symmetric block cipher
```
system, ranking among the most widely used symmetric-key encryption algorithms. The SM4 block cipher
```
algorithm is typically a dedicated block cipher designed for wireless local area networks (WLANs) and trusted
```
computing environments, though it can also be utilized for data encryption protection in other contexts.
During data encryption and decryption, keys must be loaded. For the AES algorithm, depending on the key length
set to 128/192/256 bits, the user key must be expanded into an expansion key of 11×128/13×128/15×128 bits,
respectively. In contrast, the SM4 algorithm expands a 128-bit user key into a 32×32-bit expanded key. These
expanded keys are stored in internal registers for convenient access during encryption and decryption operations.
41.3 ECB and CTR Mode
```
AES/SM4 supports two modes, electronic codebook (ECB) mode and counter (CTR) mode, in which the security
```
performance of CTR mode is higher than that of ECB mode. As shown in figure 41-1 and 41-2 working block
diagram.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 925

```
In ECB mode, plaintext and ciphertext are directly mapped one-to-one; the plaintext is encrypted verbatim to
```
produce the ciphertext. In CTR mode, however, a 128-bit counter must be preloaded. This counter is encrypted,
and the encrypted counter is then XORed with the plaintext to generate the ciphertext. It is important to note that
in CTR decryption mode, only the counter is encrypted—it is not decrypted.
41.4 Module Application
41.4.1 Initialization of Encryption and Decryption Module
 Clock configuration: set RB_ECDC_CLKDIV_MASK bit in R32_ECEC_CTRL register to configure the
clock for module operation. If you don't use this module, you can set it to 0 and turn it off to reduce power
consumption.
 Data size end: set RB_ECDC_DAT_MOD bit of R32_ECEC_CTRL register, and you can choose the storage
```
mode of the size end of the encrypted and decrypted data. According to the size of a packet of 128bits(16
```
```
bytes).
```
 Key Expansion: During encryption and decryption, an expansion key is used instead of the user key. After
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 926
setting the user key length and content, the hardware must be instructed to perform key expansion. Once
expanded, the key is stored in the module's internal registers. Only then can normal data encryption and
decryption proceed. Configure the R32_ECEC_CTRL register: set RB_ECDC_WRSRAM_EN,
RB_ECDC_ALGRM_MOD, RB_ECDC_CIPHER_MOD, and RB_ECDC_KLEN_MASK to enable SRAM
data encryption/decryption, select the encryption/decryption algorithm, specify the block cipher mode, and
define the key length. Then configure the user key register group R32_ECDC_KEY by populating it with the
user key content. After setting RB_ECDC_KEYEX_EN in the R32_ECEC_CTRL register to 1 and then
clearing it to 0, the hardware initiates the key expansion function.
 Initial counter value: When using CTR mode for encryption/decryption, an initial counter value is required.
Set the 128-bit counter value in the CTR mode counter register group R32_ECDC_IV. Each successful
```
completion of a data encryption/decryption cycle (128-bit data) increments the internal counter value by 1.
```
This counter value is not needed in ECB mode.
41.4.2 Encryption and Decryption Configuration
The encryption and decryption data flow of the module includes two ways: memory to memory and one-time
encryption and decryption of 128-bit data. Please refer to the configuration in Table 41-1 for details.

Memory-to-memory data conversion begins when non-zero data is written to the R32_ECDC_SRAM_LEN length
register. By checking the RB_ECDC_IF_WRSRAM bit in the R32_ECDC_INT_FG register, a value of 1
indicates the memory-to-memory data conversion is complete, clearing the RB_ECDC_IF_WRSRAM bit status.
If the RB_ECDC_IE_WRSRAM function in the R32_ECDC_CTRL register is enabled, an interrupt service is
triggered simultaneously with setting the RB_ECDC_IF_WRSRAM flag.
```
Single-pass encryption/decryption must be configured in big-endian mode (RB_ECDC_DAT_MOD=1) for
```
execution. The single-pass encryption/decryption conversion of 128-bit data begins with a write operation to the
upper 32 bits of the R32_ECDC_SGSD register. By checking the RB_ECDC_IF_SINGLE bit in the
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 927
R32_ECDC_INT_FG register, a value of 1 indicates completion of the single 128-bit data conversion, clearing the
RB_ECDC_IF_SINGLE bit status. If the RB_ECDC_IE_SINGLE function in the R32_ECDC_CTRL register is
enabled, an interrupt service is triggered simultaneously with the setting of the RB_ECDC_IF_SINGLE flag.

Chapter 42 Digital Filter for ΣΔ Modulator (DFSDM)
```
DFSDM is a high-performance module dedicated to connecting external ΣΔ modulator to MCU. It contains two
external digital serial interfaces and 2 digital filters, and has flexible ΣΔ digital processing options, which can
provide the final resolution of ADC up to 24 bits. DFSDM can also select parallel data stream input from internal
ADC peripherals or device memory.
42.1 Main Features
 Provide 2 multiplexed digital serial input channels
 2 internal digital parallel channels supporting optional inputs
 Support adjustable digital signal processing
 Support up to 24-bit output data resolution
 Support signed data formats
```
 Support automatic data offset correction (offset value stored by user in register)
```
 Include 2 conversion modes: single conversion mode and continuous conversion mode
 Conversion initiation supported via software trigger, internal timer, external event, or synchronization with
the first DFSDM filter
 Supports analog watchdog
```
 Built-in short-circuit detector to identify saturated analog input values (lower and upper limits)
```
 Support open-circuit generation upon analog watchdog events and short-circuit monitoring events
 Built-in extreme value detector
 Support interrupts and DMA

42.3 Function Description
42.3.1 DFSDM Reset and Clock
DFSDM Switch Control
Global enablement of the DFSDM interface is achieved by setting the DFSDMEN bit in the
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register to 1. Once the DFSDM interface is globally enabled, all configured input
```
channels y (y=0/1) and digital filters DFSDM_FLTx (x=0/1) will begin operation when their respective enable bits
```
```
(channel enable bit CHEN in R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 and DFSDM_FLTx enable bit DFEN in
```
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1) are set to 1.
```
```
The digital filter DFSDM_FLTx (x=0/1) is enabled by setting DFEN in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register to 1.
```
```
After enabling DFSDM_FLTx (DFEN=1), the Sincx digital filter unit and integrator unit will be reinitialized.
```
Clearing DFEN immediately halts all ongoing conversions and places DFSDM_FLTx into stop mode. All register
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 934
settings remain unchanged except for R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR and R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR, which are reset.
```
Enable channel y (y=0/1) by setting CHEN in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register to 1. Once a channel is
```
```
enabled, serial data is received from an external ΣΔ modulator or a parallel internal data source (CPU/DMA write
```
```
operations to ADCs or memory).
```
```
Before stopping the system clock and entering stop mode, the DFSDM must be globally disabled (by setting
```
```
DFSDMEN=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register).
```
DFSDM Clock
```
The internal DFSDM clock fDFSDMCLK drives channel transceivers, digital processing modules (including digital
```
```
filters and integrators), and subsequent auxiliary modules (such as analog watchdogs, short-circuit detectors,
```
```
extreme-value detectors, and control modules). This clock is generated by the RCC module, sourced from either
```
```
the peripheral clock HCLK or the audio clock. The DFSDM clock automatically stops in stop mode (when all
```
```
DFSDM_FLTx, x=0/1, and DFEN=0).
```
The DFSDM serial channel transceiver can accept an external serial clock to sample external serial data streams.
If standard SPI encoding is used, the internal DFSDM clock must be at least four times faster than the external
serial clock.
The DFSDM supports providing an external output clock signal to drive the clock input of an external ΣΔ
modulator. This output clock signal is delivered via the CKOUT pin. The frequency of the output clock signal
must fall within the range specified in the device manual and can be derived from either the DFSDM clock or the
```
audio clock (refer to the CKOUTSRC bit in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register) through a divider. The
```
```
programmable range of the divider is 2 to 256 (CKOUTDIV bit in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register). The
```
audio clock is obtained by selecting PLL_CLK via the SYSPLL_SEL[2:0] field in the RCC configuration, which
in turn configures PLLCLK.
42.3.2 Serial Channel Transceiver
This peripheral features 2 multiplexed serial data channels that can be selected for conversion via individual filters,
analog watchdogs, or short-circuit detectors. These serial transceivers receive data streams from external ΣΔ
```
modulators. Data streams can be transmitted in SPI format (refer to the SITP bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1
```
```
register).
```
The channel is enabled by setting the CHEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register to 1.
Channel Input Selection
```
Serial inputs (data and clock signals) for the DATINy and CKINy pins can be redirected from subsequent channel
```
pins. The redirection functionality for serial input channels is configured via the CHINSEL bit in the
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
```
Channel redirection can be used to acquire audio data from PDM (Pulse Density Modulation) stereo microphones.
```
A PDM stereo microphone contains one data signal and one clock signal, where the data signal provides
```
information for the left and right audio channels (sampling occurs on the rising edge of the clock for the left
```
```
channel and on the falling edge for the right channel).
```
```
Configuration of PDM microphone input serial channel;
```
```
 PDM microphone signals (data, clock) will be connected to the DFSDM input serial channel y (DATINy,
```
```
CKOUT) pins
```
```
 Configure channel y as follows: CHINSEL=0 (input from given channel pins: DATINy and CKINy)
```
```
 Configure channel (y-1) (mod 2) as follows:
```
```
CHINSEL=1 (input from subsequent channel ((y-1)+1) pins: DATINy and CKINy)
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 935
```
 Channel y: SITP=0 (data gated on rising edge) – left audio channel for channel y
```
```
 Channel (y-1): SITP=1 (data gated on falling edge) – right audio channel for channel (y-1)
```
```
 2 DFSDM filters will be assigned to channels y and (y-1) (for filtering left and right channels of PDM
```
```
microphones)
```

Clock Signal Output
A clock signal can be provided at the CKOUT pin to drive the clock input of an external ΣΔ modulator. The
```
CKOUT signal frequency is derived from either the DFSDM clock or the audio clock (refer to the CKOUTSRC
```
```
bit in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register) via a prescaler (refer to the CKOUTDIV bit in the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register). If the output clock is stopped, the CKOUT signal is placed in a low state
```
```
(the output clock can be stopped by setting CKOUTDIV=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register or by
```
```
setting DFSDMEN=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register). The output clock stop is executed at the
```
following times:
 When CKOUTSRC=0, 4 system clock cycles after DFSDMEN cleared
 When CKOUTSRC=1, one system clock cycle and three audio clock cycles after DFSDMEN is cleared.
 Before changing CKOUTSRC, the software must wait for CKOUT to stop to avoid glitch signals on the
CKOUT pin. The output clock signal frequency must be within the range of 0 to 20MHz.
Before changing CKOUTSRC, the software must wait for CKOUT to stop, so as to avoid generating glitch signal
on CKOUT pin. The frequency of the output clock signal must be in the range of 0 ~ 20MHz.
SPI Data Input Format Operation
In SPI format, data streams are transmitted in serial format through data and clock signals. The data signal is
always provided by the datum pin. The clock signal can be provided from the outside through CKINy pin or from
the inside through the signal from CKOUT signal source.
```
If an external clock source is selected (SPICKSEL[1:0]=0), the data signal is sampled (DATINy pin) on the rising
```
or falling edge of the clock according to the SITP bit setting in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
Internal clock source—refer to SPICKSEL[1:0] in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register:
 CKOUT signal:
- For connecting an external ΣΔ modulator, which directly uses its clock input (from CKOUT) to generate the
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 936
output serial communication clock.
- Sampling point: Rising edge/falling edge, depending on SITP settings.
```
 CKOUT/2 signal (generated on the rising edge of CKOUT):
```
- Used to connect an external ΣΔ modulator, which divides the clock input (from CKOUT) by 2 to generate the
output serial communication clock. This output clock is active on each rising edge of the clock input.
- Sampling point: Every second falling edge of CKOUT.
```
 CKOUT/2 signal (generated on the falling edge of CKOUT):
```
- Used to connect an external ΣΔ modulator, which divides the clock input (from CKOUT) by 2 to generate the
output serial communication clock. This output clock change is valid on each falling edge of the clock input.
- Sampling point: Every second rising edge of CKOUT.
```
Note: The internal clock source can only be used when an external ΣΔ modulator employs the CKOUT signal as
```
```
its clock input (to achieve synchronous clock and data operation). Using the internal clock source eliminates the
```
```
need for a CKINy pin connection (the CKINy pin can be repurposed for other functions). When using SPI
```
encoding, the clock source signal frequency must fall within the range of 0 to 20 MHz and be less than
fDFSDMCLK/4.

Clock Loss Detection
This feature detects the presence or absence of clock signals on channel serial clock inputs, ensuring proper
operation of conversion processes and error reporting. Clock absence detection is enabled or disabled for each
input channel y via the CKABEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register. If clock absence detection is
enabled for a given channel, it is continuously monitored. If an input clock error occurs, the clock loss flag is set
```
to 1 (CKABF[y]=1) and an interrupt is triggered (when CKABIE=1). After the clock miss flag is cleared (via
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 937
```
CLRCKABF in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0ICR register), the clock miss status bit CKABF[y] is reset. When the
```
```
corresponding channel y is disabled, CKABF[y] is additionally set to 1 by hardware (if CHEN[y]=0, CKABF[y]
```
```
remains set).
```
```
Upon occurrence of a clock-out event, the data conversion (and/or analog watchdog and short-circuit detector)
```
will provide erroneous data. When clock-out is reported, the user should handle this event and discard the
associated data.
```
The clock-out function is only available when the system clock is used for the CKOUT signal (CKOUTSRC=0 in
```
```
the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register).
```
When the transceiver is out of synchronization, the clock loss flag will be set and cannot be cleared via the
CLRCKABF[y] bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0ICR register. The software operation sequence associated with the
clock loss detection function should be as follows:
 Enable the specified channel by setting CHEN=1
```
 Attempt to clear the clock absent flag (by setting CLRCKABF=1) until the clock absent flag is actually
```
```
cleared (CKABF=0). At this point, the transceiver is synchronized (signal clock is valid) and capable of
```
receiving data
 Enable the clock absent function CKABEN=1 and the associated interrupt CKABIE=1 to detect whether the
SPI clock is lost
When using the SPI data format, clock loss detection is based on comparing the CKOUT signal generated from
the external input clock with the output clock. The external input clock signal in the input channel must change
```
once every 8 signal cycles of the CKOUT signal (controlled by the CKOUTDIV field in the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register).
```

```
If a clock recovery error occurs during input, the clock absent flag is set to 1 (CKABF[y]=1) and an interrupt is
```
```
triggered (when CKABIE=1). After the clock absent flag is cleared (via CLRCKABF in the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_FLT0ICR register), the clock absent flag is reset.
```
External Serial Clock Frequency Measurement
By measuring the serial clock input frequency of the channel, the data rate from the external ΣΔ modulator can be
obtained in real time, which is critical for application purposes.
```
The external serial clock input frequency can be measured using a timer that counts the DFSDM clock (fDFSDMCLK)
```
```
over one conversion duration. Counting begins at the first input data clock following conversion triggering (either
```
```
normal or injected) and ends at the last input data clock before conversion completion (when the conversion end
```
```
flag is set to 1). Upon conversion completion (JEOCF=1 or REOCF=1), the time per conversion (the interval
```
```
between the first and last serial samples) is updated in the CNVCNT[27:0] counter of register
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCNVTIMR. The user can then calculate the data rate based on the digital filter settings
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 938
```
(FORD, FOSR, IOSR, FAST). External serial frequency measurement ceases only when the filter is bypassed
```
```
(FOSR=0, only the integrator is active, and CNVCNT[27:0] in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCNVTIMR register equals
```
```
0).
```
```
For parallel data input (see Section 42.3.4: Parallel Data Input), the measured frequency represents the average
```
input data rate during a single conversion.
```
Note: When a conversion is interrupted (e.g., by disabling/enabling the selected channel), the interruption
```
duration is also counted in CNVCNT[27:0]. Therefore, to obtain accurate conversion timing results, it is
recommended not to interrupt conversions. It is recommended to measure the clock in continuous fast mode.
Conversion time:
```
Injection conversion or regular conversion at FAST=0 (or first conversion at FAST=1):
```
```
For Sincx filters (x=1..5):
```
```
t=CNVCNT/fDFSDMCLK=[FOSR*(2IOSR+FORD+1)+2]/fCKIN
```
For FastSinc filters:
```
t = CNVCNT/fDFSDMCLK = [FOSR*(FOSR*(2IOSR+5)+2)]/fCKIN
```
```
Regular conversion when FAST=1 (except first conversion):
```
For Sincx and FastSinc filters:
```
t = CNVCNT/fDFSDMCLK = [FOSR*2IOSR]/fCKIN
```
```
If FOSR=FOSR[9:0]+1=1 (filter bypassed, only integrator active), then:
```
```
t=2IOSR/fCKIN (...but CNVCNT=0)
```
Among them:
```
1) fCKIN is the channel input clock frequency (at the CKINy pin of the given channel) or the input data rate (for
```
```
parallel data input);
```
```
2) FOSR is the filter oversampling rate: FOSR = FOSR[9:0] + 1 (refer to the R32_DFSDM_FLTxFCR register);
```
```
3) 2IOSR is the integrator oversampling rate (refer to the R32_DFSDM_FLTxFCR register);
```
```
4) FORD is the filter order: FORD = FORD[2:0] (refer to the R32_DFSDM_FLTxFCR register).
```
Channel Offset Settings
```
Each channel has its own offset setting (in the register), which will eventually be subtracted from each conversion
```
```
result (injection or normal) of a given channel. Offset correction is performed after the data is shifted to the right.
```
The offset value is stored as a 24-bit signed value in the OFFSET[23:0] field of R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2
register.
Right Shift of Data
To align the result with a 24-bit value, each channel defines a series of right shifts that will be applied to each
```
conversion result (injection or normal) of a given channel. The right shift number is stored in bits DTRBS[4:0] of
```
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register.
Shift right rounds the result to the nearest integer value. The sign of the shifted result is preserved, so as to obtain
the result data in a valid 24-bit signed format.
42.3.3 Configuration Input Serial Interface
The following parameters must be configured for the input serial interface:
```
 Output clock prescaler. With the programmable prescaler, the output clock (range 2 to 256) can be generated
```
from the DFSDM clock. This setting is determined by the CKOUTDIV[7:0] bits in the
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 939
 Type of serial interface and clock phase when input. Select SPI interface and sampling edge of input clock.
This option is specified by the SITP bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
 Input clock source selection. You can select an external source from the CKINy pin or an internal source
from the CKOUT pin. This selection is determined by the spikesel [1: 0] fields in the
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
 Final data right shift setting. Defines the right shift number of the final data to ensure that the result is aligned
with the 24-bit value. This configuration is defined by the DTRBS[4:0] bits in the
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register.
```
 Channel offset configuration. Set the analog offset (that is, the offset of the connected external σ δ modulator)
```
for a specific serial channel. This value is set by bits OFFSET[23:0] in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2
register.
 Channel short detector and activation of clock missing function. In the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register,
the short-circuit detector of a given serial channel is enabled or disabled by the SCDEN bit, and the clock
missing detection is enabled or disabled by the CKABEN bit.
 Threshold configuration of analog watchdog filter and short circuit detector. Used to set the parameters of
channel analog watchdog filter and channel short circuit detector. These configurations are defined in the
R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register.
42.3.4 Parallel Data Input
```
Each input channel provides a register for 16-bit parallel data input (except serial data input). Each 16-bit parallel
```
input can only come from an internal data source:
```
 Internal ADC results (ADC1 and ADC2 only)
```
 Direct CPU/DMA write operation
Use the DATMPX[1:0] field of R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register to select whether to use serial or parallel data
input for a given channel. DATMPX[1:0] also defines parallel data source: internal ADC or write operation
directly by CPU/DMA.
```
Each channel contains a 32-bit data input register (R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR), in which 16 bits of data can be
```
written. The data is in a 16-bit signed format. These data can also be used as the input of a digital filter that
accepts 16-bit parallel data.
```
If serial data input is selected (DATMPX[1:0]=0), the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register is write-protected.
```
```
Input from internal ADC (ADC1 and ADC2 only)
```
```
For parallel ADC data inputs (DATMPX[1:0]=1), the ADC[y+1] result is assigned to channel y input (ADC1
```
```
populates the R32_DFSDM_CH0DATINR register, ADC2 populates the R32_DFSDM_CH1DATINR register).
```
```
The conversion complete event from ADC[y+1] triggers an update to channel y's data (the parallel data from
```
```
ADC[y+1] is used as the next sample for the digital filter). When the conversion complete event occurs, the data
```
```
from ADC[y+1] is written to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register (the INDAT0[15:0] field).
```
```
The data packing mode setting (DATPACK[1:0] in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register) has no effect on the
```
ADC data input.
```
Note: ADC Extension Specification: When the internal ADC is configured in interleaved mode (e.g., ADC1
```
```
interleaved with ADC2 - refer to ADC specification), each result from ADC1 or ADC2 is transmitted to the same
```
```
16-bit bus (i.e., ADC1's bus), which is connected to DFSDM Channel 0 (fixed connection). Therefore, DFSDM
```
```
channel 0 will carry double the input data rate (even samples from ADC1, odd samples from ADC2). Channel 1,
```
associated with ADC2, will remain idle.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 940
```
Input from memory (written directly by CPU/DMA)
```
```
When CPU or DMA(DATMPX[1:0]=2) directly writes data into R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register, these data
```
can be used as input to process digital data streams from memory or peripherals.
Data can be written into R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register by CPU or DMA:
```
1) CPU data writing:
```
Input data is directly written into R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register by CPU.
```
2) DMA data writing:
```
DMA should be configured as a memory-to-memory transfer mode to transfer the data in the buffer area of the
memory to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. The target memory address is the address of the
R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. Data is transferred from memory to DFSDM parallel input at DMA transfer
speed.
This DMA is different from the DMA used to read the conversion result of DFSDM. These two DMA's can be
```
used at the same time. The first DMA (configured as memory-to-memory transfer) is used for input data writing,
```
```
and the second DMA (configured as peripheral-to-memory transfer) is used for data result reading.
```
The access to R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR can be 16-bit or 32-bit wide, allowing one or two samples to be loaded
```
in one write operation, respectively. The 32-bit input data register (R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR) can be filled
```
with one or two 16-bit data samples, depending on the data packing operation mode defined in the DATPACK[1:0]
field of R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register:
```
1) Standard Mode (DATPACK[1:0]=00b):
```
Only one sample is stored in the INDAT0[15:0] field of the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register, serving as input
```
data for channel y. The upper 16 bits (INDAT1[15:0]) are ignored and write-protected. The digital filter must
```
```
perform one input sample (via INDAT0[15:0]) to clear the data register after CPU/DMA fill. This mode combines
```
with 16-bit CPU/DMA access to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register to load one sample per write operation.
```
2) Interleaved Mode (DATPACK[1:0]=01b):
```
The R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register functions as two sample buffers. The first sample is stored in
INDAT0[15:0], and the second sample is stored in INDAT1[15:0]. The digital filter must perform two input
samples through channel y to clear the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. This mode is combined with 32-bit
CPU/DMA access to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register to load two samples per write operation.
```
3) Dual-Channel Mode (DATPACK[1:0]=10b):
```
Write 2 samples into the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. Data in INDAT0[15:0] is used for channel y, while
data in INDAT1[15:0] is used for channel y+1. Data in INDAT1[15:0] is automatically copied to INDAT0[15:0]
```
of the next (y+1) channel data register (DFSDM_CH[y+1]DATINR). The digital filter must perform two samples
```
```
(one from channel y and one from channel (y+1)) to clear the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register.
```
```
Dual-channel mode configuration (DATPACK[1:0]=10b) is only possible for even channel numbers (y=0). If an
```
```
odd channel (y=1) is set to dual-channel mode, both the INDAT0[15:0] and INDAT1[15:0] sections for that
```
channel are write-protected. If an even channel is set to dual-channel mode, the next odd channel must be set to
```
standard mode (DATPACK[1:0]=00b) to properly interface with the even channel.
```
Please refer to the figure below for the data mode of R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register and the allocation of
channel data samples.

First enable the selected input channel (channel y) to initiate data acquisition (starting conversion for channel y).
```
Then, a write operation to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register is required to load one or two samples. Failure
to do so will result in the loss of written data during subsequent processing.
For example: In single conversion and interleaved mode, do not begin writing paired data samples to

R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR before initiating the single conversion (any data present in
```
```

```
42.3.5 Channel Selection
There are 2 multiplex channels, which can be selected for injection channel group conversion and/or conventional
channel conversion.
The injection channel group can select any or all of the 2 channels. JCHG[1:0] in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxJCHGR
register selects the injection group channel, where JCHG[y]=1 indicates that channel y has been selected.
```
Injection conversion can work in scan mode (JSCAN=1) or single mode (JSCAN=0). In scan mode, each selected
```
```
channel will be converted in turn. The lowest channel (channel 0, if selected) is converted first, and then the next
```
```
higher channel is converted until all channels selected by JCHG[1:0] are converted. In single mode (JSCAN=0),
```
only one selected channel will be converted, and the channel selection will be moved to the next channel. When
```
JSCAN=0, writing to JCHG[1:0] will reset the channel selection to the lowest channel selected.
```
Injection conversion can be initiated by software or triggers. Such transformations are never interrupted by regular
transformations.
Conventional channels only select one of the two channels. The RCH bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register
indicates the selected channel.
```
General transformations can only be initiated by software (not by triggers). When an injection transformation is
```
requested, the continuous regular transformation sequence is temporarily interrupted.
```
Attempting a conversion on a disabled channel (CHEN=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register) will cause
```
```
the conversion to never complete, as no input data is provided (no clock signal). In this case, either enable the
```
```
given channel (CHEN=1 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register) or stop the conversion (by setting DFEN=0
```
```
in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register).
```
42.3.6 Digital Filter Configuration
DFSDM includes a Sincx-type digital filter implementation. This Sincx filter performs filtering on the input digital
```
data stream, resulting in a reduced output data rate (decimation) and increased output data resolution. The Sincx
```
digital filter can be configured to achieve the desired output data rate and desired output data resolution.
Configurable parameters include:

- FastSinc

- Sinc3

- FOSR=1-215——Applicable to Sincx filters where x=FORD=4
- FOSR=1-73——Applicable to Sincx filters where x=FORD=5

The filter supports the following transfer functions (impulse response in the H domain):
