42.3.8 Analog Watchdog
```
The analog watchdog is used to trigger an external signal (open circuit or interrupt) when it reaches or exceeds a
```
given upper threshold or reaches or falls below a given lower threshold. Interrupt/event/open circuit generation
can then be invoked.
```
Each analog watchdog monitors the serial data receiver output (after the watchdog filter is simulated on each
```
```
channel) or the data output register (current injection or general conversion result) according to the AWFSEL bit
```
```
setting (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register). Whether the input channels need to be monitored by analog
```
watchdog X can be selected by AWDCH[1:0] in R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register.
Analog watchdog conversions on input channels are independent of standard conversions. In standard conversion
mode, the analog watchdog employs its own filter and signal processing on each input channel, unaffected by
injection or regular master conversions. In continuous conversion mode, analog watchdog conversions are
performed on selected input channels to maintain channel monitoring even when injection or regular master
```
conversions are paused (RCIP=0, JCIP=0).
```
```
The upper threshold and lower threshold registers are compared against a given data value (set via the
```
AWHT[23:0] bits of the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWHTR register and the AWLT[23:0] bits of the
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWLTR register).
```
You can choose two situations to compare the threshold register with the data value:
```
 Option 1: In this case, the input data is taken from the final output data register (AWFSEL=0). This choice
```
has the following characteristics:
- High input data resolution (up to 24 bits)
- Slow response time—not suitable for fast-response applications such as overcurrent detection
- For comparison purposes, final data requires shift and offset correction
- Final data becomes available only after executing a normal or injected main conversion
- Operates with parallel input data sources (DATMPX[1:0] ≠ 0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1
```
register)
```
```
 Option 2: In this case, the input data is taken from the output of any serial data receiver (AWFSEL=1). This
```
choice has the following characteristics:
- Serial data input is processed through a dedicated analog watchdog Sincx channel filter. The filter's
```
oversampling rate (1..32) and filter order (1..3) are configurable (refer to the AWFOSR[4:0] and
```
```
AWFORD[1:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register).
```
- Lower resolution (up to 16 bits)
- Fast response time—suitable for applications requiring rapid response, such as overcurrent/overvoltage
IOSR Sinc1 Sinc2 FastSinc Sinc3 Sinc4 Sinc5
x +/-FOSR.x +/-FOSR2.x +/-2FOSR2.x +/-FOSR3.x +/-FOSR4.x +/-FOSR5.x
4 - - - +/-67108864 - -
32 - - - +/-536870912 - -
128 - - - +/-2147483648 - -
256 - - - +/-232 - -
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 944
detection
- Data is provided in continuous mode, independent of regular or injected main conversion activity
```
During input channel monitoring (AWFSEL=1), data for threshold comparison is sourced from the channel
```
```
selected via the AWDCH[1:0] field (R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register). The filter result from each selected
```
```
channel is compared against a threshold pair (AWHT[23:0]/AWLT[23:0]). At this point, only the upper 16 bits
```
```
(AWHT[23:8]/AWLT[23:8]) define the 16-bit threshold compared against the analog watchdog filter output, as
```
```
the data from the analog watchdog filter has a maximum resolution of 16 bits. In this case (AWFSEL=1), the
```
AWHT[7:0]/AWLT[7:0] bits are not compared.
```
The parameters for the analog watchdog filter configuration of each input channel (filter order AWFORD[1:0] and
```
```
filter oversampling rate AWFOSR[4:0]) are set in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register.
```
The analog watchdog filter data for channel y can be read via firmware from the WDATA[15:0] field of the
DFSDM_CHyWDATR register. If CHEN=1 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register, this analog watchdog
filter data is continuously converted at a data rate determined by the analog watchdog filter settings and the
channel input clock frequency.
```
The analog watchdog filter operates similarly to a conventional fast continuous conversion (without integrator).
```
```
The number of serial samples required for the analog watchdog filter to output a result (with channel input clock
```
```
frequency fCKIN) is:
```
First conversion:
```
For Sincx filters (x=1..5): Number of samples = [FOSR*(FORD+1)+2]
```
For FastSinc filters: Number of samples = [FOSR*4+2+1]
Subsequent conversion:
For Sincx and FastSinc filters: Number of samples = [FOSR*FORD]
Among them:
```
FOSR, or Filter Oversampling Ratio: FOSR = AWFOSR[4:0] + 1 (refer to the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR
```
```
register)
```
```
FORD, or Filter Order: FORD = AWFORD[1:0] (refer to the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register)
```
```
For output data register monitoring (AWFSEL=0), comparison occurs after completing the final data right shift
```
```
and offset correction (refer to the OFFSET[23:0] and DTRBS[4:0] fields in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2
```
```
register). The comparison occurs after each injection or regular conversion of the channel selected by the
```
```
AWDCH[1:0] field (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register).
```
The status of simulated watchdog events is reflected in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR register, which locks the
given event. The AWHTF[y]=1 flag indicates whether the AWHT[23:0] value has been exceeded on channel y.
The AWLFTF[y]=1 flag indicates whether the AWLT[23:0] value has been exceeded on channel y. Events latched
in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR register are cleared by writing a 1 to the corresponding clear bit CLRAWHTF[y]
or CLRAWLTF[y] in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWCFR register.
42.3.9 Short Circuit Detector
The purpose of the short-circuit detector is to signal within an extremely fast response time when an analog signal
```
reaches saturation (exceeds full-scale range) and remains there for a specified duration. This feature detects
```
```
short-circuit or open-circuit faults (e.g., overcurrent or overvoltage). Interrupts/events/open-circuit generation can
```
be invoked.
The short-circuit detector's input data is derived from the channel transceiver output.
Each input channel features an incrementing counter that tallies consecutive 0s or 1s on the serial data receiver
```
output. If the received data stream changes (data signal transitions from 1 to 0 or from 0 to 1), the counter is reset.
```
```
A short-circuit event is triggered when the counter reaches the short-circuit threshold register value (SCDT[7:0]
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 945
```
bits in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register). Each input channel is equipped with a dedicated short-circuit
```
```
detector. Continuous monitoring for any channel can be enabled by setting the SCDEN bit (in the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register). Each channel has its own short-circuit detector configuration (threshold bits
```
```
SCDT[7:0], status bits SCDF[1:0], status clear bits CLRSCDF[1:0]). When the corresponding channel y is
```
```
disabled (CHEN[y]=0), the status flag SCDF[y] can also be cleared by hardware.
```
For each channel, short-circuit detector events can be assigned to the break output signals DFSDM_BK[1:0]. Two
break outputs can be assigned to a single short-circuit detector event. The break signals are assigned to a given
channel's short-circuit detector event via the BKSCD[1:0] field in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register.
```
If parallel input data channels are selected (DATMPX[1:0] ≠ 0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register), the
```
short-circuit detector cannot be used.
```
A total of two break outputs are available (shared with the analog watchdog function).
```
42.3.10 Extreme Value Detector
```
The Extreme Value Detector captures the minimum and maximum values (peak-to-peak values) of the final output
```
data word.
If the output data word exceeds the value stored in the maximum value register of the extremum detector
```
(EXMAX[23:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX register), this register is updated with the current output
```
```
data word value, and the channel storing its data is indicated in the EXMAXCH bit (of the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX register).
```
```
If the output data word is less than the value stored in the extremum detector minimum register (EXMIN[23:0]
```
```
bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN register), this register is updated with the current output data word value,
```
```
and the channel storing its data is indicated by the EXMINCH bit (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN register).
```
```
The minimum and maximum value register values can be refreshed by software (by reading the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX or R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN registers). After refresh, the minimum value data
```
```
register (R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN) is filled with 0x7FFFFF (maximum positive value), and the maximum
```
```
value register (R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX) is filled with 0x800000 (minimum negative value).
```
The extremum detector performs comparison operations only after completing right shift and offset data
correction. For each extremum detector, the input channels involved in extremum calculation are selected by the
```
EXCH[1:0] bits (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register).
```
42.3.11 Data Unit Module
The data unit module is the final module in the entire processing path: external ΣΔ modulator—serial
transceiver—Sinc filter—integrator—data unit block.
The output data rate depends on the serial data stream rate and the filter and integrator settings. The maximum
output data rate is:
```
Data rate [samples/sec]= ; FAST=0, Sincx filter
```
```
Data rate [samples/sec]= ; FAST=0, FastSinc filter
```
Or
```
Data rate [samples/sec]= ; FAST=1
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 946
Maximum output data rate for parallel data input:
```
Data rate [samples/sec]= ; FAST=0, Sincx filter
```
Or
```
Data rate [samples/sec]= ; FAST=0, FastSinc filter
```
Or
```
Data rate [samples/sec]= ; FAST=1 or any bypass case (FOSR=1)
```
```
Where: fDATAIN_RATE is the input data rate of ADC or CPU/DMA.
```
The right shift of the final data is performed in this module, because the final data width is 24 bits, and the data
from the processing path can be up to 32 bits. For each selected input channel, this right shift can be configured in
```
the range of 0-31 bits (refer to bits DTRBS[4:0] in R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register). Shift right rounds the
```
result to the nearest integer value. The sign of the shifted result is preserved, so as to obtain the result data in a
valid 24-bit signed format.
```
Next, the results are offset corrected. Subtract the offset correction value (OFFSET[23:0] stored in register
```
```
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2) from the output data of a given channel. The data in the OFFSET[23:0] field is set by
```
the software through the corresponding calibration program.
Since all operations in digital processing are performed on 32-bit signed registers, the following conditions must
be met to ensure that the results will not overflow:
```
1) FOSRFORD.2IOSR≤231, suitable for Sincx filter (x=1..5);
```
```
2) FOSR2.2IOSR≤231, suitable for FastSinc filter.
```
```
Note: When the filter and integrator are bypassed (IOSR[3:0]=0, FOSR[9:0]=0), the input data rate (fDATAIN_RATE)
```
```
must be limited to be able to read all the output data: fDATAIN_RATE≤fHCLK; Among them, fHCLK is the bus frequency
```
of DFSDM peripheral connection.
42.3.12 Signed Data Format
Each channel of the DFSDM input serial channel can be connected to an external ΣΔ modulator. An external ΣΔ
```
modulator is configured with two differential inputs (positive and negative), which can be used for either
```
differential measurements or single-ended signal measurements.
```
It is always assumed that the ΣΔ modulator's output uses a signed format (i.e., the 0/1 data stream from the ΣΔ
```
```
modulator represents the values -1 and +1).
```
Signed Data Format in Registers: Data stored in the final output data register, analog watchdog register, extreme
```
value detector register, and offset correction register are all in signed format. The most significant bit (MSB) of
```
```
the output data word indicates the sign of the value (using two's complement format).
```
42.3.13 Start Conversion
The method to start the injection conversion is as follows:
 Software: write 1 to JSWSTART in R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register.
 Trigger: with JEXTEN activated, select the trigger signal through JEXTSEL[3:0] and determine the effective
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 947
```
edge (refer to R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register).
```
```
 If JSYNC is set to 1, DFSDM_FLT0 will start injection conversion synchronously: for DFSDM_FLTx(x>0),
```
```
injection conversion will start automatically in DFSDM_FLT0; The injection conversion is triggered by
```
```
software (set to 1 by the JSWSTART bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0CR2 register). Each injection
```
```
transformation in DFSDM_FLTx(x>0) will be performed according to its local settings (such as JSCAN and
```
```
JCHG).
```
 Only one injection conversion is allowed at a specific time. Therefore, if an injection conversion request has
been issued but not yet completed, any subsequent startup request will be ignored.
The way to start a regular conversion is as follows:
 Software: write 1 to RSWSTART in R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register.
```
 If RSYNC=1, use DFSDM_FLT0 to start synchronously: for DFSDM_FLTx(x>0), normal conversion will
```
```
start automatically in DFSDM_FLT0; The normal conversion is triggered by software (set to 1 by the
```
```
RSWSTARTT bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0CR2 register). Every regular conversion in DFSDM_FLTx(x>0)
```
```
will be performed according to its local configuration settings (RCONT, RCH, etc.).
```
42.3.14 Continuous and Fast Continuous Mode
If RCONT in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register is set to 1, normal conversion will be performed in continuous
mode. RCONT=1 means that after writing 1 to RSWSTART, the channel selected by the RCH bit is repeatedly
converted.
Normal conversion performed in continuous mode can be stopped by writing 0 to RCONT. After the RCONT is
cleared, the ongoing conversion will be stopped immediately.
In continuous mode, the data rate can be increased by setting bit 1 of the FAST position in the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register. At this time, if a continuous conversion is performed on a channel, the filter
does not need to be refilled with new refresh data because the internal filter data is valid. This data was previously
obtained by sampling continuous data. The speed increase is related to the selected filter order. After initiating
```
continuous conversion with RSWSTART=1, the initial conversion in Fast mode (FAST=1) is performed fully
```
```
(identical to FAST=0), followed by subsequent conversions completed at shorter intervals.
```
Conversion time in continuous mode:
```
When FAST=0 (or fast transition when FAST=1):
```
For Sincx filter:
```
t=CNVCNT/fDFSDMCLK=[FOSR*（2IOSR+FORD+1）+2]/fCKIN
```
For FastSinc filter:
```
t=CNVCNT/fDFSDMCLK=[FOSR*（2IOSR+5）+2]/fCKIN
```
```
When FAST=1 (except for the first conversion):
```
For Sincx and FastSinc filter:
```
t=CNVCNT/fDFSDMCLK=[FOSR*2IOSR]/fCKIN
```
```
When FOSR=FOSR[9:0]+1=1 (filter bypass, only integrator is effective):
```
```
t=2IOSR/fCKIN (...but CNVCNT=0)
```
Continuous mode is not applicable to injection conversion. Injection conversion can be initiated via timer
triggering to simulate continuous mode with precise timing.
```
If a regular continuous conversion is in progress (RCONT=1), and if a write access is made to the
```
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register requesting a regular continuous conversion (RCONT=1), the regular continuous
```
```
conversion will restart from the next conversion cycle (similar to a new regular continuous conversion being
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 948
```
applied to a new channel selection, even if no change is made to the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register).
```
42.3.15 Request Priority
Injected conversions take precedence over regular conversions. An ongoing regular conversion is immediately
```
interrupted by an injected conversion request; this regular conversion will resume after the injected conversion
```
completes.
If an injected conversion is pending or in progress, no other injected conversion can be initiated: requests to start
```
an injected conversion (via JSWSTART or trigger) are ignored as long as bit JCIP (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR
```
```
register) is set to 1.
```
Similarly, if a regular conversion is pending or in progress, no other regular conversion can be initiated: requests
```
to start a regular conversion (using RSWSTART) are ignored as long as bit RCIP (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR
```
```
register) is set to 1.
```
However, if an injection conversion is requested during a regular conversion, the regular conversion stops
immediately and the injection conversion begins. The regular conversion restarts afterward, and this delayed
restart is indicated by the RPEND bit.
Injection conversion takes precedence over regular conversion because it can temporarily interrupt a continuous
sequence of regular conversions. Upon completing the injection conversion sequence, if RCONT remains set to 1,
```
the continuous regular conversion will restart (the RPEND bit will issue a delayed start signal based on the result
```
```
of the first regular conversion).
```
Priority is also critical when initiating related operations through identical write operations to DFSDM, or if
multiple operations remain pending at the conclusion of other operations. For example, assuming an injection
```
conversion is in progress (JCIP=1), a single write operation to R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 writes 1 to RSWSTART
```
to request a regular conversion. Upon completion of the injection sequence, the priority indicates execution of the
subsequent regular conversion, with the corresponding delayed start indicated via the RPEND bit.
42.3.16 Power Consumption Optimization in Running Mode
```
To reduce power consumption, the DFSDM filter and integrator automatically enter idle state (RCIP=0, JCIP=0)
```
when not used for conversion.

42.4 Interrupt
```
In order to enhance the performance of central processing unit (CPU), a set of interrupts related to CPU events
```
have been implemented:
 Injection conversion end interrupt:
- Enabled via the JEOCIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register
- Indicated via the JEOCF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register
- Cleared by reading the R32_DFSDM_FLTxJDATAR register (injection data)
- Indicates which channel completed conversion and reports it in the JDATACH bit of the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxJDATAR register
 Regular conversion end interrupt:
- Enabled via the REOCIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register
- Indicated via the REOCF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register
- Cleared by reading the R32_DFSDM_FLTxRDATAR register (regular data)
- Indicates which channel completed conversion and reports it in the RDATACH bit of the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxRDATAR register
 Injection conversion data overflow interrupt:
- This interrupt occurs when injected conversion data is not read from the R32_DFSDM_FLTxJDATAR
```
register (via CPU or DMA) and is overwritten by newly injected conversion data.
```
- Enabled via the JOVRIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register
- Indicated via the JOVRF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register
- Cleared by writing a 1 to the CLRJOVRF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxICR register
 Regular conversion data overflow interrupt:
- This interrupt occurs when conventional conversion data is not read from the
```
R32_DFSDM_FLTxRDATAR register (via CPU or DMA) and is overwritten by a new conventional
```
conversion.
- Enabled via the ROVRIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register
- Indicated via the ROVRF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register
- Cleared by writing a 1 to the CLRROVRF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxICR register
 Analog watchdog interrupt:
- This interrupt occurs when converted data (output data or data from the analog watchdog
```
filter—depending on the setting of the AWFSEL bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register) exceeds
```
the upper threshold in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWHTR/R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWLTR register or falls
below the corresponding lower threshold.
- Enabled via the AWDIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register (for the selected channel
```
AWDCH[1:0])
```
- Indicated by the AWDF bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register
- Analog watchdog upper or lower threshold errors are individually indicated via the AWHTF[1:0] and
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 950
AWLTF[1:0] fields in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR register
- Cleared by writing a 1 to the corresponding CLRAWHTF[1:0] or CLRAWLTF[1:0] bit in the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWCFR register
 Short circuit detector interrupt:
- This interrupt occurs when stable data counts exceed the threshold in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR
register
- Enabled via the SCDIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register (for channels selected by the
```
SCDEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register)
```
- Indicated via the SCDF[1:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register (also reports the channel where
```
the short-circuit detector event occurred)
```
- Cleared by writing a 1 to the corresponding CLRSCDF[1:0] bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxICR register
- Short circuit detector interrupt:
 Channel clock missing interrupt:
- This interrupt occurs when a clock loss is detected on the CKINy pin (refer to Section 42.3.2: Serial
```
Channel Transceiver Clock Loss Detection)
```
- Enabled via the CKABIE bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register (for the channel selected by the
```
CKABEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register)
```
- Indicated via the CKABF[y] bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register
- Cleared by writing a 1 to the CLRCKABF[y] bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxICR register

42.5 DFSDM DMA Transfer
To reduce CPU intervention, DMA transfers can be used to transfer conversions to memory. DMA transfers for
injected conversions are enabled by setting the JDMAEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register. DMA
transfers for regular conversions are enabled by setting the RDMAEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 951
```
Note: With DMA transfers, interrupt flags (JEOCF or REOCF bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register) are
```
automatically cleared at the end of an injection or regular conversion because DMA is reading the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxJDATAR or R32_DFSDM_FLTxRDATAR registers.

Chapter 43 LCD-TFT Display Controller (LTDC)
```
```
LCD-TFT (Thin Film Transistor-Liquid Crystal Display) Display Controller (LTDC) mainly provides parallel
```
digital RGB, horizontal synchronization, vertical synchronization, pixel clock and data enable signals, which can
be used as output signals to interface with different LCD and TFT panels.
43.1 Main Features
 Provide 2 display layers, each containing a proprietary 8×256-bit FIFO
```
 Support color lookup tables (CLUT) with up to 256 colors per layer
```
 Support programmable timing for different display panels
 Support programmable background color
 Support programmable polarity for HSYNC, VSYNC, and data enable signals
 Each display layer supports up to 8 input colors
```
 Flexible blending between 2 layers using alpha values (per-pixel or constant)
```
```
 Support chroma key (transparent color)
```
 Support programmable window position and size
```
 Support thin-film transistor (TFT) color displays
```
 Support up to 3 programmable interrupt timers
43.2 Overview

43.3 Function Description
43.3.1 LTDC Synchronization Timing
The LTDC interface is a synchronous data interface comprising pixel clock, pixel data, and horizontal and vertical
sync signals. Figure 43-2 illustrates the configurable timing parameters generated by the LTDC synchronous
timing generator module.
Figure 43-2 LTDC synchronization timing
VSYNC width
VBP
Active height
VFP
Data1,Line1
```
Data(n),Line(n)
```
Active display area
Total height
HSYNC width
HBP
Active width
Total width
HFP
```
Note: (1) HSYNC and VSYNC denote horizontal and vertical sync widths, respectively; HBP and HFP denote
```
```
horizontal back-edge period and horizontal front-edge period, respectively; VBP and VFP denote vertical
```
back-edge period and vertical front-edge period, respectively.
```
(2) When LTDC is enabled, the generated timing uses the X/Y=0/0 position as the first horizontal sync pixel within
```
the vertical sync region, followed by the back edge, active data display region, and front edge.
```
(3) When LTDC is disabled, the timing generator module resets to X=total width-1 and Y=total height-1, holding
```
the previous pixel during the vertical sync phase and before FIFO refresh. Consequently, only blanking data is
continuously output.
An example of synchronization timing configuration is as follows:
```
1) LCD-TFT timing (to be extracted from the panel datasheet);
```
```
2) Horizontal and vertical sync width: 0xA pixels, 0x2-1 lines;
```
```
3) Horizontal and vertical trailing edge: 0x14 pixels, 0x2 lines;
```
```
4) Effective width and effective height: 0x140 pixels, 0xF0 lines (320x240);
```
```
5) Horizontal leading edge: 0xA pixels;
```
```
6) Vertical leading edge: 0x4 lines;
```

```
43.3.2 Pixel Format
Programmable pixel format is used for data stored in the frame buffer of the layer. Up to eight input pixel format
can be configured for each layer through the R32_LTDC_LxPFCR register.
```
The ARGB8888 format requires 8 bits of data per channel (Alpha, Red, Green and Blue). However, some
```
channels in ARGB1555 and ARGB4444 formats are less than 8 bits. The pixel processing unit converts it into
ARGB8888 by copying the high bits and filling them into the low bits. When processing RGB888 and RGB565
formats, the pixel processing unit assumes Alpha=255, and if the number of bits of the channel is less than 8, the
copy high bits are also padded to the low bits.
```
43.3.3 Color Look-up Table (CLUT)
```
CLUT can be enabled for each layer at runtime through the CLUTEN bit in the R32_LTDC_LxCR register. CLUT
is only suitable for index colors when using L8, AL44 and AL88 input pixel format.
First, CLUT must load R, G and B values to replace the original R, G and B values of the corresponding pixels
```
(index colors). Each color (RGB value) has its own corresponding address in CLUT. The values of r, g and b and
```
their respective addresses are programmed by R32_LTDC_LxCLUTWR register.
When using L8 and AL88 to input pixel format, CLUT must be loaded with 256 colors. The address of each color
is configured in the CLUTADD bit of R32_LTDC_LxCLUTWR register.
When using AL44 to input pixel format, CLUT must only load 16 colors. The address of each color must be filled
by repeating the 4-bit L channel into 8 bits, as follows:
```
–L0 (Index Color 0), at address 0x00;
```
```
–L1, at address 0x11;
```
```
–L2, at address 0x22;
```
```
–.....;
```
–L15, at address 0xFF.
43.3.4 Color Frame Buffer
44.3.4.1 Color Frame Buffer Address
The color frame buffer of each layer has a start address, which is configured by R32_LTDC_LxCFBAR register.
When a layer is enabled, the data will be obtained from the color frame buffer.
44.3.4.2 Color Frame Buffer Length
```
Each layer is set with the total length (in bytes) and the number of lines of the color frame buffer, which can be
```
configured by the R32_LTDC_LxCFBLR and R32_LTDC_LxCFBLNR registers respectively.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 980
The length and number of rows are set to prevent data beyond the end of the frame buffer from being prefetched
into the FIFO corresponding to the layer.
```
If it is set below the required bytes, a FIFO underflow interrupt will be generated (if previously enabled).
```
If it is set to more bytes than actually needed, useless data read from FIFO will be discarded and will not be
displayed.
44.3.4.3 Color Frame Buffer Spacing
```
The color frame buffer of each layer has a configurable spacing, which is the distance (in bytes) from the
```
beginning of one line to the beginning of the next line. It is configured through the R32_LTDC_LxCFBLR
register.
43.3.5 Layer Window and Blending Function
Each layer supports windowing functionality as well as two-layer blending. LTDC first performs windowing
operations on each layer, then blends the two layers into a single frame.
Window functions define a display window, with each layer having independent window position configuration
```
registers: R32_LTDC_LxWHPCR and R32_LTDC_LxWVPCR. Window configuration defines the display
```
window within a layer. Pixels within the window retain their original values, while pixels outside the window are
replaced with the pixel value defined by the R32_LTDC_LxDCCR register.
The blending order is fixed, proceeding from bottom to top. The blending unit first blends layer 0 with the
background layer to produce a temporary layer, then blends layer 1 with the temporary layer to generate the final
layer. The ARGB values of the background layer are defined in the R32_LTDC_BCCR register. If a layer is
disabled, the blending function uses that layer's default color. To prevent the default color from appearing when a
layer is disabled, set the blending coefficient for that layer in the R32_LTDC_LxBFCR register to its reset value.
The blending process is illustrated in Figure 43-3.
Figure 43-3 Block diagram of blending process
BG Layer
Layer 0
Temporary layer
Layer 1
Target layer
```
General blending formula: BC = BF1 * C + BF2 * CS;
```
```
BC represents the blended color; BF1 is blending factor 1; C is the current layer's color; BF2 is blending factor 2;
```
CS is the color of the next layer to be blended.
The blending factors for the current pixel have two possible values, determined by register configuration. One is
the pixel's alpha multiplied by a constant Alpha, and the other is a constant Alpha.
```
Note: The constant Alpha value is programmed into the register and implemented by hardware as 255 equal
```
divisions.
```
Example: To enable only the first layer, configure BF1 to the constant Alpha and BF2 to 1 minus the constant
```
Alpha.
```
Constant Alpha: The constant Alpha programmed into the LxCACR register is 240 (0xF0).
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 981
Therefore, the constant Alpha value is 240/255 = 0.94
```
C: The red channel of the current layer is 0x80.
```
```
Cs: The red channel of the background is 0x30.
```
The first layer blends with the background color.
```
Final red channel result = Constant Alpha * C + (1 - Constant Alpha) * Cs
```
```
= 0.94 * 0x80 + (1 - 0.94) * 0x30 = 0x7B.
```
The green and blue channels follow the same principle.
43.3.6 Layer Window and Blending Function
```
Color keys (RGB) can be configured to represent transparent pixels. At runtime, the color key value can be
```
configured and used to replace the pixel RGB value.
```
When the color key is enabled, the current pixel (the pixel after format conversion and before CLUT is mixed
```
```
separately) will be compared with the color key. If the current pixel matches the programmed RGB value, all
```
```
channels (ARGB) of the pixel are set to 0.
```
Color keys are configured through the LTDC_LxCKCR register. The programmed value depends on the pixel
format, because it will be compared with the current pixel after the pixel format is converted to ARGB888.
```
For example, if medium yellow (50% red +50% green) is used as the transparent color key, then:
```
- In RGB565, the mid-yellow value is 0x8400. Set LTDC_LxCKCR to 0x848200.
- In ARGB8888, the mid-yellow value is 0x808000. Set LTDC_LxCKCR to 0x808000.
- In all CLUT-based color modes (L8, AL88, AL44), set one of the palette entries to mid-yellow 0x808000 and set
LTDC_LxCKCR to 0x808000.
43.3.7 Reloaded shadow register
Some configuration registers perform shadow operations. When writing to the active register, or at the beginning
of the vertical blanking period after the configuration phase of R32_LTDC_SRCR register, the shadow register
value can be reloaded into the active register immediately. If the immediate overload configuration is selected,
overloading should only be activated after all new registers have finished writing.
The shadow register should not be modified again before the overload is completed. Reading the shadow register
will return the actual effective value. The newly written value can only be read after the overload occurs.
If enabled in the R32_LTDC_IER register, a register overload interrupt can be generated.
Shadow registers are Layer 1 and Layer 2 registers, except R32_LTDC_LxCLUTWR register.
43.3.8 Interrupt
The LTDC provides three maskable interrupts, which are logically ORed into a single interrupt vector.
```
Interrupt sources can be individually enabled or disabled via the R32_LTDC_IER register; corresponding interrupt
```
```
flags can be read through the R32_LTDC_ISR register; and the corresponding interrupt flag bits can be cleared by
```
setting the R32_LTDC_ICR register to 1.
Interrupts are generated when the following events occur:
 Line interrupt: Generated upon reaching a programmed line. The interrupt position is programmed in the
```
R32_LTDC_LIPCR register;
```
 Register reload interrupt: Generated during shadow register reload execution within the vertical blanking
```
interval;
```
 FIFO underflow interrupt: Generated when requesting pixels from an empty layer FIFO.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 982

Chapter 44 Graphics Processing Hardware accelerator (GPHA)
```
```
Image Processing Hardware Accelerator (GPHA) is a DMA dedicated to image processing, which supports
```
indexed color mode or direct color mode and all classical color coding schemes. In addition, the GPHA module
```
also has its own exclusive CLUT (Color Lookup Table).
```
44.1 Main Features
 Support single HB master bus architecture
```
 HB slave programming interface supports 8/16/32-bit access (except for 32-bit CLUT access)
```
 Support programmable source and destination region sizes and offsets
 Support programmable source and destination addresses across entire memory space
```
 Support adjustable alpha values (source value, fixed value, modulation value)
```
 Support hybrid operations with up to 2 sources
 Support programmable source and target color formats, accommodating up to 11 color formats with a
maximum of 32 bits per pixel
 Support two internal memories for storing CLUTs in indirect color mode
 Support programmable CLUT size, with CLUTs automatically loaded via CPU or programmed manually
 Support internal timer control for HB bandwidth
 Support three operating modes: register-to-memory, memory-to-memory with pixel format conversion, and
memory-to-memory with pixel format conversion and mixing
 Support filling specified portions or the entire area of the target image with a specific color
 Support copying portions or the entire content of the source image to corresponding portions or the entire
target image
 Support copying portions or the entire content of the source image to portions or the entire target image with
pixel format conversion
 Support blending two source image sections and/or entire images with differing pixel formats, then copying
the result to sections or the entire target image with differing color formats
 Support canceling or suspending GPHA operations
 Support generating interrupts upon bus errors or access conflicts
 Support generating interrupts upon process completion
44.2 Function Description
44.2.1 Overview
```
The foreground layer (FG)FIFO and background layer (BG)FIFO of GPHA acquire the input data to be copied
```
and processed. These FIFO acquire pixels according to the preset color format in the corresponding pixel format
```
converter (PFC), perform color format conversion, wherein the foreground layer and background layer can be
```
processed separately or mixed, and finally output the converted color data. As shown in Figure 44-1, it shows the
structural block diagram of GPHA in detail.

GPHA controller performs direct memory transfer. As a HB master, it can control HB bus matrix to start HB
transactions. HB slave port is used to program GPHA controller.
GPHA supports the following 3 modes of operation:
- Register-to-memory;
- Memory-to-memory with pixel format conversion;
- Memory-to-memory with pixel format conversion and blending.
GPHA functions include the following operations:
- Support filling specified portions or the entire area of the target image with a specific color;
- Support copying portions or the entire content of the source image to corresponding portions or the entire target
```
image;
```
- Support copying portions or the entire content of the source image to portions or the entire target image with
```
pixel format conversion;
```
- Support blending portions and/or the entire content of two source images with different pixel formats, then
copying the result to portions or the entire target image with different color formats.
44.2.2 GPHA Control
The GPHA controller can be configured via the R32_GPHA_CTLR register to perform the following operations:
```
1) Select the GPHA operating mode;
```
```
2) Enable/disable GPHA interrupts;
```
```
3) Start/suspend/abort an ongoing data transfer.
```
44.2.3 GPHA Foreground Layer FIFO and Background Layer FIFO
```
The coordinated operation of the GPHA Foreground Layer (FG) FIFO and Background Layer (BG) FIFO is
```
critical to the efficient image processing of the GPHA. These FIFOs acquire input data for replication and
processing, fetching pixels according to the color format preset in the corresponding Pixel Format Converter
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 997
```
(PFC). They can be programmed via the following registers:
```
- GPHA Foreground Layer Memory Address Register (R32_GPHA_FGMAR)
- GPHA Foreground Layer Offset Register (R32_GPHA_FGOR)
- GPHA Foreground Memory Address Register (R32_GPHA_BGMAR)
- GPHA Foreground Offset Register (R32_GPHA_BGBOR)
- GPHA Number of Lines Register (Number of Lines and Pixels per Line) (R32_GPHA_NLR)
GPHA works in register-to-memory mode and does not activate any FIFO. When GPHA works in
```
memory-to-memory mode and supports pixel format conversion (no mixed operation), BGFIFO will not be
```
activated.
```
44.2.4 GPHA Foreground Layer and Background Layer Pixel Format Converter (PFC)
```
```
The GPHA Foreground and Background Layer Pixel Format Converter (PFC) performs pixel format conversion to
```
generate 32-bit values per pixel. Additionally, the PFC possesses the capability to modify the alpha channel.
This converter performs color format conversion in the first stage. The CM[3:0] bits of the
R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register and the CM[3:0] bits of the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register configure the raw
color formats for foreground layer pixels and background layer pixels, respectively. The supported input color
modes are listed in Table 44-1.
Table 44-1 Color modes supported during input
CM[3:0] Color mode
0000 ARGB8888
0001 RGB888
0010 RGB565
0011 ARGB1555
0100 ARGB4444
0101 L8
0110 AL44
0111 AL88
1000 L4
1001 A8
1010 A4
The Alpha channel is an extra channel used to represent the transparency of each pixel in the image. It is often
```
used with red, green and blue (RGB) channels to form RGBA model.
```
The following is a description of the encoding methods of color formats appearing in Table 44-1:
Alpha value field: transparent, with 0xFF value corresponding to opaque pixels and 0x00 corresponding to
```
transparent pixels;
```
```
R field: Represents red;
```
```
G field: Represents green;
```
```
B field: Represents blue;
```
```
L field: Represents luminance; this field serves as the CLUT index for retrieving 3 or 4 RGB/ARGB components.
```
If the original format is in direct color mode, it is expanded to 8 bits per channel by copying the most significant
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 998
```
bit (MSB) to the least significant bit (LSB). This ensures the conversion exhibits good linearity.
```
```
If the original format does not include an alpha channel, the alpha value is automatically set to 0xFF (opaque).
```
If the original format is in indirect color mode, a CLUT is required, and each pixel format converter is associated
with a CLUT containing 256 32-bit entries.
For specific alpha modes A4 and A8, neither color information is stored nor indexed. The colors used to generate
the image are fixed, with the foreground layer pixel color defined in the R32_GPHA_FGCOLR register and the
background layer pixel color defined in the R32_GPHA_BGCOLR register.

registers.
44.2.5 GPHA Foreground Layer and Background Layer CLUT Interface
CLUT is a table for storing color mapping, which maps the index value of each pixel to a specific color value.
CLUT interface can manage the access to CLUT memory and the automatic loading of CLUT. CLUT interface
supports the following access methods:
- PFC reads the CLUT during pixel format conversion;
- The CPU accesses the CLUT via the HB from the device port to read or write data;
- When performing automatic CLUT loading, CLUT writing is executed through the HB master device port.
CLUT memory loading can be realized by automatic loading and manual loading:
Autoloading
```
1) Program the CLUT address into the R32_GPHA_FGCMAR register (foreground layer CLUT) or the
```
```
R32_GPHA_BGCMAR register (background layer CLUT).
```
```
2) Program the CLUT size into the CS[7:0] bits of the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register (foreground layer CLUT)
```
```
or the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register (background layer CLUT).
```
```
3) Set the START bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register (foreground layer CLUT) or R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR
```
```
register (background layer CLUT) to 1 to initiate the transfer. During auto-loading, the CPU must not access the
```
CLUT. If a conflict occurs and the CAEIE bit in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register is set to 1, a CLUT access error
interrupt is generated.
Manual loading
```
The application must manually program the local CLUT memory via the GPHA HB from the device port; this
```
CLUT maps to the CLUT in the dedicated SRAM.
```
1) Program the CLUT pixel address into the FG_CLUT_INDEX bit of the R32_GPHA_FGCRWS register
```
```
(foreground layer CLUT) or the BG_CLUT_INDEX bit of the R32_GPHA_FGCRWS register (background layer
```
```
CLUT).
```
```
2) Program the CLUT pixel value into the R32_GPHA_FGCDAT register (foreground layer CLUT) or the
```
```
R32_GPHA_BGCDAT register (background layer CLUT). The CPU automatically loads this pixel value into the
```
corresponding CLUT memory.
```
The CLUT format supports 24-bit or 32-bit. The CCM bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register (for the
```
```
foreground layer CLUT) or the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register (for the background layer CLUT) configures the
```
CLUT color mode. Refer to Table 44-4 for specific configuration details.
Table 44-4 Supported CLUT color modes
CCM CLUT color modes
0 32-bit ARGB8888
1 24-bit RGB888

The output FIFO programs pixels according to the color format defined in the output PFC. The target area can be

- GPHA Output Memory Address Register (R32_GPHA_OMAR)
- GPHA Output Offset Register (R32_GPHA_OOR)
- GPHA Number of Lines Register (Number of Lines and Pixels per Line) (R32_GPHA_NLR)
When the GPHA operates in register-to-memory mode, the configured output rectangle will be filled with the

```

register.

44.2.9 GPHA HB Master Port Timer
An 8-bit timer is embedded in the port of HB master device, which aims to limit the bandwidth of crossbar matrix
optionally. This timer is driven by HB clock, and is responsible for counting the dead zone between 2 consecutive
accesses, so as to limit the bandwidth usage.
The enabling of the timer and the dead-time value can be configured through the EN bits and DT[7:0] bits of
R32_GPHA_AMTCR register. Please refer to Chapter 44.2.15 for the setting of HB dead-time.
44.2.10 GPHA Transaction
GPHA transaction consists of a series of data transmission sequences with a preset number. The quantity and
width of data can be programmed by software.
Each GPHA data transmission project needs at most 4 steps:
```
1) Load data from the memory location specified by the R32_GPHA_FGMAR register and perform pixel format
```
conversion as defined in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register.
```
2) Load data from the memory location specified by the R32_GPHA_BGMAR register and perform pixel format
```
conversion as defined in the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register.
```
3) Process alpha values using PFC operations to obtain alpha channel information, then blend all retrieved pixels.
```
```
4) Perform pixel format conversion on the blended pixels according to the R32_GPHA_OPFCCR register, then
```
program the converted data into memory cells addressed via the R32_GPHA_OMAR register.
44.2.11 GPHA Configuration
```
Source and destination data transmission can address peripherals and memory in the entire 4GB area (address
```
```
range between 0x00000000 and 0xFFFFFFFF).
```
GPHA can work in the following three modes, and the working mode can be selected through bits MODE[1:0] of
R32_GPHA_CTLR register:
- Register to Memory
- Memory to Memory with PFC Execution
- Memory to Memory with PFC and Hybrid Execution
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1002
44.2.11.1 Register to Memory
Register-to-memory mode is used to fill user-defined areas with predefined colors.
The color format is set in the R32_GPHA_OPFCCR register.
The GPHA does not acquire data from any source. It only writes the color defined in the R32_GPHA_OCOLR
register to the region defined by R32_GPHA_OMAR addressing and the R32_GPHA_NLR and
R32_GPHA_OOR registers.
44.2.11.2 Memory to Memory and Perform PFC
In this mode, GPHA performs pixel format transform on the source data and stores the result in the target storage
unit.
For the size of the region to be transferred, the source region size is defined by the R32_GPHA_NLR and
R32_GPHA_FGOR registers, while the destination region size is defined by the R32_GPHA_NLR and
R32_GPHA_OOR registers.
Data is retrieved from the location defined by the R32_GPHA_FGMAR register and processed by the foreground
layer PFC. The original pixel format is configured via the GPHA_FGPFCCR register.
If the original pixel format is in direct color mode, all color channels are expanded to 8 bits.
If the pixel format is in indirect color mode, the corresponding CLUT must be loaded into the CLUT memory.
CLUT loading can be performed automatically in the following sequence:
```
1) Set the CLUT address in the R32_GPHA_FGCMAR register.
```
```
2) Set the CLUT size in the CS[7:0] bits of the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register.
```
```
3) Set the CLUT format (24-bit or 32-bit) in the CCM bit of the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register.
```
```
4) Enable CLUT loading by setting the START bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register to 1.
```
```
Upon completion of CLUT loading, the CTCIF flag in the R32_GPHA_ISR register will be set; if the CTCIE bit
```
in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register is set to 1, an interrupt will also be generated. The automatic CLUT loading
process cannot occur concurrently with traditional GPHA transfers.
The CLUT can also be filled by the CPU or by any other host device via the HB port. The CLUT cannot be
```
accessed during GPHA transfers or when using CLUT (indirect color format).
```
44.2.11.3 Memory to Memory and Perform PFC and Mixing
In this mode, two source images will be captured in the foreground layer FIFO and the background layer FIFO
```
(defined in R32_GPHA_FGMAR register and R32_GPHA_BGMAR register respectively).
```
2 pixel format converters must be configured as described in memory-to-memory mode. Since these 2 pixel
format converters are independent and have their own CLUT memory, their configurations can be different.
After each pixel is converted into 32 bits by the corresponding PFC, it will be mixed according to the formula in
44.3.6. The output PFC will encode the obtained 32-bit pixel value according to the specified output format, and
the encoded data will be written into the target storage unit addressed by GPHA_OMAR.
44.2.11.4 Configuration Error Detection
GPHA will check whether the configuration is correct before each transmission. When starting a new
transfer/autoload, if a configuration error is detected, the hardware will set a configuration error interrupt flag. If
the CEIE bit in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register is set, an interrupt will also be generated.
Detectable errors are configured as follows:
- Memory transfer (except register-to-memory mode): The MA bit in the R32_GPHA_FGMAR register does not
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1003
```
match the CM bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register;
```
- Memory transfer (except register-to-memory mode): The CM bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register is
```
invalid;
```
- Memory transfer (except register-to-memory mode): The PL bit in the R32_GPHA_NLR register is odd, while
```
the CM bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register is A4 or L4;
```
- Memory transfer (except register-to-memory mode): The LO bit in the R32_GPHA_FGOR register is odd, while
```
the CM bit in the R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register is A4 or L4;
```
- Memory Transfer (Hybrid Mode Only): The MA bit in the R32_GPHA_BGMAR register does not match the
```
CM bit in the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register;
```
- Memory Transfer: The CM bit in the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register is invalid (Hybrid Mode Only);
- Memory Transfer (Hybrid Mode Only): The PL bit in the R32_GPHA_NLR register is odd, while the CM bit in
```
the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register is A4 or L4;
```
- Memory Transfer (Hybrid Mode Only): R32_GPHA_BGOR register LO bit is odd while
```
R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register CM bit is A4 or L4;
```
- Memory Transfer: The MA bit in the R32_GPHA_OMAR register does not match the CM bit in the
```
R32_GPHA_OPFCCR register;
```
- Memory Transfer: The CM bit in the R32_GPHA_OPFCCR register is invalid;
- Memory Transfer: The NL bit in the R32_GPHA_NLR register is set to 0;
- Memory Transfer: PL bit in R32_GPHA_NLR register = 0;
```
44.2.12 GPHA Transmission Control (Start, Suspend, Stop and Complete)
```
After configuring the GPHA, setting the START bit to 1 in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register initiates data transfer.
Upon completion, the START bit automatically resets and the TCIF flag is set in the R32_GPHA_ISR register. If
the TCIE bit in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register is set to 1, an interrupt is also generated.
The user application can suspend the GPHA at any time by setting the SUSP bit in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register
to 1. The transaction can then be aborted by setting the ABORT bit in the GPHA_CTLR register to 1, or resumed
by clearing the SUSP bit in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register.
The user application may terminate a transaction in progress at any time by setting bit 1 of the ABORT field in the
R32_GPHA_CTLR register. In this case, the TCIF flag will not be set.
The CLUT automatic transfer process may also be terminated or suspended by setting the START bit in the
R32_GPHA_FGPFCCR register or the R32_GPHA_BGPFCCR register itself.
44.2.13 Watermark
The watermark can be programmed to generate an interrupt when the last pixel in a specified row is written to the
target storage area.
The row number is defined in bits LW[15:0] of the R32_GPHA_LWR register.
```
Upon completion of the last pixel transfer in that row, the R32_GPHA_ISR will set the TWIF flag; an interrupt
```
will also be generated if the TWIE bit in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register is set to 1.
44.2.14 Error Management
```
Triggerable error: CLUT access conflict (CPU attempts to access CLUT during CLUT loading or GPHA transfer
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1004
```
execution), indicated by the CAEIF flag in the R32_GPHA_ISR register.
```
```
This flag correlates with the interrupt enable flags (TEIE and CAEIE) in the R32_GPHA_CTLR register, which
```
control whether interrupts are generated when required.
44.2.15 HB Dead-time
To limit HB bandwidth usage, a dead-time can be programmed between 2 consecutive HB accesses.
The dead-time function is enabled by setting bit EN in the R32_GPHA_AMTCR register to 1.
The dead-time value is stored in bits DT[7:0] of the R32_GPHA_AMTCR register. This value represents the
minimum number of cycles allowed between 2 consecutive transactions on the HB bus.
Updates to the dead-time value during GPHA operation take effect during the next HB transmission.

46.2 Flash Memory Programming and Safety
46.2.1 Two Program/Erase Methods
```
 Standard Programming: This is the default programming mode (compatibility mode). In this mode, the CPU
```
executes programming in single 2-byte increments. When DBMODE=1, the chip performs erase operations
```
in single 8K-byte increments; when DBMODE=0, the chip performs erase operations in single 4K-byte
```
increments.
```
 Fast Programming: This method employs a page operation mode (recommended). After unlocking via a
```
specific sequence, it executes a single 256-byte programming operation. When DBMODE=1, the chip
```
performs a single 64K-byte erase operation; when DBMODE=0, the chip performs a single 32K-byte erase
```
operation.
```
46.2.2 Security-preventing against Illegal Access (read, write and erase)
```
 Page write protection
 Read protection
When the chip is in read protection:
```
1) When DBMODE=1, pages 0-31 (8K bytes) of the chip's main memory are automatically write-protected and
```
are not controlled by the R32_FLASH_WPR register. When read protection is disabled, all main memory pages
are controlled by the R32_FLASH_WPR register.
```
2) When DBMODE=0, pages 0-15 (4K bytes) of the chip's main memory are automatically write-protected and
```
not controlled by the R32_FLASH_WPR register. When read protection is disabled, all main memory pages are
controlled by the R32_FLASH_WPR register.
```
3) The system boot code area, SWD or SDI mode, and RAM regions cannot be erased or programmed. The
```
user-selectable word area can be erased or programmed. If an attempt is made to disable read protection
```
(programming user words), the chip will automatically erase the entire user area.
```
46.3 FLASH Enhanced Read Mode
FLASH Enhanced Read Mode is suitable for user programs to run in FLASH, which can improve the access
efficiency of FLASH. To enable this mode, set bit 1 of the EHMOD field in the R32_FLASH_ACTLR register.
```
Then, read the ENHANCE_STATUS bit; if bit 1 of ENHANCE_STATUS is set, the enhanced read mode is active.
```
To disable this mode, first clear bit 1 of EHMOD, then set RSENACT to 1.
```
Note: When using FLASH enhanced reading mode, you should pay attention to the following points:
```
```
1) Before performing any erase or program operations on the FLASH (including user programming such as read
```
```
protection removal), you must first exit Enhanced Read Mode. Failure to do so will cause erase and program
```
operations to fail.
```
2) Before entering Stop Mode, you must first exit Enhanced Read Mode. Failure to do so may cause Stop Mode to
```
malfunction.
```
3) After a power reset or system reset completes, the chip automatically exits Enhanced Read Mode under
```
hardware control.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1026

46.5 Flash Operation Procedure
46.5.1 Read Operation
Direct addressing is in the general address space, and the user can access the content of the flash memory module
and get the corresponding data through any read operation of 8/16/32-bit data.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1034
46.5.2 Flash Memory Unlock
```
After the system reset, the flash memory controller (FPEC) and FLASH_CTLR register will be locked and cannot
```
be accessed. The flash memory controller module can be unlocked by writing the sequence to the
R32_FLASH_KEYR register.
Unlock sequence:
```
1) Write KEY1 = 0x45670123 to the FLASH_KEYR register (must operate KEY1 first);
```
```
2) Write KEY2 = 0xCDEF89AB to the FLASH_KEYR register (must operate KEY2 secondly).
```
The above operations must be performed sequentially and continuously. Otherwise, it is an error operation, which
will lock the FPEC module and FLASH_CTLR register and generate a bus error until the next system reset.
```
The flash memory controller (FPEC) and the R32_FLASH_CTLR register can be locked again by setting the
```
"LOCK" bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register to 1.
46.5.3 Main Memory Standard Program
Standard programming writes 2 bytes per operation. When the PG bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register is set to
```
‘1’, each write of a half-word (2 bytes) to a flash address initiates one programming cycle. Writing any
```
```
non-half-word data causes FPEC to generate a bus error. During programming, the BSY bit is ‘1’; upon
```
completion, BSY becomes ‘0’ and EOP becomes ‘1’.
```
Note: When the BSY bit is ‘1’, write operations to any register are prohibited.
```
Figure 46-1 FLASH program
Read the LOCK bit ofFLASH_CTRL
BSY bit=1？
Perform "Unlock FlashMemory" operation
Set FLASH_CTLR PG bit=1
```
Specified address writehalf word (2 bytes)
```
Read EOP/WRPRTERR to judge theprogramming result Read the programmed
address to check the written data
Continueprogramming?
Over，PG bit=0
LOCK bit=1? YES
NO
NO
YES
YES
NO
```
1) Check the LOCK bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is 1, you need to perform the "Release Flash
```
Memory Lock" operation.
```
2) Set the PEG bit in the FLASH_CTLR register to ‘1’ to enable the standard page erasure mode.
```
```
3) Write the half-word to be programmed to the specified flash memory address (even address).
```
```
4) Wait for the BSY bit to become ‘0’ or for the EOP bit in the R32_FLASH_STATR register to become ‘1’,
```
indicating programming completion. Then clear the EOP bit to ‘0’.
```
5) Check the R32_FLASH_STATR register for errors, or read the programmed address data for verification.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1035
```
6) To continue programming, repeat steps 3-5. To end programming, clear the PG bit.
```

```
```
1) Check the LOCK bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is 1, you need to perform the "Release Flash
```
Memory Lock" operation.
```
2) Set the PEG bit in the FLASH_CTLR register to ‘1’ to enable the sector erasure mode.
```
```
3) Write the page heading address of the page to be erased to the FLASH_ADDR register.
```
```
4) Set the STAT bit in the FLASH_CTLR register to ‘1’ to start an erase action.
```
```
5) When the BYS bit changes to '0' or the EOP bit in the FLASH_STATR register to be '1', it indicates the end of
```
erasure. Clear the EOP bit to 0.
```
6) Read the page of erasure page for verification.
```
```
7) To erase the sector continuously, you can repeat steps 3-5 to end erasing and clear the PEG bit to 0.
```
```
Note: After successful erasure, words read -0xe339e339, half words read -0xe339, even address bytes read -0x39,
```
and odd addresses read 0xe3.
46.5.5 Fast Programming Mode Unlock
Fast programming mode operation can be unlocked by writing a sequence to the R32_FLASH_MODEKEYR
register. After unlocking, the block bit of the R32_FLASH_CTLR register will be cleared to 0, indicating that
quick erasure and programming operations can be performed. Lock again by setting the "FLOCK" bit of the
R32_FLASH_CTLR register to 1.
Unlock sequence:
```
1) Write KEY1=0x45670123 to the FLASH_MODEKEYR register.
```
```
2) Write KEY2=0xCDEF89AB to the FLASH_MODEKEYR register.
```
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1036
The above operations must be performed sequentially and continuously, otherwise the error operation will be
locked and cannot be unlocked until the next system reset.
```
Note: Fast programming requires unlocking the "LOCK" and "FLOCK" layers.
```
46.5.6 Main Memory Fast Programming
```
The fast programming (256 bytes) is made according to the page.
```
```
1) Check the LOCK bit of the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is '1', you need to perform the "unlock flash"
```
operation.
```
2) Check the R32_FLASH_CTLR register FLOCK bit, if it is '1', you need to perform a "quick programming
```
mode unlock" operation.
```
3) Check the BSY bit of the R32_FLASH_STATR register to confirm that there are no other programming
```
operations in progress.
```
4) Set the FTPG bit of the R32_FLASH_CTLR register to '1' to enable fast page programming mode.
```
```
5) Write data to a FLASH address in a 32-bit manner, such as.
```
- (uint32_t*) 0x80000000=0x12345678.
```
6) Wait for WRBSY of R32_FLASH_STATR register to be '1', and write the next data.
```
```
7) Repeat steps 5-6 64 times
```
```
8) Set the FTPG bit in R32_FLASH_CTLR register to' 1' to start fast page programming.
```
```
9) Waiting for the BSY bit to change to '0' or the EOP bit of the FLASH_STATR register to '1' means that a quick
```
page programming is completed and the EOP bit is cleared to 0.
```
10) Query the R32_FLASH_STATR register to see if there are any errors, or read the programming address data
```
check.
```
11) Continue fast page programming to repeat steps 5-10 and end the programming to clear the FTPG bit 0.
```
46.5.7 Main Memory Fast Erasure
Fast erase erases in blocks.
```
1) Check the R32_FLASH_CTLR register LOCK bit, if it is '1', you need to perform the "unlock flash memory"
```
operation.
```
2) Check the R32_FLASH_CTLR register FLOCK bit, if it is '1', you need to perform a "fast programming mode
```
unlock" operation.
```
3) Check the BSY bit of the R32_FLASH_STATR register to confirm that there are no other programming
```
operations in progress.
```
4) Set the FTER bit of the R32_FLASH_CTLR register to '1', and turn on the fast page erasure mode function.
```
```
5) Write the first address of the quick erase page to the R32_FLASH_ADDR register.
```
```
6) Set the STAT bit of the R32_FLASH_CTLR register to '1' to start a quick page erase (256byte) action.
```
```
7) Wait for the BSY bit to change to'0' or the EOP bit of the R32_FLASH_STATR register to '1' means the erasure
```
is over, and the EOP bit is cleared to 0.
```
8) Query the R32_FLASH_STATR register to see if there are any errors, or read the erase page address data
```
check.
```
9) Continue to quickly erase the page and repeat steps 5-8 to end the erase to clear the FTER bit 0.
```
```
Note: After successful erasure, the byte reads -0xe339e339, the half-byte reads -0xe339, the even-address byte
```
reads -0x39, and the odd-address byte reads 0xe3.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1037

```

46.6.1 User Option Bytes Unlock
The user option bytes operation can be unlocked by writing the sequence to the R32_FLASH_OBKEYR register.
After unlocking, the OBWRE bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register will be set to 1, indicating that user option
bytes can be erased and programmed. By setting the OBWRE bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register, it will be
cleared to 0 by software to lock again.
Unlocking sequence
```
1) Write KEY1 = 0x45670123 to the R32_FLASH_OBKEYR register;
```
```
2) Write KEY2 = 0xCDEF89AB to the R32_FLASH_OBKEYR register.
```
```
Note: The user needs to unlock the 2 layers: "LOCK" and "OBWRE" for word selection.
```
46.6.2 User Option Bytes Programming
```
Only standard programming mode is supported, and half word (2 bytes) is written at a time. In the actual process,
```
when programming the user-selected word, FPEC only uses the low byte in the half word, and automatically
```
calculates the high byte (the high byte is the anti-code of the low byte), and then starts the programming operation,
```
which will ensure that the byte in the user-selected word and its anti-code are always correct.
```
1) Check the LOCK bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is set to 1, perform the “Unlock Flash” operation.
```
```
2) Check the BSY bit in the R32_FLASH_STATR register to confirm no other programming operations are in
```
progress.
```
3) Check the OBWRE bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is 0, perform the “User Option Byte Unlock”
```
operation.
```
4) Set the OBPG bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register to ‘1’.
```
```
5) Write the half-word (2 bytes) to be programmed to the specified address.
```
```
6) Wait for the BSY bit to become ‘0’ or for the EOP bit in the R32_FLASH_STATR register to become ‘1’,
```
indicating programming completion. Then clear the EOP bit.
```
7) Read the programming address data for verification.
```
```
8) To continue programming, repeat steps 5-7. To end programming, clear the OBPG bit.
```
```
Note: when "read protected" in the modified selection word is changed to "unprotected" state, an entire erase
```
main storage area operation is automatically performed. If you modify a selection other than read Protection, the
whole erase operation will not occur.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1039
46.6.3 User Option Bytes Erasure
Erase the entire 128-byte user option bytes area directly.
```
1) Check the LOCK bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is set to 1, perform the “Unlock Flash” operation.
```
```
2) Check the BSY bit in the R32_FLASH_STATR register to confirm no programming operation is in progress.
```
```
3) Check the OBWRE bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register. If it is 0, perform the “User Option Byte Unlock”
```
operation.
```
4) Set the OBER bit in the R32_FLASH_CTLR register to ‘1’. Subsequently, set the STRT bit in the
```
R32_FLASH_CTLR register to ‘1’ to initiate user-selected word erase.
```
5) Wait for the BSY bit to become ‘0’ or for the EOP bit in the R32_FLASH_STATR register to become ‘1’
```
indicating erase completion, then clear the EOP bit to 0.
```
6) Read the erased address data for verification.
```
```
7) Clear the OBER bit to 0 to conclude the operation.
```
```
Note: After successful erasure, the character reads -0xe339e339, the half-character reads -0xe339, and the byte
```
reads -0x39.
46.6.4 Read Protection Release
Whether the flash memory is read-protected or not is determined by the user option byte. Read the
R32_FLASH_OBR register. When the RDPRT bit is'1', it indicates that the current flash memory is in
read-protected state, and the flash operation is protected by a series of read-protected states. The process of
unprotecting read is as follows:
```
1) Erase the entire user option byte area, read the protection field RDPR, and the read protection is still valid.
```
```
2) The user chooses words to program and writes the correct RDPR code 0xA5 to remove the read protection of
```
```
the flash memory. (This step will first cause the system to automatically erase the entire piece of flash memory.).
```
```
3) A power-on reset is performed to reload the selected bytes (including the new RDPR code), and the read
```
protection is removed.
46.6.5 Write Protection Release
Whether flash memory is write-protected is determined by the user-selectable bits. Reading the
R32_FLASH_WPR register reveals that each bit represents a sector of flash memory space. A bit value of ‘1’
indicates an unprotected state, while ‘0’ indicates write protection. The process to remove write protection is as
```
follows:
```
```
1) Erase the entire user option byte area.
```
```
2) Write the correct RDPR code 0xA5 to allow read access.
```
```
3) Perform a system reset, reload the selected bytes (including the new WRPR [3:0] bytes), and write protection is
```
removed.
CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
V1.7 1040
```
Chapter 47 Universal High-speed Interface (UHSIF)
```
The module description in this chapter only applies to CH32H417 microcontroller products.
```
The chip incorporates a universal high-speed interface (UHSIF) capable of operating at a maximum transmission
```
clock frequency of 125MHz. It supports 8-bit, 16-bit, or 32-bit data widths, with a theoretical maximum data
transfer rate of 500Mbytes/s.
For specific applications, please refer to and utilize the provided subroutine library.
